得人以溥斯道之傳，君子澤世之心慰矣。蓋君子者，有世道之責者也。斯道之傳而盡得其人焉，則澤之所及也遠矣，其樂寧容已乎？昔孟子立言之意，以爲體萬物而不遺者，君子之道；曠百世而相感者，君子之心。故君子既樂得其道矣，而豈如是止耶？蓋道者，天下之公；英才者，傳道之器也。如其道既我得矣，風聲所感，而天下之廣，凡負明睿之資者，罔不相率以宗予。教自
translation_en:
…Nevertheless, once these words had been uttered, Zisi and Mencius transmitted them in subsequent generations, and the Confucian scholars of the Song continued their work, so that our Way did not fall into oblivion. Thus, although the Master’s teaching was not put into practice in Lu, it was indeed put into practice throughout the world and in later ages! May those who study in subsequent generations know what they should seek!
“To obtain the outstanding talents of the world and educate them: this is the third delight.”
Zhong Jiarui
Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: 〔Elegant and vigorous without being superficial; measured and expansive [?] without being sluggish.〕
Associate Examiner Lin, School Director, comments: 〔It has reasoned substance and depth of implication; therefore it is selected.〕 Surely he is an outstanding talent of Zhongzhou!
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔On reading it, one finds it full and ample [?]; it merits selection.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔Even and fluent.〕
By obtaining suitable people to spread the transmission of this Way, the gentleman finds satisfaction in his desire to benefit the world. For the gentleman bears responsibility for the moral order of the world. If, in transmitting this Way, he obtains all the right people, then its benefits will reach far indeed. How could his delight be restrained? The intent of Mencius’s words was this: what embraces the myriad things without omission is the gentleman’s Way; what evokes a response across a hundred generations is the gentleman’s heart. Thus, once the gentleman delights in having attained the Way, how could he stop there? For the Way is the common possession of all under Heaven, and outstanding talents are the vessels through which it is transmitted. If I have already attained the Way, then, moved by the influence of my reputation, all throughout the vast world who possess the gifts of intelligence and discernment will lead one another to take me as their master. Teaching proceeds from…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
我立矣意氣所招而一世之人凡爲俊髦之流
者莫不翕然而就正不愧不怍之學不專有於
已也必推而與之同成德達材蓋有舉天下而
喻於道焉者矣於天於人之樂不獨善其身也
必推而與之共荅問時雨蓋有盡一世而囿於
敎焉者矣夫如是豈非君子之三樂乎何者蓋
君子之心固欲與人同歸於善者也而勢之在
人者常患其難於必得固欲使人各得其道者
也而機之不由已者常苦於有所未遂今也英
===
才盡得於天下則心法傳授之懿付托得人善
之有諸已者將覃被於天下矣不可必得者而
幸得之斯文之慶殆與天性眞樂者無異焉甄
陶旣合乎一世則道統相承之緒賴以不墜道
之得於已者將流衍於後世矣不可必遂者而
今遂之名敎之樂殆與天倫至樂者不殊焉是
則君子之三樂而性分之在已者至此始全則
夫王天下者固宜有所不與存矣抑斯樂也惟
吾夫子足以當之觀其與顏曾由夏之徒相與
punctuated: 我立矣，意氣所招，而一世之人凡爲俊髦之流者，莫不翕然而就正。不愧不怍之學，不專有於已也，必推而與之同，成德達材，蓋有舉天下而喻於道焉者矣。於天於人之樂，不獨善其身也，必推而與之共，荅問時雨，蓋有盡一世而囿於敎焉者矣。夫如是，豈非君子之三樂乎？何者？蓋君子之心，固欲與人同歸於善者也，而勢之在人者，常患其難於必得；固欲使人各得其道者也，而機之不由已者，常苦於有所未遂。今也英才盡得於天下，則心法傳授之懿，付托得人，善之有諸已者，將覃被於天下矣。不可必得者而幸得之，斯文之慶，殆與天性眞樂者無異焉。甄陶旣合乎一世，則道統相承之緒，賴以不墜，道之得於已者，將流衍於後世矣。不可必遂者而今遂之，名敎之樂，殆與天倫至樂者不殊焉。是則君子之三樂，而性分之在已者，至此始全，則夫王天下者，固宜有所不與存矣。抑斯樂也，惟吾夫子足以當之。觀其與顏、曾、由、夏之徒相與
translation_en:
… established by me, and, drawn by my spirit and purpose, all the outstanding men of the age come together to seek correction. The learning that leaves one without shame or embarrassment is not kept for oneself alone: one must extend it to others and share it with them, bringing their virtue to completion and developing their talents. Thus the whole world may be brought to understand the Way. The joy of being without shame before Heaven or others does not consist merely in perfecting oneself: one must extend it to others and share it with them, answering their questions and nurturing them like timely rain. Thus an entire generation may be embraced within one's teaching. Is this not, then, the gentleman's third joy?

Why is this so? The gentleman's heart certainly desires to return to goodness together with others; yet, because circumstances depend on other people, he constantly worries that this cannot be assured. He certainly desires that everyone should attain the Way; yet, because the opportunities are beyond his control, he constantly suffers from leaving something unfulfilled. Now, when outstanding talents throughout the world have all been gathered, the precious teaching of the mind has found worthy recipients to whom it can be entrusted, and the goodness possessed within oneself will spread throughout the world. What could not be assured has fortunately been attained. This blessing for our cultural tradition is scarcely different from the true joy rooted in our Heaven-endowed nature. Once one's work of molding and nurturing has reached an entire generation, the succession through which the Way is transmitted will thereby be kept from lapsing, and the Way attained within oneself will flow onward to later generations. What could not be certain of fulfillment has now been fulfilled. This joy in the moral teaching is scarcely different from the supreme joy of family relationships. These, then, are the gentleman's three joys; only at this point is the fulfillment of one's own endowed nature complete. It is therefore fitting that ruling the world should not be counted among them.

Yet only our Master could fully embody this joy. Consider how he associated with disciples such as Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zhong You, and Zixia …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
周旋問荅而侍側之樂油然自不容已故其言
曰有朋自遠方來不亦樂乎蓋皆爲斯道得人
幸也孟子得統於孔子者也豈不欲傳其道於
天下後世乎奈之何萬章公孫丑諸人舉不足
以任斯道之寄則孟子之惓惓有望於一世之
英者其能以自已乎噫君子三樂之教其重有
所感也夫
易
動靜不失其時其道光明
中嘉瑞
===
同考試官教諭崔　批　當其可之謂時雖動亦止
場中作者率多未瑩達是古者僅見此篇可以式矣
同考試官學正林　批　易奇而法所□義者類皆粗
淺此篇詞理精潔是邃於易教者
考試官教諭鄭　批　體認切當可錄
考試官教諭曲　批　學易而有得艮之義者
動靜各協於一止之道斯顯矣夫道一而已動
靜而能協焉止之道不其顯矣乎夫子之意蓋
punctuated:
周旋問荅，而侍側之樂油然自不容已。故其言曰：「有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？」蓋皆爲斯道得人幸也。孟子得統於孔子者也，豈不欲傳其道於天下後世乎？奈之何萬章、公孫丑諸人，舉不足以任斯道之寄，則孟子之惓惓有望於一世之英者，其能以自已乎？噫！君子三樂之教，其重有所感也夫！
易
動靜不失其時，其道光明。
中嘉瑞
同考試官教諭崔批：當其可之謂時，雖動亦止。場中作者率多未瑩達，是古者僅見此篇，可以式矣。
同考試官學正林批：易奇而法，所□義者類皆粗淺。此篇詞理精潔，是邃於易教者。
考試官教諭鄭批：體認切當，可錄。
考試官教諭曲批：學易而有得艮之義者。
動靜各協於一，止之道斯顯矣。夫道一而已，動靜而能協焉，止之道不其顯矣乎？夫子之意蓋
translation_en:
…in their exchanges and questions and answers, the joy of attending at his side welled up irresistibly. Thus he said: “When friends come from afar, is it not a joy?” All this was surely rejoicing that this Way had found people to carry it on. Mencius inherited the succession of the Way from Confucius: how could he not wish to transmit his Way throughout the world and to later generations? Yet Wan Zhang, Gongsun Chou, and the others were all inadequate to bear the responsibility of this Way. Could Mencius then restrain his earnest hopes for the outstanding men of his age? Ah! The teaching concerning the gentleman’s three joys must have arisen from deeply felt concerns!

Book of Changes
“When movement and stillness do not miss their proper times, the Way shines brightly.”
By Zhong Jiarui.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: To accord with what is appropriate is what is meant by timeliness; even movement is then a form of resting in the proper place. Most writers in the examination hall have not understood this clearly. Among those who take antiquity as their standard [?], this is the only essay I have seen that can serve as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The Changes is remarkable yet follows a pattern [?]; most treatments of its meanings in the text here obscured by an illegible character are crude and shallow [?]. This essay is refined and lucid in both expression and reasoning: its author has penetrated deeply into the teaching of the Changes.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its grasp of the meaning is precise and apt; it merits selection.

Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: Here is someone who has studied the Changes and attained an understanding of the meaning of Gen, Keeping Still.

When movement and stillness each accord with the One, the Way of resting in the proper place becomes manifest. The Way is one, and that is all. If movement and stillness can accord with it, does not the Way of resting in the proper place become manifest? The Master’s meaning was presumably…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰理之不可易者止也行之不可違者時也時
固未始有定用而理實未始無定在君子亦惟
協諸理而已是故卦以艮名有止之義焉而時
有動靜焉則各有止之道也故夫時止則止之
時行則行之是蓋感物而動將有猷有爲焉斯
時也豈固爲是憧憧者耶感於動也吾不可以
有止也出謀發慮允爲順應之常揆事宰物不
拂大中之矩蓋有見於理而無見於人行亦止
矣動之時不隨之而變易也哉至若寂然不動
===
而何思何慮焉斯時也豈固爲是含章者耶定
於靜也吾不可以有行也一貞自如而渾無偏
倚之雜洗心藏密而確有靜正之守蓋有見於
理而無見於已止亦止矣靜之時不與之而偕
行也哉夫動靜各止而皆不失乎時焉道不其
光明矣乎蓋動焉而有物欲之擾不免爲邪暗
之塞靜焉而有意必之私其何爲昭明之融今
則其動也直其靜也虛純一不雜而自有篤實
不揜之著其靜亦定其動亦定内外俱泯而自
punctuated: 曰：理之不可易者，止也；行之不可違者，時也。時固未始有定用，而理實未始無定在，君子亦惟協諸理而已。是故卦以艮名，有止之義焉，而時有動靜焉，則各有止之道也。故夫時止則止之，時行則行之。是蓋感物而動，將有猷有爲焉，斯時也，豈固爲是憧憧者耶？感於動也，吾不可以有止也。出謀發慮，允爲順應之常；揆事宰物，不拂大中之矩。蓋有見於理而無見於人，行亦止矣，動之時不隨之而變易也哉？至若寂然不動，而何思何慮焉，斯時也，豈固爲是含章者耶？定於靜也，吾不可以有行也。一貞自如，而渾無偏倚之雜；洗心藏密，而確有靜正之守。蓋有見於理而無見於已，止亦止矣，靜之時不與之而偕行也哉？夫動靜各止，而皆不失乎時焉，道不其光明矣乎？蓋動焉而有物欲之擾，不免爲邪暗之塞；靜焉而有意必之私，其何爲昭明之融？今則其動也直，其靜也虛，純一不雜，而自有篤實不揜之著；其靜亦定，其動亦定，内外俱泯，而自
translation_en: …says: What cannot be altered in principle is abiding; what cannot be disregarded in conduct is the appropriate time. The time has never had a fixed application, yet principle has never lacked a fixed abiding place. The gentleman need only accord with principle. Thus the hexagram is named Gen, Keeping Still, and conveys the meaning of abiding. Yet circumstances call for both movement and stillness, and each has its own way of abiding. Therefore, when it is time to stop, one stops; when it is time to act, one acts. When one is stirred by things and is about to make plans and undertake actions, is one necessarily beset by restless thoughts? Once stirred to movement, I cannot remain still. In devising plans and giving thought to matters, one truly follows the constant norm of responding appropriately; in assessing affairs and directing things, one does not contravene the rule of perfect centrality. Seeing only principle and not human considerations, one abides even while acting. When the time calls for movement, does one not change accordingly? As for remaining tranquil and unmoving, with neither thought nor deliberation, is one necessarily concealing one's excellence at such a time? Settled in stillness, I cannot act. Unwavering rectitude remains spontaneous, wholly free of any admixture of partiality or bias; cleansing the mind and retiring into secrecy, one firmly maintains stillness and correctness. Seeing only principle and not oneself [?], one abides also in stopping. When the time calls for stillness, does one not proceed in step with it? When movement and stillness each find their proper abiding place, and neither misses its appropriate time, does not the Way become radiant? For if, in movement, one is disturbed by material desires, one inevitably suffers obstruction by perversity and darkness. If, in stillness, one harbors the selfishness of preconceptions and insistence, how can there be luminous, unobstructed clarity? Now, however, one's movement is upright and one's stillness empty: pure, single-minded, and unmixed, one naturally manifests a solidity and genuineness that cannot be concealed. One is settled in stillness and settled also in movement; distinctions between inner and outer alike dissolve, and naturally…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
有誠精而明之妙成心忘而眞性湛執極而不
變者燦乎明通而丕顯矣泰宇定而天光發推
行以爲通者煥乎緝熙而懋昭矣其光明也爲
何如哉由是觀之道之所貴者止也而止之所
貴者時也艮之義大矣伏羲名卦豈徒也哉嘗
觀止之爲道雖妙於一動一靜之間而所以止
之者非無爲也無心也非無心也無私心也私
則雖槁灰一念亦動也無私心則雖酬酢萬變
亦靜也是故聖人立極而唯主於靜者非無動
===
也雖動亦靜者也若專事於靜而淪於寂者亦
豈可以言止乎要之無欲而靜無爲而爲斯可
矣
子曰易其至矣乎夫易聖人所以崇德而
廣業也知崇禮卑崇效天卑法地天地
設位而易行乎其中矣成性存存道義
之門
溫如春
同考試官教諭崔　批〔題本正大而體認精切者〕
punctuated:
有誠精而明之妙。成心忘而眞性湛，執極而不變者，燦乎明通而丕顯矣；泰宇定而天光發，推行以爲通者，煥乎緝熙而懋昭矣。其光明也爲何如哉！由是觀之，道之所貴者止也，而止之所貴者時也。艮之義大矣，伏羲名卦豈徒也哉！嘗觀止之爲道，雖妙於一動一靜之間，而所以止之者，非無爲也，無心也；非無心也，無私心也。私則雖槁灰，一念亦動也；無私心則雖酬酢萬變，亦靜也。是故聖人立極而唯主於靜者，非無動也，雖動亦靜者也。若專事於靜而淪於寂者，亦豈可以言止乎？要之，無欲而靜，無爲而爲，斯可矣。

子曰：「易其至矣乎！夫易，聖人所以崇德而廣業也。知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道義之門。」

溫如春

同考試官教諭崔　批〔題本正大，而體認精切者〕
translation_en:
…there is the subtle efficacy of sincerity becoming refined and luminous. When fixed preconceptions are forgotten and the true nature is clear and still, holding fast to the ultimate standard without changing shines forth in lucid understanding and becomes greatly manifest. When the inner dwelling is settled and Heaven’s light issues forth, extending this into practice to achieve free operation shines with sustained brilliance and becomes abundantly radiant. How great is its luminosity! Viewed in this light, what is prized in the Way is stopping, and what is prized in stopping is timeliness. Great indeed is the meaning of Gen, Keeping Still! Surely Fuxi did not name the hexagram without purpose!

I have considered that, although the Way of stopping finds its subtlety in the alternation of activity and stillness, that by which one stops is not inactivity, but freedom from deliberate intent. This does not mean having no mind; it means having no selfish mind. With selfishness, even if one is like withered wood and dead ashes, a single thought is still activity. Without a selfish mind, even responding to ten thousand changes is stillness. Thus, when the sage establishes the ultimate standard and takes stillness alone as primary, this does not mean that he has no activity: even in activity he is still. If one devotes oneself exclusively to stillness and sinks into quiescence, how could this be called stopping? In essence, to be still through freedom from desire, and to act without contrived action—this will suffice.

The Master said: “Has not the Book of Changes reached the utmost? The Book of Changes is that by which the sages exalt their virtue and broaden their undertakings. Knowledge is lofty; ritual is lowly. Loftiness emulates Heaven; lowliness models itself on Earth. Heaven and Earth take their positions, and change operates between them. Maintaining the fully realized nature continually is the gateway to the Way and righteousness.”

Wen Ruchun 溫如春

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui 崔, Instructor: 〔The topic itself is upright and grand, but those whose understanding of it is refined and exact…〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
殊少是篇詞不煩而發揮明盡必有得之士也允宜高薦
同考試官學正林　批〔簡約而理自足佳作也〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔潔淨可錄〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔明潔〕
大傳贊易道之至即聖人之全體至極者焉蓋
聖人德業配天地可謂全體至極者矣而皆不
外乎易焉易之道何其至哉昔孔子深見易道
之無窮而聖人莫能違也乃言曰易之爲書也
蓋不徒卦爻之布列象數之顯設而已而包涵
盡天下之理精蘊達造化之微其斯至矣乎何
===
以言之彼凡言盛德者孰不曰聖人言大業者
亦孰不曰聖人而不知聖人德之所以崇業之
所以廣者而皆資之易焉是故惟易理之散殊
而不可象也聖人窮之有精義入神之妙心與
易而流通矣知不亦崇乎惟易理之體事而無
不在也聖人循之有從容中道之美身與易而
合一矣禮不亦卑乎然高明莫如天而知之崇
也效之蓋與丕冒不遺者而同神卑順莫如地
punctuated:
殊少。是篇詞不煩而發揮明盡，必有得之士也，允宜高薦。
同考試官學正林，批〔簡約而理自足，佳作也。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔潔淨可錄。〕
考試官教諭曲，批〔明潔。〕
大傳贊易道之至，即聖人之全體至極者焉。蓋聖人德業配天地，可謂全體至極者矣，而皆不外乎易焉。易之道何其至哉！昔孔子深見易道之無窮，而聖人莫能違也，乃言曰：易之爲書也，蓋不徒卦爻之布列、象數之顯設而已，而包涵盡天下之理，精蘊達造化之微，其斯至矣乎？何以言之？彼凡言盛德者，孰不曰聖人？言大業者，亦孰不曰聖人？而不知聖人德之所以崇、業之所以廣者，而皆資之易焉。是故惟易理之散殊而不可象也，聖人窮之，有精義入神之妙，心與易而流通矣，知不亦崇乎？惟易理之體事而無不在也，聖人循之，有從容中道之美，身與易而合一矣，禮不亦卑乎？然高明莫如天，而知之崇也效之，蓋與丕冒不遺者而同神；卑順莫如地，
translation_en:
…are exceedingly few. This essay is free of verbosity, yet expounds its meaning clearly and fully. Its author must be a scholar who has attained genuine understanding and assuredly deserves recommendation at a high rank.
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Concise, yet fully sufficient in its reasoning: an excellent composition.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and clean in expression; worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and clean in expression.〕
The Great Commentary praises the ultimate perfection of the Way of the Changes by reference to the sage’s complete embodiment of it at its highest perfection. For the sage’s virtue and achievements match Heaven and Earth and may indeed be called complete and supremely perfect; yet none of this lies outside the Changes. How perfect is the Way of the Changes! In former times, Kongzi profoundly perceived that the Way of the Changes was inexhaustible and that even sages could not depart from it. He therefore said: As a book, the Changes does not merely array hexagrams and their lines and set forth images and numbers. It comprehensively embraces all the principles under Heaven, and its profound subtleties penetrate the mysteries of creation and transformation. Is this not ultimate perfection?
How can this be explained? Whenever people speak of abundant virtue, who does not speak of the sage? Whenever they speak of great achievements, who does not likewise speak of the sage? Yet they do not understand that the sage draws entirely upon the Changes to exalt his virtue and broaden his achievements. Thus, because the principles of the Changes are manifold and cannot be represented in images, the sage investigates them to the utmost, attaining the marvel of refining his understanding of rightness until he penetrates the numinous. His mind thus moves in communion with the Changes. Is his understanding not exalted? Because the principles of the Changes give substance to affairs and are everywhere present, the sage follows them, attaining the excellence of effortlessly keeping to the Way of the Mean. His person thus becomes one with the Changes. Is his ritual propriety not lowly?
Now nothing equals Heaven in loftiness and brilliance, and his exalted understanding takes it as its exemplar, sharing the numinous efficacy of that which broadly encompasses all without omission. Nothing equals Earth in lowliness and compliance…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
而禮之卑也法之蓋與順承時行者而同體夫
知崇禮卑則德崇而業廣矣妙用不自此出乎
蓋自造化觀之天位乎上地位乎下而兩儀奠
矣則陰陽之往來生成之變化而大化行焉殆
猶聖人知禮效法乎天地而成性存存於不已
由是全體立而妙用出大本固而達道行凡散
殊而爲道者莫不自吾心以發越蓋足以周萬
用之資矣曷有窮乎凡裁制而爲義者莫不自
此心以呈露蓋足以達萬變之妙矣寧有旣乎
===
是知天下之理盡於易而聖人全體妙乎易易
道之至曷以加哉抑易書之作聖人所以前民
用者也而天地鬼神之奥道德性命之微無不
具焉雖以用之卜筮而實盡乎義理者也故孔
子旣以盡性至命歸之聖人用易之事而于此
復以聖人德業言之可謂盡易之道而達易之
神矣世儒考象辭者泥於術數而不得乎弘通
簡易之法論義理者涉於空虛而不適乎仁義
中正之歸而易道微矣噫是又烏足與議於斯
punctuated:
而禮之卑也法之，蓋與順承時行者而同體。夫知崇禮卑，則德崇而業廣矣，妙用不自此出乎？蓋自造化觀之，天位乎上，地位乎下，而兩儀奠矣；則陰陽之往來，生成之變化，而大化行焉。殆猶聖人知禮效法乎天地，而成性存存於不已。由是全體立而妙用出，大本固而達道行。凡散殊而爲道者，莫不自吾心以發越，蓋足以周萬用之資矣，曷有窮乎？凡裁制而爲義者，莫不自此心以呈露，蓋足以達萬變之妙矣，寧有旣乎？

是知天下之理盡於易，而聖人全體妙乎易，易道之至，曷以加哉？抑易書之作，聖人所以前民用者也，而天地鬼神之奥，道德性命之微，無不具焉。雖以用之卜筮，而實盡乎義理者也。故孔子旣以盡性至命歸之聖人用易之事，而于此復以聖人德業言之，可謂盡易之道而達易之神矣。世儒考象辭者，泥於術數而不得乎弘通簡易之法；論義理者，涉於空虛而不適乎仁義中正之歸，而易道微矣。噫！是又烏足與議於斯
translation_en:
…and ritual propriety, in its lowliness, takes Earth as its model, sharing the very substance of that which compliantly receives Heaven’s influence and acts in accord with the seasons. When knowledge is lofty and ritual propriety lowly, virtue becomes exalted and achievement extensive. Does not wondrous functioning emerge from this? Viewed in terms of creation and transformation, Heaven occupies the position above and Earth the position below, and the Two Modes are thereby established. Through the coming and going of yin and yang and the transformations of generation and completion, the great process of transformation proceeds. This is much like the sage’s knowledge and ritual propriety taking Heaven and Earth as their models, while his perfected nature is preserved without cease. Thus the complete substance is established and wondrous functioning emerges; the great foundation is secured and the universally operative Way proceeds. All that constitutes the Way in its diverse manifestations issues forth from my own heart, fully supplying the resources for its myriad applications. How could these ever be exhausted? All that constitutes rightness through discrimination and regulation manifests itself from this heart, fully realizing the wondrous workings of myriad changes. How could these ever come to an end?

From this we know that the principles of all under Heaven are comprehensively contained in the Changes, and that the sage, in his whole being, wondrously accords with the Changes. What could surpass the utmost perfection of the Way of the Changes? Moreover, the sages composed the book of Changes to guide the people in its use. It contains without exception the mysteries of Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, and the subtleties of the Way and virtue, human nature and destiny. Although employed for divination by tortoise shell and milfoil stalks, it in fact comprehensively embraces moral principles. Thus Confucius had already attributed fully realizing human nature and reaching destiny to the sage’s use of the Changes; here he speaks of it again in terms of the sage’s virtue and achievements. He may truly be said to have fully expounded the Way of the Changes and penetrated its spiritual efficacy. Among the scholars of this age, those who investigate its images and statements become mired in techniques and numerical calculations, failing to grasp its method of comprehensive understanding, simplicity, and ease. Those who discuss its moral principles stray into emptiness and fail to arrive at its ultimate purport of humaneness, rightness, centrality, and correctness. Thus the Way of the Changes has fallen into obscurity. Alas! How could such men be worthy of joining in a discussion of this…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
也歟
書
翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂在官百僚師師
百工惟時撫于五辰庶績其凝
孫榮仁
同考試官教諭楊　批〔皐陶欲帝舜盡用天下賢才此有虞之治所以稱盛是作獨能發揮其義〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔用典謨自相發明讀之想見有虞都俞氣象〕
===
考試官教諭曲　批〔說賢才竝用及相觀法自效處俱明暢有體〕
用賢才而成治功大臣陳謨於聖君也蓋任賢
圖治君道之急務也君以任人爲務而臣以盡
職爲賢天下之治豈有不舉者哉有虞皐陶以
知人之謨陳於帝舜至此若謂人君宰制天下
必在於任用賢才以御一世者何哉蓋未有不
勤於求賢而能逸於得人以致治者也是故廣
進賢之路四門雖嘗闢矣其能無或遺者乎或
punctuated:
也歟？

書

翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師。百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績其凝。

孫榮仁

同考試官教諭楊　批〔皐陶欲帝舜盡用天下賢才，此有虞之治所以稱盛，是作獨能發揮其義。〕

考試官教諭鄭　批〔用典謨自相發明，讀之想見有虞都俞氣象。〕

考試官教諭曲　批〔說賢才竝用及相觀法自效處，俱明暢有體。〕

用賢才而成治功，大臣陳謨於聖君也。蓋任賢圖治，君道之急務也。君以任人爲務，而臣以盡職爲賢，天下之治豈有不舉者哉？有虞皐陶以知人之謨陳於帝舜，至此若謂：人君宰制天下，必在於任用賢才以御一世者，何哉？蓋未有不勤於求賢而能逸於得人以致治者也。是故廣進賢之路，四門雖嘗闢矣，其能無或遺者乎？或
translation_en:
…could they?

Book of Documents

“Receive them all and distribute their employment: let those possessing the nine virtues all serve, and let men of outstanding ability hold office, with the hundred officials taking one another as models. Let all officers attend to their duties at the proper times, following the five seasonal periods, so that all achievements may be firmly established.”

Sun Rongren

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔Gao Yao wished Emperor Shun to employ all the worthy and talented men of the realm. This is why the government of Youyu was acclaimed as flourishing. This composition is distinctive in its ability to bring out that meaning.〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔It uses the “Canons” and “Counsels” to illuminate one another. Reading it, one can imagine the atmosphere of consultation and assent at the court of Youyu.〕

Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: 〔Its explanations of employing worthy and talented men together, and of their observing and emulating one another as they render service, are clear, fluent, and properly structured.〕

Employing worthy and talented men to achieve good government: this is the counsel a great minister presented to a sage ruler. Appointing the worthy and seeking good government are urgent duties in the ruler’s way. If the ruler makes appointing men his task, and ministers count the fulfillment of their duties as their worthiness, how could the government of the realm fail to be well conducted? Gao Yao of Youyu presented to Emperor Shun his counsel on discerning men. At this point, he seems to say: Why must a ruler, in governing all under Heaven, rely on employing worthy and talented men to direct his age? Because no one has ever achieved good government through the ease that comes from obtaining the right men without first diligently seeking the worthy. Thus, to broaden the avenues by which worthy men enter service, although the four gates have already been opened, could there be none still overlooked? Whether …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
有德或有才必合而受之茅茹兼收明明之在
朝也揆庶官之政九官雖嘗命矣其能無不備
者乎或以賢或以能必布而用之圭璋竝列穆
穆之在位也夫如是則大賢小賢莫不以德稱
位踪附先後九德與共天事非特三德六德之
見用也多才多藝莫不以能稱職綱紀經營俊
乂皆在官使非特有家有邦之得人也將見賢
俊滿朝而羣后德讓大臣以法小臣以廉也負
乗而非度者何有焉謨猷濟美而百職奮庸五
===
行不忒四時無易也後時而弗諧者何有焉由
是天功時亮六府爲之孔脩禮樂其宣和矣政
刑其平措矣國家不自爾而雍熙也乎帝載惟
熙九功爲之各敘教化其誕敷矣民物其咸遂
矣天下不於是而康寧也乎噫大臣以是忠告
於君而聖神功化之極要不出此忠愛又孰有
大焉者哉盡用天下之才以成一世之治此虞
帝之所以不可及也舜以不得禹臯陶爲已憂
信夫抑君道固必急於親賢而大臣猶必勞於
punctuated: 有德或有才，必合而受之，茅茹兼收，明明之在朝也。揆庶官之政，九官雖嘗命矣，其能無不備者乎？或以賢，或以能，必布而用之，圭璋竝列，穆穆之在位也。夫如是，則大賢小賢莫不以德稱位，踪附先後，九德與共天事，非特三德六德之見用也。多才多藝莫不以能稱職，綱紀經營，俊乂皆在官使，非特有家有邦之得人也。將見賢俊滿朝，而羣后德讓，大臣以法，小臣以廉也，負乗而非度者何有焉？謨猷濟美，而百職奮庸，五行不忒，四時無易也，後時而弗諧者何有焉？由是天功時亮，六府爲之孔脩，禮樂其宣和矣，政刑其平措矣，國家不自爾而雍熙也乎？帝載惟熙，九功爲之各敘，教化其誕敷矣，民物其咸遂矣，天下不於是而康寧也乎？噫！大臣以是忠告於君，而聖神功化之極要不出此，忠愛又孰有大焉者哉？盡用天下之才，以成一世之治，此虞帝之所以不可及也。舜以不得禹臯陶爲已憂，信夫！抑君道固必急於親賢，而大臣猶必勞於
translation_en:
…whether they possess virtue or talent, all must be received together, gathered like intertwined roots of thatch, so that men of shining virtue stand at court. In overseeing the administration of the various offices, although the nine officials have already been appointed, can there be no deficiencies? Whether distinguished by worthiness or ability, they must all be assigned posts and employed, arrayed together like gui and zhang jade tablets, standing with solemn dignity in office. In this way, worthies great and small will all possess virtue commensurate with their positions. Following one another, those possessing the nine virtues will share in Heaven’s work; employment will not be confined to those possessing three or six virtues. Men of many talents and accomplishments will all possess abilities commensurate with their duties. Ordering and managing affairs, outstanding men will all serve in office; it will not merely be the holders of great households and states who secure suitable men.

Then we shall see worthies and men of outstanding talent filling the court, and the various lords yielding to one another in virtue: great ministers will uphold proper standards, and lesser ministers will maintain integrity. How could there be men who, fit only to carry burdens, improperly ride in carriages? Plans and counsels will complement one another’s excellence, and the hundred offices will exert themselves to achieve results. The five agents will not deviate, and the four seasons will not depart from their proper order. How could there be delays and failures of coordination?

Thus Heaven’s work will receive timely assistance, and the six resources will be thoroughly ordered. Rites and music will spread harmony, and government and punishments will be administered equitably. Will not the state thereby attain concord and prosperity? The sovereign’s undertakings will flourish, and the nine achievements will each attain their proper order. Moral instruction will spread widely, and the people and all living things will flourish. Will not all under Heaven thereby enjoy peace and tranquillity?

Ah! A great minister offers this loyal counsel to his ruler, and the essential means by which a sage of wondrous wisdom achieves transformative rule go no further than this. What greater loyalty and love could there be? Fully employing the talents of all under Heaven to bring about good government for an entire age: this is what made the sovereign of Yu unequalled. Shun regarded failing to obtain Yu and Gao Yao as his own cause for concern—how true this is! Yet, while the ruler’s way certainly requires urgency in drawing close to the worthy, great ministers must still labor at…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
吐握聖君賢臣之遇皆不偶也故伊尹勤於鼎
俎傅說伏於版築太公鼓刀奚之自鬻值此患
也若謂世既有賢智之君亦必有賢明之臣進
退關其忠任職行其術此猶未盡之論何足以
與此
皇建其有極斂時五福
李希孔
同考試官教諭楊　批〔皇建之極即天命極至之理天人一氣流通中和位育其諸福百祥皆太和元氣也〕
===
考試官教諭鄭　批〔推明禹第皇極居洛書中篇中類能言之可謂能闡其義者〕
〔數為天地之心是禹由精一之極得執中之要正見衍疇授受心法〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔皇極為九疇樞要建極斂福是天道自然此作得之〕
人君以至德先天下而隆眷命者天道然也蓋
極者天德之至善而福者天心之眷愛也君以
至德先天下而隆眷命於上焉豈非天道之自
punctuated:
吐握。聖君賢臣之遇，皆不偶也。故伊尹勤於鼎俎，傅說伏於版築，太公鼓刀，奚之自鬻，值此患也。若謂世既有賢智之君，亦必有賢明之臣，進退關其忠，任職行其術，此猶未盡之論，何足以與此？
皇建其有極，斂時五福。
李希孔
同考試官教諭楊，批〔皇建之極，即天命極至之理。天人一氣流通，中和位育，其諸福百祥，皆太和元氣也。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔推明禹第皇極居洛書中，篇中類能言之，可謂能闡其義者。〕〔數為天地之心，是禹由精一之極得執中之要，正見衍疇授受心法。〕
考試官教諭曲，批〔皇極為九疇樞要，建極斂福，是天道自然，此作得之。〕
人君以至德先天下而隆眷命者，天道然也。蓋極者，天德之至善，而福者，天心之眷愛也。君以至德先天下而隆眷命於上焉，豈非天道之自
translation_en:
…spitting out his food and grasping his unbound hair [in his haste to receive worthy men]. The encounters of sage rulers and worthy ministers are never mere accidents. Thus Yi Yin labored over cauldrons and sacrificial stands; Fu Yue remained obscure amid work on rammed-earth walls; Taigong wielded a butcher’s knife; and Xi sold himself [?]: they faced this same concern. To say that, when the world has a worthy and wise ruler, it must also have worthy and enlightened ministers, whose loyalty is bound up with their advancing into office or withdrawing, and who put their methods into practice while holding office—this is still an incomplete account. How could it compare with this?
The sovereign establishes the supreme standard and gathers these five blessings.
Li Xikong
Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔The standard established by the sovereign is the ultimate principle ordained by Heaven. Heaven and humanity are pervaded by a single vital force. Through equilibrium and harmony, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nurtured; the many blessings and hundred auspicious signs are all the primal vital force of supreme harmony.〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔The essay elucidates how Yu placed the sovereign’s supreme standard at the center of the Luo River Writing [?]. The discussion in the essay generally succeeds in expressing this and may be said to bring out its meaning.〕〔Number constitutes the heart of Heaven and Earth. Thus Yu, through the utmost refinement and singleness of mind, grasped the essentials of holding fast to the mean. This precisely reveals the teaching of the mind transmitted and received in the elaboration of the categories.〕
Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: 〔The sovereign’s supreme standard is the pivot of the Nine Categories. Establishing the standard and gathering blessings are the natural operation of Heaven’s Way. This composition grasps this.〕

For the supreme standard is the highest goodness of Heaven’s virtue, while blessings are the loving favor of Heaven’s heart.
