title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
然哉昔者箕子衍洪範皇極之疇以告武王若
謂人君受天命以居天下之正位體元資始萬
物之所覩也首羣動而立天下之大中獲端酬
物萬夫之所望也然中正之德純粹之誼豈非
君身所固有哉是故帝有降衷所以寵綏四方
也則帝命是勑爲天地而立心天有顯道所以
陰隲下民也則天敘是惇爲斯民而立極標準
建而民志自此定也經綸正而民行自此同也
躬行盛德凡威儀言辭之繫觀聽以昭法則者
===
皆足以正朝廷而式萬方焉風示儀刑凡綱常
典禮之盡倫制以表中正者皆足以脩人紀而
張四維焉夫如是則皇極建矣吾知脩禮達義
惠迪之吉慶與善而茲臻體信達順福善之祥
效以類而自應道積於躬而哲命其自貽也心
純乎天而天地其弗違也純嘏是錫福祿其永
綏矣保佑之荐至者夫豈有不周矣乎蘩祉是
增降福其孔皆矣休祚之聿懷者夫豈有未全
矣乎夫人君居五位之尊建斯民之極而獲眷
punctuated: 然哉！昔者箕子衍《洪範》皇極之疇以告武王，若謂人君受天命以居天下之正位，體元資始，萬物之所覩也；首羣動而立天下之大中，獲端酬物，萬夫之所望也。然中正之德、純粹之誼，豈非君身所固有哉？是故帝有降衷，所以寵綏四方也，則帝命是勑，爲天地而立心；天有顯道，所以陰隲下民也，則天敘是惇，爲斯民而立極。標準建而民志自此定也，經綸正而民行自此同也。躬行盛德，凡威儀言辭之繫觀聽以昭法則者，皆足以正朝廷而式萬方焉；風示儀刑，凡綱常典禮之盡倫制以表中正者，皆足以脩人紀而張四維焉。夫如是則皇極建矣。吾知脩禮達義，惠迪之吉慶與善而茲臻；體信達順，福善之祥效以類而自應。道積於躬而哲命其自貽也，心純乎天而天地其弗違也。純嘏是錫，福祿其永綏矣，保佑之荐至者，夫豈有不周矣乎？蘩祉是增，降福其孔皆矣，休祚之聿懷者，夫豈有未全矣乎？夫人君居五位之尊，建斯民之極，而獲眷
translation_en:
…the natural working of Heaven’s Way!

Formerly, Jizi elaborated the section on the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard in the Great Plan to instruct King Wu. It was as though he said: The ruler receives Heaven’s mandate and occupies the rightful position in the world. Embodying the primal force from which all things take their beginning, he is the one to whom all beings look. Leading all activity and establishing the great mean for the world, he grasps the beginning [?] and responds to things; he is the one to whom all people turn in expectation. Yet are not the virtue of centrality and correctness, and the principles of purity, inherent in the ruler himself?

Thus, the Supreme Lord has bestowed an inner moral norm, thereby favoring and pacifying the four quarters. The ruler accordingly upholds the Lord’s command, establishing a heart for Heaven and Earth. Heaven has its manifest Way, thereby silently ordering the people below. The ruler accordingly strengthens Heaven’s ordering, establishing an ultimate standard for the people. Once this standard is established, the people’s aspirations become settled; once the ordering of affairs is correct, their conduct becomes unified. He personally practices abundant virtue: every aspect of his dignified bearing and speech that engages people’s eyes and ears and makes the proper rules manifest suffices to rectify the court and provide a model for all regions. He offers an exemplary pattern through his influence: all the cardinal relationships, constant norms, canonical institutions, and rites that fully express human relationships and their regulations, and display centrality and correctness, suffice to cultivate the bonds of human society and uphold its four supports—ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame.

When this is so, the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard is established. I know that, through cultivating ritual propriety and fully realizing righteousness, the good fortune of following the Way arrives together with goodness; through embodying trustworthiness and fully realizing harmony, the auspicious effects of blessings bestowed upon goodness naturally respond to what is of their own kind. The Way accumulates within his person, and he thereby brings a favorable mandate upon himself [?]. His heart accords purely with Heaven, and Heaven and Earth do not act contrary to him. Great blessings are bestowed, and good fortune and emolument will bring lasting peace. How could the protection and assistance that arrive repeatedly fail to extend everywhere? Abundant blessings increase, and the blessings sent down are most comprehensive. How could the gracious good fortune that comes to him be in any way incomplete?

Now the ruler occupies the honored fifth position, establishes the ultimate standard for the people, and receives Heaven’s favor…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
命之隆者如此則天下之所以有賴而各遂者
豈不繫於一人也哉大抵天人福極其理一也
善之所至福亦至焉誠能上下一於恭敬則天
地自位萬物自育四靈畢至又何啻斂福於身
而已箕子衍洪範以著天人之學而皇極者洪
範九疇之樞紐也建極之義寔又神禹仰稽天
地之心而發明授受執中之要周家之所以致
太平爲民極者不亦有由然哉
詩
天保定爾以莫不興如山如阜如岡如陵
如川之方至以莫不增
劉淮
同考試官教諭李　批〔錫福之全擬諸高大盛長〕
〔而以興以增義實相承無非形容臣子愛君無已之意發〕
〔揮明暢讀之可以興焉〕
同考試官教諭胡　批〔寫出臣子祝君之意整雅〕
〔可錄〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔昔謂太和在成周宇宙間〕
punctuated:
命之隆者如此，則天下之所以有賴而各遂者，豈不繫於一人也哉？大抵天人福極，其理一也。善之所至，福亦至焉。誠能上下一於恭敬，則天地自位，萬物自育，四靈畢至，又何啻斂福於身而已？箕子衍《洪範》以著天人之學，而皇極者，《洪範》九疇之樞紐也。建極之義，寔又神禹仰稽天地之心，而發明授受執中之要。周家之所以致太平、爲民極者，不亦有由然哉？

詩

天保定爾，以莫不興。如山如阜，如岡如陵，如川之方至，以莫不增。

劉淮

同考試官教諭李　批〔錫福之全，擬諸高大盛長，〕〔而以興以增，義實相承，無非形容臣子愛君無已之意。發〕〔揮明暢，讀之可以興焉。〕

同考試官教諭胡　批〔寫出臣子祝君之意，整雅〕〔可錄。〕

考試官教諭鄭　批〔昔謂太和在成周宇宙間，〕
translation_en:
…such is the abundance of the favor bestowed by Heaven. Does not everything upon which all under Heaven depend, and through which each fulfills their aspirations, therefore hinge upon this one man? In general, Heaven and humanity, blessings and the supreme standard, share a single principle. Wherever goodness reaches, blessings also arrive. If those above and below can truly be united in reverence and respect, Heaven and Earth will naturally take their proper places, the myriad things will naturally flourish, and the four numinous creatures will all appear. How could this amount merely to gathering blessings upon oneself? Jizi expounded the Great Plan to elucidate the learning concerning Heaven and humanity; the sovereign’s supreme standard is the pivot of the Great Plan’s nine categories. The meaning of establishing that standard also derives from the divine Yu’s reverent examination of the heart of Heaven and Earth, through which he elucidated the essential teaching of holding fast to the Mean, handed down in the transmission of rulership. Was there not, then, a foundation for the Zhou dynasty’s achievement of Great Peace and its establishment of a standard for the people?

Book of Odes

“Heaven protects and establishes you, so that nothing fails to flourish. Like mountains and hills, like ridges and high mounds, like a river’s rising flood, nothing fails to increase.”

Liu Huai

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The completeness of the blessings bestowed is likened to things lofty, great, flourishing, and growing. ‘Flourish’ and ‘increase’ indeed carry the meaning forward in succession: all of this depicts the unceasing love of subjects for their ruler. The exposition is clear and fluent; reading it can stir the heart.”

Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “It expresses the subjects’ wish to invoke blessings upon their ruler. Orderly and elegant, it merits inclusion.”

Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “It was said of old that supreme harmony pervaded Heaven and Earth in the age of Zhou’s consummate rule …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
讀此益信
考試官教諭曲　批〔是善於忠愛其君者〕
臣子願天眷君以全福而必歷擬諸其形容焉
夫福以高大盛長爲全也臣子願天眷君而必
以是焉忠愛之心寧有既乎周之臣子歌天保
所以荅君貺也至此蓋曰人君不難於身享天
下之福而難於福兼天下之全使天之錫之也
而有歉焉是豈吾人之所願哉吾願天心隆其
簡在斂五福於宗子之愛而單厚多益之祉固
愈熾而愈昌也上帝肆其監觀會百順於大君
===
之宜而戩穀罄宜之休固彌壽而彌臧也而亦
何有弗興矣乎夫福矣而高大之未至不可以
言興也今夫休禎磅礴莫與京焉殆如山阜岡
陵者乎物之高大盡乎山阜岡陵而君福之不
可以限量窺者似之蓋巍乎不可及矣福矣而
盛長之未至不可以言興也今夫瑞慶流衍有
難量焉殆川之方至者乎物之盛長盡乎川流
而君福之不可以涯涘測者似之蓋沛然莫之
punctuated:
讀此益信。
考試官教諭曲，批〔是善於忠愛其君者〕。
臣子願天眷君以全福，而必歷擬諸其形容焉。
夫福以高大盛長爲全也，臣子願天眷君而必以是焉，忠愛之心寧有既乎？周之臣子歌《天保》，所以荅君貺也。至此蓋曰：人君不難於身享天下之福，而難於福兼天下之全。使天之錫之也而有歉焉，是豈吾人之所願哉？吾願天心隆其簡在，斂五福於宗子之愛，而單厚多益之祉，固愈熾而愈昌也；上帝肆其監觀，會百順於大君之宜，而戩穀罄宜之休，固彌壽而彌臧也。而亦何有弗興矣乎？夫福矣而高大之未至，不可以言興也。今夫休禎磅礴，莫與京焉，殆如山阜岡陵者乎？物之高大盡乎山阜岡陵，而君福之不可以限量窺者似之，蓋巍乎不可及矣。福矣而盛長之未至，不可以言興也。今夫瑞慶流衍，有難量焉，殆川之方至者乎？物之盛長盡乎川流，而君福之不可以涯涘測者似之，蓋沛然莫之
translation_en:
…Reading this strengthens my belief all the more.
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: “This is someone who knows well how to be loyal to and love his ruler.”
Subjects wish Heaven to favor their ruler with complete blessings, and therefore draw successive comparisons to describe them.
Blessings are complete when they are lofty, great, flourishing, and enduring. When subjects wish Heaven to favor their ruler, they invariably wish for these qualities. Can their loyal and loving hearts ever reach an end? The subjects of Zhou sang “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao) to repay their ruler’s bounty. At this point, they seem to say: For a ruler, the difficulty lies less in personally enjoying the blessings of all under Heaven than in possessing those blessings in their full completeness. If Heaven’s bestowal were in any way deficient, could that possibly be what we desire? We wish Heaven’s heart to deepen its regard for its chosen ruler, gathering the five blessings in its love for the ancestral heir, so that blessings of abundance and increase may surely grow ever more brilliant and prosperous. May the Lord on High extend his watchful gaze, gathering every favorable circumstance for the great ruler’s benefit, so that the blessings of enduring goodness and complete well-being may surely become ever more lasting and excellent. How, then, could they fail to rise?
If blessings have not attained loftiness and greatness, one cannot speak of their rising. Now these auspicious blessings are vast, with nothing to equal them: are they not like mountains, hills, ridges, and mounds? Mountains, hills, ridges, and mounds embody the utmost loftiness and greatness among things. The ruler’s blessings, whose magnitude cannot be apprehended within any fixed limits, resemble them: towering indeed beyond reach! If blessings have not attained flourishing abundance and enduring growth, one cannot speak of their rising. Now these auspicious favors flow and spread beyond all measure: are they not like a river in its rising flood? Flowing rivers embody the utmost flourishing abundance and enduring growth among things. The ruler’s blessings, which cannot be measured by shores or banks, resemble them: surging forth, with nothing to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
能禦矣由是純嘏有緝熙之妙其來也幾微其
究也廣大是克當乎天心者君也而申錫之下
將有與造化同其悠久矣天休有滋至之美其
發也日新其積也富有是栽培乎有德者天也
而眷顧之餘將有與天地相爲終始矣而亦何
有於弗增耶是則唯興也而盛斯不窮唯增也
而興斯有繼保定之福必如是而後全而天心
之仁愛斯其至矣抑人臣祝君未有如天保之
盛者也至推其極始本於先王之孝享終及於
===
羣黎之徧德而惓惓法祖勸民之意溢於褒美
祝頌之外此其所以爲愛君之實者歟噫有周
盛治氣象觀此益可想見
貽我來牟帝命率育無此疆爾界陳常于
時夏
劉希尹
同考試官教諭李　批〔不修雕琢而蔚然可觀可以爲式矣〕
同考試官教諭胡　批〔周人頌后稷之意藹然寫〕
punctuated:
能禦矣。由是，純嘏有緝熙之妙，其來也幾微，其究也廣大。是克當乎天心者，君也；而申錫之下，將有與造化同其悠久矣。天休有滋至之美，其發也日新，其積也富有。是栽培乎有德者，天也；而眷顧之餘，將有與天地相爲終始矣。而亦何有於弗增耶？是則唯興也，而盛斯不窮；唯增也，而興斯有繼。保定之福，必如是而後全，而天心之仁愛，斯其至矣。抑人臣祝君，未有如《天保》之盛者也。至推其極，始本於先王之孝享，終及於羣黎之徧德，而惓惓法祖勸民之意，溢於褒美祝頌之外。此其所以爲愛君之實者歟？噫！有周盛治氣象，觀此益可想見。
「貽我來牟，帝命率育。無此疆爾界，陳常于時夏。」
劉希尹
同考試官教諭李　批〔不修雕琢，而蔚然可觀，可以爲式矣。〕
同考試官教諭胡　批〔周人頌后稷之意，藹然寫〕
translation_en:
…nothing can withstand it. Thus, these great blessings possess the subtle wonder of continuing illumination: imperceptible in their coming, vast in their ultimate reach. It is the ruler who accords with Heaven’s heart; through its repeated bestowals, his blessings will endure as long as the workings of creation. Heaven’s favor has the beauty of arriving in ever greater abundance: daily renewed as it unfolds, rich in its accumulation. It is Heaven that nurtures the virtuous; through its loving regard, the ruler’s blessings will share the beginning and end of Heaven and Earth. How, then, could they fail to increase? Only through flourishing can their abundance be inexhaustible; only through increase can their flourishing continue. The blessings that preserve and secure the ruler must be like this before they are complete, and herein the benevolent love of Heaven’s heart reaches its utmost.
Now, among subjects’ prayers for their ruler, none is as magnificent as “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao). Pursuing its meaning to the fullest, it begins with filial offerings to the former kings and ends with virtue extending throughout the common people. Its earnest intention to encourage emulation of the ancestors and exhortation of the people overflows beyond its praise and benedictions. Is this not what makes it a true expression of love for the ruler? Ah! Reading this, one can all the more readily picture the flourishing governance of the Zhou.
“You bequeathed to us wheat and barley; the Lord on High commanded that all be nourished. Without distinction between this boundary and yours, you established the enduring norms throughout these lands of Xia.”
Liu Xiyin.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔Without elaborate ornamentation, it is richly impressive and worthy of serving as a model.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔The Zhou people’s intention in praising Hou Ji is warmly expressed…〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
出
考試官教諭鄭　批〔頌義是如此作宜録〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔典雅不浮〕
聖人承天意以養民而因得以教民焉蓋教養
治之大經也聖人繼天養民而教成因之如此
此其文德之至所以克配天也歟周人郊祀獻
后稷追述其德以爲樂歌也意謂有不可忘之
德者斯有不容已之報我后稷之所以克配彼
天者固以其有粒民之至德也然何以見其爲
===
德之至哉蓋來牟之播所以導其養以拯阻饑
之民者固稷憫時以奉職也而其始非稷也嘉
種之降所以普其利以惠艱食之民者固稷開
物以成務也而其意則天也何者天生物以養
人不能以直遂也固必有待於人美利利民天
蓋命后稷以成其能焉爾天無心而成化不能
以自弘也固必有藉於人粒我烝民稷蓋順帝
則以賛化育焉爾如是則民生遂矣民性不由
是而可復耶吾知疆界所限習俗若是其異齊
punctuated:
出。
考試官教諭鄭　批〔頌義是如此作，宜録。〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔典雅不浮。〕
聖人承天意以養民，而因得以教民焉。蓋教養，治之大經也。聖人繼天養民，而教成因之如此，此其文德之至，所以克配天也歟！周人郊祀獻后稷，追述其德以爲樂歌也。意謂有不可忘之德者，斯有不容已之報。我后稷之所以克配彼天者，固以其有粒民之至德也。然何以見其爲德之至哉？蓋來牟之播，所以導其養以拯阻饑之民者，固稷憫時以奉職也，而其始非稷也。嘉種之降，所以普其利以惠艱食之民者，固稷開物以成務也，而其意則天也。何者？天生物以養人，不能以直遂也，固必有待於人。美利利民，天蓋命后稷以成其能焉爾。天無心而成化，不能以自弘也，固必有藉於人。粒我烝民，稷蓋順帝則以賛化育焉爾。如是則民生遂矣，民性不由是而可復耶？吾知疆界所限，習俗若是其異齊
translation_en:
…expressed.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔This is how an exposition of the meaning of a hymn should be written. It merits inclusion.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔Classically elegant, without superficiality.〕
The sage follows Heaven’s intent in nourishing the people and thereby gains the means to teach them. Teaching and nourishment are the great guiding principles of government. The sage carries on Heaven’s work of nourishing the people, and successful teaching follows from this. Is this not the consummation of his civil virtue, by which he becomes worthy to be paired with Heaven in sacrifice? When the people of Zhou performed the suburban sacrifice and made offerings to Hou Ji, they recounted his virtue in a song for musical performance. Its meaning is that virtue which cannot be forgotten calls for recompense which cannot be withheld. Our Hou Ji was worthy to be paired with Heaven precisely because he possessed the supreme virtue of feeding the people with grain. But how can we see that his virtue was supreme?
The sowing of wheat and barley provided the means to nourish and rescue people afflicted by hunger. This was indeed Ji’s compassionate response to the difficulties of his age in fulfilling his office; yet it did not originate with Ji. The descent of excellent seeds provided the means to spread their benefits widely and aid people struggling to obtain food. This was indeed Ji’s work of developing the resources of things and bringing undertakings to completion; yet the intention was Heaven’s. Why is this? Heaven produces things to nourish human beings, but cannot accomplish this directly: it must depend upon human beings. To benefit the people with its abundant bounty, Heaven charged Hou Ji to bring its capacities to fruition. Heaven effects transformation without conscious intent, but cannot extend that transformation by itself: it must rely upon human beings. In feeding our multitudes with grain, Ji followed the Lord on High’s principles to assist the work of transformation and nurture.
In this way the people’s livelihood was secured. Could not their inherent nature thereby be restored? I know that, within the limits imposed by territorial boundaries, customs differ so greatly [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
也而綱常之懿則人固有之生養遂而倫理明
會何疆界之足限乎風氣所囿好尚若是其異
宜也而秉彝之心則人同得之衣食足而教化
行會何風氣之可囿乎五教可敷爲五典可惇
爲偏爲稼穡之區皆其明倫之地也是典教者
雖司徒之職也而所以使民得率其教者稷之
功實有足多矣百姓以親焉五品以遜焉盡乎
時夏之中皆其正經之所也是司教者雖契之
責也而不有斯民得遂其養焉契之教豈能得
===
行耶吁此后稷之德所以爲至而郊祀以配天
夫豈不宜也哉抑周人以農事開國者也所以
成八百年有道之長實肇端於此故其制禮舉
郊祀之典尊后稷以配之不忘本也而又追述
其德以爲樂歌昭其功也不忘本者情也昭其
功者義也情義備而仁孝達矣書曰黍稷非馨
明德惟馨其是之謂乎
春秋
春鄭人來輸平〔隱公六年〕
punctuated:
也，而綱常之懿，則人固有之。生養遂而倫理明，會何疆界之足限乎？風氣所囿，好尚若是其異宜也，而秉彝之心，則人同得之。衣食足而教化行，會何風氣之可囿乎？五教可敷爲，五典可惇爲，偏爲稼穡之區，皆其明倫之地也。是典教者，雖司徒之職也，而所以使民得率其教者，稷之功實有足多矣。百姓以親焉，五品以遜焉，盡乎時夏之中，皆其正經之所也。是司教者，雖契之責也，而不有斯民得遂其養焉，契之教豈能得行耶？吁！此后稷之德所以爲至，而郊祀以配天，夫豈不宜也哉？抑周人以農事開國者也，所以成八百年有道之長，實肇端於此。故其制禮，舉郊祀之典，尊后稷以配之，不忘本也；而又追述其德，以爲樂歌，昭其功也。不忘本者，情也；昭其功者，義也。情義備而仁孝達矣。《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」其是之謂乎？

春秋

春，鄭人來輸平。〔隱公六年〕
translation_en:
…yet the excellence of the cardinal bonds and constant moral relationships is inherent in human beings. Once their livelihood is secured and ethical relationships are understood, how could territorial boundaries constrain this? Within the confines of local customs, tastes and preferences differ so greatly; yet all people alike possess a heart endowed with constant moral principles. Once clothing and food are sufficient and moral instruction takes effect, how could local customs confine it? The five teachings can be disseminated, and the five constant relationships strengthened [?]; throughout the regions devoted to sowing and reaping [?], every place becomes a setting for illuminating human relationships. Although responsibility for this instruction belongs to the Minister of Education, Ji’s contribution in enabling the people to follow that instruction is indeed worthy of great praise. Through it, the people become affectionate toward one another, and the five relationships become harmonious. Throughout these lands of Xia, every place becomes a setting for setting the enduring norms aright. Although overseeing instruction was Xie’s responsibility, if the people had not secured their sustenance, how could Xie’s teaching have been put into practice?

Ah! This is why Hou Ji’s virtue was considered supreme. Was it not fitting that he should be honored as Heaven’s associate in the suburban sacrifice? Moreover, the people of Zhou founded their state upon agriculture. Their achievement of eight hundred years of enduring rule in accordance with the Way truly had its beginnings here. Thus, when they established their rites and instituted the suburban sacrifice, they exalted Hou Ji as Heaven’s associate: this was to remember their origins. They also recounted his virtue in ceremonial songs: this was to make his achievements manifest. Remembering one’s origins expresses feeling; making his achievements manifest expresses righteousness. With feeling and righteousness both fulfilled, benevolence and filial devotion find full expression. The Book of Documents says: “It is not the millet offerings that are fragrant; only shining virtue is fragrant.” Is this not what it means?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In spring, men of Zheng came to offer peace.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
何思
同考試官教諭鄭　批　君子恥言利實防其源也
而不知爲國有大義焉觀鄭之納成意欲離魯之黨而解
宋之閧終亦不免於岌岌矣利之不可恃有如此春秋書
之以示戒也作者往往失之此篇發揮傳意殆盡讀之凜
然
考試官教諭鄭　批　說義利處明潔可錄
考試官教諭曲　批　得謹嚴體
===
內外以利結成春秋貶之以示戒也此見爲國
以義不以利也鄭魯之平異是春秋貶之以示
戒也宜哉且鄭魯搆怨爲日已久茲胡爲而平
耶蓋以鄭間宋魯之隙用離合兵之黨于是乎
來輸平焉春秋何貶之彼脩睦以蕃王室者諸
侯之職循義以保治安者立國之本今乃假釋
怨之名而利交是奉崇鄙夫之行而大道罔聞
前乎此者狐壤之止宿地之盟宋魯之恩怨明
矣茲果何爲而向背若是其外耶後乎此者祊
田之歸郜防之取宋鄭之雠好驗矣又果何爲
punctuated:
何思

同考試官教諭鄭批：君子恥言利，實防其源也，而不知爲國有大義焉。觀鄭之納成，意欲離魯之黨而解宋之閧，終亦不免於岌岌矣。利之不可恃有如此，春秋書之以示戒也。作者往往失之，此篇發揮傳意殆盡，讀之凜然。

考試官教諭鄭批：說義利處明潔可錄。

考試官教諭曲批：得謹嚴體。

內外以利結成，春秋貶之以示戒也。此見爲國以義不以利也。鄭魯之平異是，春秋貶之以示戒也，宜哉！且鄭魯搆怨爲日已久，茲胡爲而平耶？蓋以鄭間宋魯之隙，用離合兵之黨，於是乎來輸平焉。春秋何貶之？彼脩睦以蕃王室者，諸侯之職；循義以保治安者，立國之本。今乃假釋怨之名，而利交是奉；崇鄙夫之行，而大道罔聞。前乎此者，狐壤之止、宿地之盟，宋魯之恩怨明矣。茲果何爲而向背若是其外耶？後乎此者，祊田之歸、郜防之取，宋鄭之雠好驗矣。又果何爲
translation_en:
He Si 何思

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The gentleman is ashamed to speak of profit: this is truly to guard against it at its source. Yet people fail to understand that governing a state involves great principles of righteousness. Consider Zheng’s offer of peace: its intention was to break up Lu’s alliance and resolve its conflict with Song, yet in the end it still could not escape its precarious position. Such is the unreliability of profit. The Spring and Autumn Annals records this as a warning. Writers frequently miss this point; this essay brings out almost the entire meaning of the commentary. Reading it inspires solemn apprehension.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “The discussion of righteousness and profit is clear and concise, and merits inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: “It achieves a scrupulous and rigorous style.”

When the home state and an outside state conclude peace for profit, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures them to convey a warning. This shows that a state should be governed through righteousness, not profit. The peace between Zheng and Lu departed from this principle. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals censures it as a warning! Moreover, Zheng and Lu had long been at enmity. Why, then, did they now make peace? Zheng sought to exploit the rift between Song and Lu to break apart their military alliance; thus it came to offer peace. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals censure this? Cultivating harmonious relations to serve as a bulwark for the royal house is the duty of the feudal lords; following righteousness to preserve order and security is the foundation of a state. Now, however, under the pretext of settling grievances, they pursued only connections based on profit. They exalted the conduct of petty men and paid no heed to the Great Way.

Earlier, the detention at Hurang and the covenant at Su had made clear the enmity and friendship between Song and Lu. Why, then, did their allegiances and opposition now display such estrangement [?]? Subsequently, the transfer of the fields of Beng and the capture of Gao and Fang would furnish evidence of the enmity and friendship between Song and Zheng. Again, why indeed …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
而從違若是其悖耶鄭之意豈不以伐國圍邑
被宋之困極矣與其較兵革以取勝曷若散黨
與以求安殊不知自強爲善者雖大國何畏焉
顧欲賂友邦以紓目前之患其謀國亦踈矣魯
之意豈不以勤兵會伐爲宋之役頻矣與其尋
舊好而無功孰若許新成以獲地殊不知以理
律身者雖天下弗顧焉遽欲絕友邦以快啓疆
之心其制行亦卑矣以若所爲利源開而末流
之弊愈滋善念微而效尤之風益熾將使爲臣
===
懷利以事君爲子懷利以事父爲弟懷利以事
兄法軌既斁而乖戾將興其何以致理乎諸侯
求以利其國大夫求以利其家士庶人求以利
其身綱紀既失而攘奪必至豈可以爲訓乎聖
人特稱輸平以貶之明有國者正其義不謀其
利著守國保家之道也由是觀之聖人不以輸
平爲難而以明義爲貴然則崇小善而潰大防
者爲足取乎抑鄭魯之失豈止於是鄭莊克叔
段而兄弟之情薄魯隱擅卽位而君臣之義乖
punctuated:
而從違若是其悖耶？鄭之意豈不以伐國圍邑，被宋之困極矣，與其較兵革以取勝，曷若散黨與以求安？殊不知自強爲善者，雖大國何畏焉？顧欲賂友邦以紓目前之患，其謀國亦踈矣。魯之意豈不以勤兵會伐，爲宋之役頻矣，與其尋舊好而無功，孰若許新成以獲地？殊不知以理律身者，雖天下弗顧焉。遽欲絕友邦以快啓疆之心，其制行亦卑矣。
以若所爲，利源開而末流之弊愈滋，善念微而效尤之風益熾。將使爲臣懷利以事君，爲子懷利以事父，爲弟懷利以事兄。法軌既斁而乖戾將興，其何以致理乎？諸侯求以利其國，大夫求以利其家，士庶人求以利其身。綱紀既失而攘奪必至，豈可以爲訓乎？聖人特稱輸平以貶之，明有國者正其義不謀其利，著守國保家之道也。由是觀之，聖人不以輸平爲難，而以明義爲貴。然則崇小善而潰大防者，爲足取乎？抑鄭魯之失豈止於是？鄭莊克叔段而兄弟之情薄，魯隱擅卽位而君臣之義乖。
translation_en:
…and why were their choices of whom to follow and whom to oppose so perverse? Was Zheng’s reasoning not that, through attacks upon its state and sieges of its towns, it had suffered extreme distress at Song’s hands, and that, rather than seeking victory through a contest of arms, it would be better to break up Song’s alliances and seek security? Little did it understand that those who strengthen themselves and practice goodness have nothing to fear even from a great state. Instead, it sought to bribe a friendly state to relieve its immediate troubles: its planning for the state was indeed shortsighted. Was Lu’s reasoning not that it had repeatedly mobilized its troops for joint attacks in Song’s service, and that, rather than renewing an old friendship without benefit, it would be better to accept a new peace and acquire territory? Little did it understand that those who regulate their conduct by principle need not be deterred even by the whole world. Yet it hastily sought to sever relations with a friendly state to gratify its desire to expand its territory: its standard of conduct was indeed base.
With conduct such as this, the source of profit-seeking is opened, and its downstream abuses multiply; good intentions dwindle, and the tendency to imitate wrongdoing grows ever more intense. It will lead ministers to serve their rulers with profit in mind, sons to serve their fathers with profit in mind, and younger brothers to serve their elder brothers with profit in mind. Once established norms are ruined, disorder will arise: how could good government then be achieved? The feudal lords seek to profit their states, the grandees to profit their houses, and the gentlemen and common people to profit themselves. Once the guiding bonds of order are lost, seizure and plunder must follow: how could this serve as an example? The Sage specifically uses the expression “offering peace” to censure them, making clear that those who possess states must uphold righteousness rather than scheme for profit, and setting forth the way to preserve states and protect houses. Viewed in this light, the Sage does not regard offering peace as the difficult achievement; he prizes making righteousness clear. Can conduct that honors a minor good while breaching the great moral safeguards, then, deserve approval? Moreover, were the failings of Zheng and Lu confined to this? Duke Zhuang of Zheng defeated Shu Duan, showing scant affection between brothers; Duke Yin of Lu assumed the rulership without authority, violating the righteousness proper to ruler and minister…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
他何足責哉聖人嚴義利之辨特假輸平以立
法耳他日孟子述其意以告梁惠王而宋牼之
對反覆推明其說蓋學孔子而有得者然則有
國者可不慎諸
春王三月及齊平　夏公會齊侯于夾谷
公至自夾谷　齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田
〔俱定公十年〕
孫文登
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔魯有三家而不能專用孔子是貽敵於齊也故始爲求好而無所處繼歸侵田而不〕
===
〔能文魯亦奈齊之何作者非泛則俗周悉明整僅見此篇〕
〔錄之以式多士〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔有斷制是長於春秋者〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔精到〕
望國始結成而有以畏乎大國繼講好而有以
化乎大國夫兵非爲國可恃而理乃化強之本
也攷諸魯定之行事而其義自明矣昔定公當
國齊魯交兵至是魯欲釋齊之怨遂要齊侯以
punctuated:
他何足責哉？聖人嚴義利之辨，特假輸平以立法耳。他日孟子述其意以告梁惠王，而宋牼之對，反覆推明其說，蓋學孔子而有得者。然則有國者可不慎諸？
春王三月，及齊平。夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕
孫文登
同考試官教諭鄭批〔魯有三家而不能專用孔子，是貽敵於齊也。故始爲求好而無所處，繼歸侵田而不〕〔能文魯，亦奈齊之何？作者非泛則俗，周悉明整，僅見此篇。〕〔錄之以式多士。〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔有斷制，是長於春秋者。〕
考試官教諭曲批〔精到。〕
望國始結成而有以畏乎大國，繼講好而有以化乎大國。夫兵非爲國可恃，而理乃化強之本也。攷諸魯定之行事，而其義自明矣。昔定公當國，齊魯交兵。至是，魯欲釋齊之怨，遂要齊侯以
translation_en:
…What else need be reproached? The Sage drew a strict distinction between righteousness and profit, merely using the making of peace to establish a rule. Later, Mengzi expounded this meaning to King Hui of Liang, and in his response to Song Keng repeatedly developed and clarified this teaching. He was indeed someone who had learned from Confucius and gained understanding. How, then, can those who possess a state fail to exercise caution?
“In spring, in the third month of the royal calendar, we made peace with Qi. In summer, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The duke returned from Jiagu. The people of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” 〔All are from the tenth year of Duke Ding.〕
Sun Wendeng
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔“Lu had the Three Families and could not give Confucius exclusive authority: this was to give Qi an opportunity to act as its enemy. Thus, at first it sought friendly relations but had no means of managing the situation; later, the occupied lands were returned, yet this could not〕〔embellish Lu’s standing [?]. What, then, could Lu do about Qi? Other writers are either vague or commonplace; only this essay is comprehensive, clear, and well ordered.”〕 〔“It is recorded here to serve as a model for the candidates.”〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔“It shows decisive judgment: here is someone accomplished in the Spring and Autumn Annals.”〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Refined and penetrating.”〕
A state of standing [?] first concluded peace, having reason to fear the great state; afterward it cultivated friendly relations, having the means to transform the great state. Military force is not what one can rely upon in governing a state; moral principle is the foundation for transforming the powerful. Examine the actions of Duke Ding of Lu, and this meaning becomes clear of itself. Formerly, when Duke Ding governed the state, Qi and Lu were at war. At this point, Lu wished to resolve Qi’s resentment and therefore invited the Marquis of Qi to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
平兩君相好而休兵息民之令行焉是舉也請
之者魯許之者齊何以見魯之畏耶蓋以定公
初年三家專政欲其歸怨於君上顧乃導公以
虐齊方其初侵也爲陽州之次激其出戰之心
及其再侵也攻廩丘之郛致其焚衝之慘魯無
大義可執倡甲冑啓戎之端齊無大罪可討犯
佳兵不祥之戒于是惴惴以求好用蓋前行之
愆汲汲于行成以息將來之報不然則景公無
四境之虞而國夏諸臣又非久於下人者安能
===
忘侵犯之故而即魯以平哉故紀平書及以見
其我之所欲魯公以弱畏人之失不于是可見
乎嗣是魯再尋齊之好復有夾谷之會公方至
國齊以鄆讙龜陰之田歸焉是舉也請會者魯
歸田者齊何以見魯之化耶蓋以定公中年孔
子攝相知齊有用詐劫好之常乃預爲左右司
馬之具壇坫初登也萊兵方起則折以用夷亂
華之罪會好既成也享禮將設則正其嘉樂野
合之非從容於禮文之間而犂彌之計無所施
punctuated:
平。兩君相好，而休兵息民之令行焉。是舉也，請之者魯，許之者齊，何以見魯之畏耶？蓋以定公初年，三家專政，欲其歸怨於君上，顧乃導公以虐齊。方其初侵也，爲陽州之次，激其出戰之心；及其再侵也，攻廩丘之郛，致其焚衝之慘。魯無大義可執，倡甲冑啓戎之端；齊無大罪可討，犯佳兵不祥之戒。于是惴惴以求好，用蓋前行之愆；汲汲于行成，以息將來之報。不然，則景公無四境之虞，而國夏諸臣又非久於下人者，安能忘侵犯之故，而即魯以平哉？故紀平書及，以見其我之所欲。魯公以弱畏人之失，不于是可見乎？

嗣是，魯再尋齊之好，復有夾谷之會。公方至國，齊以鄆、讙、龜陰之田歸焉。是舉也，請會者魯，歸田者齊，何以見魯之化耶？蓋以定公中年，孔子攝相，知齊有用詐劫好之常，乃預爲左右司馬之具。壇坫初登也，萊兵方起，則折以用夷亂華之罪；會好既成也，享禮將設，則正其嘉樂野合之非。從容於禮文之間，而犂彌之計無所施，
translation_en:
…make peace. The two rulers established friendly relations, and orders to cease hostilities and give the people respite took effect. In this undertaking, Lu made the request and Qi consented. How does this reveal Lu’s fear? In the early years of Duke Ding’s reign, the three great families monopolized government. Wishing resentment to fall upon their ruler, they instead led the duke into aggression against Qi. During the first invasion, they encamped at Yangzhou, provoking Qi to come out and fight; during the second, they attacked the outer walls of Linqiu, bringing about the calamity of the burning siege vehicles. Lu had no great righteous cause to uphold, yet took up arms and initiated hostilities. Qi had committed no great offense warranting punishment, yet Lu violated the admonition that delighting in arms brings misfortune. Thus Lu sought friendship in trepidation, hoping to cover the faults of its earlier conduct, and urgently pursued peace to avert future retaliation. Otherwise, Duke Jing faced no danger along his borders, and Guo Xia and the other ministers were hardly men to remain subordinate to others: how could they have forgotten the invasions and approached Lu to make peace? Thus, in recording the peace, the text uses the word ji, “with,” to show that it was something desired by our side, Lu. Is not the duke of Lu’s failing—fearing others because of his weakness—apparent here?

After this, Lu renewed its friendship with Qi, and another meeting took place at Jiagu. The duke had only just returned to his state when Qi restored the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. In this undertaking, Lu requested the meeting, while Qi returned the lands. How does this reveal Lu’s power to transform others? In the middle years of Duke Ding’s reign, Confucius served as acting chief minister. Knowing that Qi habitually used deception and coercion in conducting friendly relations, he made advance arrangements for the Commanders of the Left and Right. When they first ascended the ceremonial platform and troops from Lai rose up, he rebuked Qi for the offense of using barbarians to disrupt the Chinese states. Once friendly relations had been established at the meeting and a ceremonial banquet was about to be prepared, he corrected the impropriety of performing ceremonial music at a gathering in the open countryside. Moving with composure amid the forms of ritual, he left Li Mi no opportunity to put his scheme into effect…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
發强於行事之際而侏儒之誅尤可懼于是君
則引咎責躬而以相率夷狄爲恥臣則謝過以
質而以鄆讙龜陰來歸不然景公方强於爲國
而晏子賢臣又未可以力勝者安能致屈服之
誠而惟魯是聽哉故於夾谷之會繼以三田之
歸聖人以理化强之效不于是可徵乎夫魯一
也用失其人則悖用得其人則强然則人君之
用舍可不擇哉大抵定公非有爲之君魯國終
於不治亦其自致也三家植根膠固乃去之不
===
決孔子過化存神乃用之不專三都雖隳而公
室弗張女樂一阻而孔子遂去厥後國都被伐
宗社震驚卒無以勝齊之强豈不深可惜哉夫
子脩經拳拳於平會之間立法以訓後世有國
者可不鑒乎
禮記
大學之法禁於未發之謂豫當其可之謂
時不陵節而施之謂孫相觀而善之謂
摩此四者敎之所由興也
punctuated:
發强於行事之際，而侏儒之誅尤可懼。于是君則引咎責躬，而以相率夷狄爲恥；臣則謝過以質，而以鄆讙龜陰來歸。不然，景公方强於爲國，而晏子賢臣，又未可以力勝者，安能致屈服之誠，而惟魯是聽哉？故於夾谷之會，繼以三田之歸，聖人以理化强之效，不于是可徵乎？夫魯一也，用失其人則悖，用得其人則强。然則人君之用舍，可不擇哉？大抵定公非有爲之君，魯國終於不治，亦其自致也。三家植根膠固，乃去之不決；孔子過化存神，乃用之不專。三都雖隳，而公室弗張；女樂一阻，而孔子遂去。厥後國都被伐，宗社震驚，卒無以勝齊之强，豈不深可惜哉？夫子脩經，拳拳於平會之間，立法以訓後世，有國者可不鑒乎？

禮記

大學之法：禁於未發之謂豫，當其可之謂時，不陵節而施之謂孫，相觀而善之謂摩。此四者，敎之所由興也。
translation_en:
…He displayed his strength when action was required, and the execution of the dwarfs was especially fearsome. Thereupon the ruler acknowledged his fault and reproached himself, ashamed of having joined others in leading barbarians; his ministers sincerely acknowledged their errors [?] and returned the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. Otherwise, Duke Jing was then governing his state vigorously, and Yanzi was a worthy minister: they could not simply have been overcome by force. How could they have been brought to submit sincerely and heed Lu alone? Thus the meeting at Jiagu was followed by the return of the three territories. Does this not demonstrate the sage’s efficacy in transforming the powerful through moral principle?

Lu was the same state throughout: when it employed the wrong men, its conduct went astray; when it employed the right men, it became strong. Can a ruler, then, fail to exercise care in deciding whom to employ and whom to dismiss? In general, Duke Ding was no ruler of achievement, and Lu’s ultimate failure to attain good government was also of his own making. The Three Families were deeply rooted and firmly entrenched, yet he was irresolute about removing them. Confucius transformed people wherever he passed and exerted a spiritual influence wherever he remained, yet the duke did not employ him with undivided trust. Although the three strongholds were demolished, the ducal house did not gain strength; once female entertainers became an impediment, Confucius departed. Thereafter the capital was attacked, the ancestral temples and altars of state were shaken with alarm, and Lu ultimately had no means of overcoming Qi’s power. Is this not profoundly regrettable? In compiling the Classic, the Master devoted earnest attention to settlements of peace and meetings between rulers, establishing standards to instruct later generations. Can those who govern states fail to take warning?

Book of Rites

The methods of the Great Learning are these: preventing faults before they arise is called anticipation; acting at the appropriate moment is called timeliness; imparting instruction without overstepping the stages of learning is called orderly progression; observing one another and thereby improving is called mutual refinement. These four are the means by which teaching flourishes.

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
楊永貴
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔豫時孫摩處上子作者多　欠發明此作詞意充足蓋留心于體認者錄之以式〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔教與處發明殆盡〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔精切〕
記者詳大學之法因著教之所由成焉夫教明
乎道而立於法也聖王之教以是焉而有不成
焉者鮮矣記者述之所以詔爲師者如此若曰
爲政以人才爲本人才由善教而成大學教人
===
之法果何如耶是故人之生也不能無欲倏其
發而制之計亦晩矣故必窒慾之方施於念慮
之將萌閑邪之術運於事機之未露先事而慮
不見是圖也不有所謂豫乎學之悟也自有其
機及其至而達焉則沛然矣故必因其能憤悱
也而後加夫啓發之功見其將自得也而後益
以時雨之化觸機而應適當其期也不有所謂
時乎學莫要於循序躐等而教是誣之也于焉
進必有方不陵躐以强其不能因才而篤必優
punctuated:
楊永貴

同考試官教諭蔡，批〔豫時孫摩處上子，作者多欠發明，此作詞意充足，蓋留心于體認者，錄之以式。〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔教與處發明殆盡。〕
考試官教諭曲，批〔精切。〕

記者詳大學之法，因著教之所由成焉。夫教明乎道而立於法也，聖王之教以是焉，而有不成焉者鮮矣。記者述之，所以詔爲師者如此。若曰：爲政以人才爲本，人才由善教而成，大學教人之法果何如耶？是故人之生也，不能無欲，倏其發而制之，計亦晩矣。故必窒慾之方施於念慮之將萌，閑邪之術運於事機之未露，先事而慮，不見是圖也，不有所謂豫乎？學之悟也，自有其機，及其至而達焉，則沛然矣。故必因其能憤悱也，而後加夫啓發之功；見其將自得也，而後益以時雨之化。觸機而應，適當其期也，不有所謂時乎？學莫要於循序，躐等而教，是誣之也。于焉進必有方，不陵躐以强其不能，因才而篤，必優
translation_en:
Yang Yonggui

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔In treating anticipation, timeliness, orderly progression, and mutual refinement, the wording here is doubtful [?]. Writers often fail to elucidate these matters adequately. This composition is full in both expression and meaning, evidently the work of someone attentive to understanding them through personal reflection. It is selected to serve as a model.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The passage on the flourishing of education [?] elucidates the subject almost exhaustively.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔Precise and incisive.〕

The recorder explains in detail the methods of the Great Learning, thereby revealing how education succeeds. Education makes the Way clear and is established through proper methods. The sage kings taught by these means, and instances of failure were rare indeed. Such is the instruction for teachers conveyed by the recorder’s account. It is as though he were saying: government takes men of talent as its foundation, and men of talent are formed through good teaching. What, then, are the methods by which the Great Learning teaches people?

People cannot be born without desires. To restrain these only when they suddenly emerge is already too late a strategy. Thus methods for checking desire must be applied when thoughts are about to sprout, and means for warding off perversity must be employed before the incipient signs of action have appeared. To consider matters before they happen and plan for what is not yet visible—is this not what is called anticipation?

Understanding in learning has its own opportune moment. If one brings it to realization when that moment arrives, it flows abundantly. Thus one must wait until learners are struggling to understand and express themselves before undertaking the work of opening their minds; one must see that they are about to grasp something for themselves before further benefiting them with instruction that transforms like timely rain. To respond when the opportunity presents itself, at precisely the right moment—is this not what is called timeliness?

Nothing in learning is more essential than proceeding in sequence. Teaching that skips stages misleads the learner. Thus advancement must follow a proper course, without overstepping stages to force learners to do what they cannot. One must nurture them according to their capacities and must allow them ease…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
游以待其自化事有難易教有本末也非孫耶
成德莫貴於交脩孤立無與則業荒矣于焉見
賢思齊使知善之可爲不賢自省使求義之當
徙交相切磋互爲砥礪也非摩耶夫豫則有以
防其情時則有以成其性科設而軌範以端孫
則有以因其類摩則有以輔其仁法立而化義
以寓施之者非悖也求之者非拂也誘掖獎勸
之下咸有成德達村之望將日成其亹亹矣師
之所以爲教者善教也弟子之所以爲學者善
===
學也觀感興起之餘咸有懋脩錫類之功將日
見其濟濟矣夫教之興也孰能禦之此士有成
德而治有成功不其然乎抑大學之法固足以
致教之興矣然非本諸身則亦徒法焉爾也故
先王昭德塞違立於無過之地是以言不逆理
而民作辭行不踰矩而民作則教之成也特易
易耳後世知不出此而規規於條教之末無惑
乎人才之不古若也故曰古之成村也易今之
成村也難
punctuated: 游以待其自化，事有難易，教有本末也，非孫耶？成德莫貴於交脩，孤立無與則業荒矣。于焉見賢思齊，使知善之可爲；不賢自省，使求義之當徙。交相切磋，互爲砥礪也，非摩耶？夫豫則有以防其情，時則有以成其性，科設而軌範以端；孫則有以因其類，摩則有以輔其仁，法立而化義以寓。施之者非悖也，求之者非拂也。誘掖獎勸之下，咸有成德達村之望，將日成其亹亹矣。師之所以爲教者善教也，弟子之所以爲學者善學也。觀感興起之餘，咸有懋脩錫類之功，將日見其濟濟矣。夫教之興也，孰能禦之？此士有成德而治有成功，不其然乎？抑大學之法固足以致教之興矣，然非本諸身，則亦徒法焉爾也。故先王昭德塞違，立於無過之地，是以言不逆理而民作辭，行不踰矩而民作則。教之成也，特易易耳。後世知不出此，而規規於條教之末，無惑乎人才之不古若也。故曰：「古之成村也易，今之成村也難。」
translation_en:
…at ease, awaiting their spontaneous transformation. Tasks differ in difficulty, and teaching has its fundamentals and its subsidiary details: is this not orderly progression? In perfecting virtue, nothing is more valuable than mutual cultivation; standing alone without companions, one’s studies fall into neglect. Thus, on seeing the worthy, students aspire to equal them and come to know that goodness is attainable; on seeing the unworthy, they examine themselves and seek the right course toward which they should turn. They polish one another through discussion and serve as mutual whetstones: is this not mutual refinement?

Anticipatory guidance provides the means to guard their feelings; timely instruction provides the means to perfect their nature. A curriculum is established, and standards are thereby set aright. Orderly progression provides the means to accommodate their differing aptitudes; mutual refinement provides the means to foster their benevolence. Methods are established, embodying the principles of moral transformation. Those who impart instruction do not act perversely, and those who seek learning do not resist it. Through guidance, assistance, encouragement, and exhortation, all have the prospect of perfecting their virtue and developing their talents [?], becoming daily more diligent. The teachers teach well, and the disciples learn well. Inspired by what they observe and experience, all achieve results in earnest cultivation and in extending goodness to others of their kind; day by day, a flourishing company of worthy people will emerge.

Who, then, could check the flourishing of education? Scholars thus attain perfected virtue, and government attains successful results: is this not so? Yet although the methods of the Great Learning are indeed sufficient to bring about the flourishing of education, unless they are rooted in one’s own person, they remain mere methods. Therefore, the former kings manifested virtue and prevented wrongdoing, establishing themselves where they were free of faults. Their words did not run counter to principle, and the people took them as expressions to follow; their conduct did not transgress the rules, and the people took it as their model. Bringing education to fruition was thus exceedingly easy. In later ages, understanding did not extend to this, and people confined themselves narrowly to the minutiae of instructional regulations. No wonder talented people failed to equal those of antiquity. Thus it is said: “In antiquity, developing talent [?] was easy; today, developing talent [?] is difficult.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
射者何以射何以聽循聲而發發而不失
正鵠者其唯賢者乎
張冲霄
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔善形容何字意子其禮樂〕
〔兼得者耶可嘉可嘉〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔詞理俱到〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔典雅可觀〕
聖人論射者兼盡禮樂之難而因歸之君子焉
蓋射比禮樂而實難於兼盡者也自非君子其
===
孰能與於此哉記射義者引夫子之言有曰射
者男子之事而可數為以立德行者也先王恐
其愿慤無文而不足以飭天下之觀也故嘗飾
之以禮樂矣然豈可以易能耶蓋聽樂以耳而
容則運于身者也使射一于射則凡動容合禮
者皆可能矣奚其難惟夫射不專于禮也而復
欲節比于樂焉吾知心在于樂則容節或有所
遺矣何以能聽樂之音而又不失射之容矣乎
聽一于聽則凡審聲知音者皆可能矣奚其難
punctuated:
射者何以射？何以聽？循聲而發，發而不失正鵠者，其唯賢者乎？
張冲霄
同考試官教諭蔡，批〔善形容何字意。子其禮樂〕〔兼得者耶？可嘉，可嘉！〕
考試官教諭鄭，批〔詞理俱到。〕
考試官教諭曲，批〔典雅可觀。〕
聖人論射者兼盡禮樂之難，而因歸之君子焉。蓋射比禮樂，而實難於兼盡者也。自非君子，其孰能與於此哉？記射義者引夫子之言，有曰：「射者，男子之事，而可數為以立德行者也。」先王恐其愿慤無文，而不足以飭天下之觀也，故嘗飾之以禮樂矣。然豈可以易能耶？蓋聽樂以耳，而容則運于身者也。使射一于射，則凡動容合禮者皆可能矣，奚其難？惟夫射不專于禮也，而復欲節比于樂焉，吾知心在于樂，則容節或有所遺矣。何以能聽樂之音，而又不失射之容矣乎？聽一于聽，則凡審聲知音者皆可能矣，奚其難？
translation_en:
“How does the archer shoot? How does he listen? Surely only a worthy person can release the arrow in time with the music and, on releasing it, never miss the center of the target?”
Zhang Chongxiao
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “You express well the meaning of the word ‘how.’ Are you one who has mastered both ritual and music? Admirable, admirable!”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant, well worth reading.”
In discussing archery, the Sage addresses the difficulty of fully satisfying the requirements of both ritual and music, and accordingly attributes this accomplishment to the gentleman. For archery conforms to ritual and music, yet fully satisfying both is truly difficult. Who but a gentleman could attain this? The author of The Meaning of Archery quotes the Master as saying: “Archery is a man’s occupation, which he may practice repeatedly to establish virtuous conduct.” The former kings feared that it would be earnest and sincere but lack refinement, and thus be insufficient to provide an impressive spectacle for the world; they therefore adorned it with ritual and music. Yet how could proficiency in it be considered easy? Music is heard with the ears, while deportment is expressed through the movements of the body. If shooting were concerned solely with shooting, anyone whose movements accorded with ritual could accomplish it. What difficulty would there be? But archery is not concerned exclusively with ritual: its timing must also accord with music. I know that when the mind attends to music, some requirements of deportment may be overlooked. How can one listen to the sounds of music without losing the proper deportment of archery? If listening were concerned solely with listening, anyone able to distinguish sounds and understand music could accomplish it. What difficulty would there be? …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
惟夫射不專于樂也而復欲容比于禮焉吾知
心在于禮則音節或有所遺矣何以能善射之
容而能聽樂之音矣乎禮樂既涉于異致射聽
信難于兼得矣求其循聲而發而音射之相恊
發中正鵠而舍矢之如破其唯賢者乎蓋賢者
樂以治心而和順素畜于中積禮以治躬而威
儀素安于卒度情深而文明也體具而用周也
蓋不惟容比于禮而且節比于樂矣聲音與耳
謀也動容與身謀也蓋不惟聽足以聽而且巧
足以中矣否則得乎樂或失乎禮心乎射或忘
===
乎聽矣彼將安能以中哉射聽兼得信非賢者
不能也射者豈可以射爲易而不以賢者爲則
耶雖然射一藝也而奚必禮樂之皆得耶蓋古
者諸侯歲獻貢士于天子天子試之于射宮其
容體比禮節奏比樂而中多者益地以示慶其
不能者削地以讓之夫其所繫一至於此是射
也而可以弗重乎是故先王隆之也柰何尚德
之風微而貫革之射興則不知所謂射者爲何
punctuated: 惟夫射不專于樂也，而復欲容比于禮焉。吾知心在于禮，則音節或有所遺矣，何以能善射之容而能聽樂之音矣乎？禮樂既涉于異致，射聽信難于兼得矣。求其循聲而發，而音射之相恊，發中正鵠，而舍矢之如破，其唯賢者乎？蓋賢者樂以治心，而和順素畜于中；積禮以治躬，而威儀素安于卒度。情深而文明也，體具而用周也。蓋不惟容比于禮，而且節比于樂矣；聲音與耳謀也，動容與身謀也。蓋不惟聽足以聽，而且巧足以中矣。否則得乎樂，或失乎禮；心乎射，或忘乎聽矣。彼將安能以中哉？射聽兼得，信非賢者不能也。射者豈可以射爲易，而不以賢者爲則耶？雖然，射一藝也，而奚必禮樂之皆得耶？蓋古者諸侯歲獻貢士于天子，天子試之于射宮。其容體比禮、節奏比樂而中多者，益地以示慶；其不能者，削地以讓之。夫其所繫一至於此，是射也，而可以弗重乎？是故先王隆之也。柰何尚德之風微，而貫革之射興，則不知所謂射者爲何
translation_en:
Yet archery is not concerned exclusively with music: the archer’s bearing must also accord with ritual. I know that when the mind attends to ritual, something of the musical rhythm may be missed. How, then, can one perfect one’s bearing in archery while also attending to the sounds of music? Since ritual and music have different aims, shooting and listening are indeed difficult to accomplish together. To seek someone who releases the arrow in time with the sound, so that music and shooting accord, who hits the center of the target and releases the arrow as though piercing it—would this not require a worthy person? For the worthy person uses music to regulate his heart, so that harmony and compliance are habitually nurtured within; he accumulates practice in ritual to regulate his person, so that his dignified bearing is habitually at ease within the prescribed measures [?]. His feelings are profound and their expression cultured; the substance is complete and its application comprehensive. Thus not only does his bearing accord with ritual, but his timing also accords with music. Sounds work in concert with his ears, and movements work in concert with his body. Not only is his hearing sufficient to attend to the music, but his skill is also sufficient to hit the target. Otherwise, success in music may entail failure in ritual, and attention to shooting may entail forgetting to listen. How could such a person hit the mark? Truly, only a worthy person can accomplish both shooting and listening. How, then, could an archer regard archery as easy and fail to take the worthy person as his model?

Even so, archery is but one art: why must one master both ritual and music in it? In antiquity, the regional lords annually presented recommended men to the Son of Heaven, who tested them in the archery hall. Where their bearing accorded with ritual, their timing accorded with music, and they scored many hits, he enlarged their lord’s territory to express approval; where they failed, he reduced the territory as a reprimand. When so much depended upon it, could archery be treated as unimportant? This is why the former kings accorded it such honor. Alas, the practice of esteeming virtue declined, while archery devoted to piercing leather arose, until people no longer knew what this thing called archery was …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
物矣如禮何如樂何此孔子所以思古也嗚呼
射禮至今在也有志于射者其圖之
第貳塲
論
君子莫大乎與人爲善
申嘉瑞
同考試官教諭崔　批　文似織錦理如貫珠聖人
公善之心宛在意表自非積學之士惡能以及此耶
同考試官學正林　批　大舜與人爲善之旨未易
形容塲中作者非泛則深漫無眞見此卷體格渾成才思
清逸有養之士也高薦何忝
考試官教諭鄭　批　思婉意足塲中獨見此篇
考試官教諭曲　批　精確
===
性統天下之善者也聖人取善於天下而天下
歸於聖人是故聖人之善合天下而成其大矣
夫善原於性雖有人己之分而實無彼此之間
者也夫惟有我之心勝則見己而不見人故善
之在人者止於人而無以與於己善之在己者
punctuated:
物矣！如禮何？如樂何？此孔子所以思古也。嗚呼！射禮至今在也，有志于射者其圖之。

第貳塲

論

君子莫大乎與人爲善

申嘉瑞

同考試官教諭崔批：文似織錦，理如貫珠。聖人公善之心宛在意表，自非積學之士，惡能以及此耶？

同考試官學正林批：大舜與人爲善之旨，未易形容。塲中作者非泛則深，漫無眞見。此卷體格渾成，才思清逸，有養之士也，高薦何忝？

考試官教諭鄭批：思婉意足，塲中獨見此篇。

考試官教諭曲批：精確。

性統天下之善者也。聖人取善於天下，而天下歸於聖人，是故聖人之善合天下而成其大矣。夫善原於性，雖有人己之分，而實無彼此之間者也。夫惟有我之心勝，則見己而不見人，故善之在人者止於人，而無以與於己；善之在己者
translation_en:
…what archery is! What, then, becomes of ritual? What becomes of music? This is why Confucius yearned for antiquity. Alas! The rites of archery still survive today. Let those who aspire to practice archery give thought to this.

Second Session

Discourse

“For the gentleman, nothing is greater than joining with others in doing good.”

Shen Jiarui

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: The writing resembles woven brocade; the reasoning is like a string of pearls. The sage’s intention to share goodness with all emerges vividly beyond the words. Without accumulated learning, how could anyone attain this?

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Director of Studies: The purport of the great Shun’s joining with others in doing good is not easily expressed. Writers in the examination hall are either vague or obscurely profound [?], altogether lacking true insight. This paper is fully integrated in form and structure, and its literary inspiration is clear and graceful. Its author is a man of cultivated attainments. What shame could there be in recommending him highly?

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The thinking is subtle and the meaning fully expressed. Among the essays in the examination hall, this alone has these qualities.

Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: Refined and precise.

Human nature encompasses all the goodness under Heaven. The sage draws goodness from all under Heaven, and all under Heaven turn to the sage. Thus the sage’s goodness achieves its greatness by bringing together the goodness of all under Heaven. Goodness originates in human nature: although there is a distinction between others and oneself, there is in fact no separation between their goodness and one’s own. Only when the sense of self predominates does one see oneself and fail to see others. Consequently, the goodness in others remains confined to them, with no means of being shared with oneself; the goodness in oneself …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
止於已而無以及於人無與於已則善猶在人
也無及於人則善猶在我也人已分而善始小
矣聖人之善本足於已初無待於取之天下也
天下之善各足於身初無待於聖人之取之也
然而聖人見人之善則不知在人而取之於我
人見聖人之取善則知善之在我而咸為之勸
是聖人不以有我間之而合天下以成其善善
之所以為大歟噫此孟子即舜之與人為善而
著其大其示人以盡性之極乎今夫天生人而
===
賦之性純粹以精莫不各有本然之理也人之
生也而各一其性無少駁雜莫不全其固有之
良也率吾之性循吾之良而善在我矣何待於
取人何利於人之取我亦何必無間於人已而
後大也蓋善之在人雖人之所同有然惟聖人
能全之而衆人不能使無聖人以勸之則天下
終無以歸於善而聖人之善亦於是乎小矣是
故善也者衆人有之而未能全君子全之而未
能大聖人則合天下而大焉者也是非有所加
punctuated: 止於已而無以及於人。無與於已，則善猶在人也；無及於人，則善猶在我也。人已分而善始小矣。聖人之善本足於已，初無待於取之天下也；天下之善各足於身，初無待於聖人之取之也。然而聖人見人之善，則不知在人而取之於我；人見聖人之取善，則知善之在我而咸為之勸。是聖人不以有我間之，而合天下以成其善，善之所以為大歟！噫！此孟子即舜之與人為善而著其大，其示人以盡性之極乎！今夫天生人而賦之性，純粹以精，莫不各有本然之理也。人之生也，而各一其性，無少駁雜，莫不全其固有之良也。率吾之性，循吾之良，而善在我矣。何待於取人？何利於人之取我？亦何必無間於人已而後大也？蓋善之在人，雖人之所同有，然惟聖人能全之，而衆人不能。使無聖人以勸之，則天下終無以歸於善，而聖人之善亦於是乎小矣。是故善也者，衆人有之而未能全，君子全之而未能大，聖人則合天下而大焉者也。是非有所加
translation_en:
…remains confined to oneself and cannot reach others. If it contributes nothing to oneself, goodness still remains with others; if it does not reach others, goodness still remains with oneself. Once others and self are divided, goodness becomes small. The sage’s goodness is inherently sufficient within himself; from the outset, it does not depend on his drawing upon the goodness of all under Heaven. The goodness of people throughout the world is sufficient within each person; from the outset, it does not depend on the sage’s drawing upon it. Yet when the sage sees goodness in others, he takes it into himself without regarding it as belonging to others. When people see the sage drawing upon goodness, they recognize the goodness within themselves and are all encouraged by this. Thus the sage does not let a sense of self create a division, but brings together all under Heaven to fulfill his goodness. Is this not how goodness becomes great? Ah! In explaining the greatness of Shun’s joining with others in doing good, was Mengzi not showing people the ultimate fulfillment of their nature?

Now, Heaven gives birth to people and endows them with a nature, pure and refined; each possesses its inherent principles. At birth, each person’s nature is undivided, without the slightest admixture, and each possesses innate goodness in its entirety. By following my nature and abiding by my innate goodness, I have goodness within myself. Why need I draw upon others? What benefit is there in others drawing upon me? And why must there be no division between others and self before goodness can become great? Although goodness is something all people possess alike, only the sage can fully realize it; ordinary people cannot. If there were no sage to encourage them, all under Heaven would ultimately have no means of turning toward goodness, and the sage’s goodness would thereby also become small. Thus ordinary people possess goodness but cannot fully realize it; the gentleman fully realizes it but cannot make it great; the sage brings together all under Heaven and thereby makes it great. This does not mean that anything is added…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
也蓋善之在人本自大也蘊之爲德則五性具
焉所以立天下之有者此也措之爲行則衆妙
出焉所以一天下之動者此也發之於事業則
功化昭焉所以畢天下之能事者此也理雖具
於一心而道則極於天下苟於其本大者而挾
之以有我之私見已之善而不知公於天下見
天下之善而不知公於在我岐物我而爲二則
善雖有於已而不及於人善雖有於天下而不
與於已既無以會體用之全亦何以語盡性之
極哉是故聖人者視天下之人惟我而視我惟
===
天下之人善言善行感而遂通焉好問好察用
中於民焉固不見其善之在已在人也然而天
下之人見聖人之取其善也則知聖人之所欲
者在是吾性之所具者在是即其善而益自勵
焉則吾之所取者人之善也人之被勸者亦我
之善也分殊也而機則相通迹異也而理則一
致孰知天下之善爲聖人之善聖人之善爲天
下之善乎善而至是則勸者既多而告者益廣
punctuated: 也。蓋善之在人，本自大也。蘊之爲德，則五性具焉，所以立天下之有者，此也；措之爲行，則衆妙出焉，所以一天下之動者，此也；發之於事業，則功化昭焉，所以畢天下之能事者，此也。理雖具於一心，而道則極於天下。苟於其本大者，而挾之以有我之私，見已之善而不知公於天下，見天下之善而不知公於在我，岐物我而爲二，則善雖有於已而不及於人，善雖有於天下而不與於已。既無以會體用之全，亦何以語盡性之極哉？是故聖人者，視天下之人惟我，而視我惟天下之人。善言善行，感而遂通焉；好問好察，用中於民焉。固不見其善之在已在人也。然而天下之人見聖人之取其善也，則知聖人之所欲者在是，吾性之所具者在是，即其善而益自勵焉。則吾之所取者，人之善也；人之被勸者，亦我之善也。分殊也，而機則相通；迹異也，而理則一致。孰知天下之善爲聖人之善，聖人之善爲天下之善乎？善而至是，則勸者既多，而告者益廣。
translation_en: … For goodness in human beings is inherently great. Stored within as virtue, it comprises the five moral qualities: this is what establishes all that exists under Heaven. Put into practice as conduct, it gives rise to manifold wondrous workings: this is what unifies all movement under Heaven. Manifested in undertakings, it makes achievements and transforming influence evident: this is what brings to completion all that can be accomplished under Heaven. Although principle is fully present within a single mind, the Way extends throughout all under Heaven. If one confines what is inherently great within the selfishness of possessing an individual self, seeing one’s own goodness without knowing to share it impartially with all under Heaven, and seeing the goodness of all under Heaven without knowing to share in it oneself, one splits things and self into two. Then, though goodness exists in oneself, it does not reach others; though goodness exists throughout all under Heaven, one has no part in it. Unable to unite substance and function in their entirety, how could one speak of the utmost fulfillment of one’s nature? Thus the sage regards all people under Heaven as himself, and himself as all people under Heaven. In response to good words and good deeds, he immediately enters into communion with them; delighting in inquiry and scrutiny, he applies the mean among the people. He makes no distinction between goodness residing in himself and in others. Yet when people under Heaven see the sage adopting their goodness, they recognize that this is what the sage desires and what their own nature possesses. Through that goodness, they encourage themselves to still greater effort. Thus what I adopt is the goodness of others, while the goodness in which others are encouraged is also my own. Their respective positions differ, but the moving impulse passes between them; their outward manifestations differ, but their principle is one. Who recognizes that the goodness of all under Heaven is the sage’s goodness, and that the sage’s goodness is the goodness of all under Heaven? When goodness reaches this point, those encouraged are already many, and those who offer him counsel become ever more numerous…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
無間而心無不虛也無在而善無不取也無所
喜而人無不告也無所拜而言無不聞也其取
善也固無窮矣然而底豫於親讓畔於耕善公
於家於鄉者可徵也百工熙熙四門穆穆善公
於國者可徵也萬邦協和黎民敏德善公於天
下者可徵也其與人爲善又豈有窮已乎是其
始也以天下之善而萃之於一人終也以一人
之善而達之天下大哉舜乎所以合天下而成
其大也雖然聖人萬理咸備固非必取足於天
===
下而天下之善固非有過於聖人而取之也蓋
天下之理無窮善無微而可忽是故不能已其
取善之心而况性者萬物之一源人性之未盡
已性之有歉也又豈能已其勸善之心乎嗣是
而後有不自滿假者焉有用人惟已者焉有好
問則裕者焉皆是道也故曰聖人通天下爲一
身又曰聖人同乎人而無我斯之謂矣
表
擬宋以歐陽脩參知政事謝表〔嘉祐六年〕
punctuated:
無間而心無不虛也，無在而善無不取也，無所喜而人無不告也，無所拜而言無不聞也。其取善也固無窮矣。然而底豫於親，讓畔於耕，善公於家於鄉者可徵也；百工熙熙，四門穆穆，善公於國者可徵也；萬邦協和，黎民敏德，善公於天下者可徵也。其與人爲善，又豈有窮已乎？是其始也，以天下之善而萃之於一人；終也，以一人之善而達之天下。大哉舜乎！所以合天下而成其大也。雖然，聖人萬理咸備，固非必取足於天下，而天下之善固非有過於聖人而取之也。蓋天下之理無窮，善無微而可忽，是故不能已其取善之心。而况性者萬物之一源，人性之未盡，已性之有歉也，又豈能已其勸善之心乎？嗣是而後，有不自滿假者焉，有用人惟已者焉，有好問則裕者焉，皆是道也。故曰：「聖人通天下爲一身。」又曰：「聖人同乎人而無我。」斯之謂矣。

表

擬宋以歐陽脩參知政事謝表〔嘉祐六年〕
translation_en:
…At every moment his mind remains receptive; wherever goodness is found, he adopts it. He confines his delight to no particular object, and everyone offers him counsel; he confines his reverence to no particular object, and no counsel goes unheard. His adoption of goodness is indeed inexhaustible. Yet there is evidence that goodness was shared within his family and community: he brought his parents to contentment, and cultivators yielded their field boundaries to one another. There is evidence that goodness was shared throughout the state: the many officials flourished in their work, and solemn harmony prevailed at the four gates. There is evidence that goodness was shared throughout the world: the myriad states lived in concord, and the common people applied themselves diligently to virtue. How, then, could his helping others to do good ever have an end?

Thus, at the outset, he gathered the goodness of the world into one person; in the end, he extended the goodness of one person throughout the world. Great indeed was Shun! He achieved his greatness by uniting the whole world. Nevertheless, the sage possesses all principles in their completeness: he certainly need not depend upon the world to supply what he lacks. Nor does he adopt the goodness of the world because it surpasses his own. Rather, the principles of the world are inexhaustible, and no goodness is so slight that it may be disregarded. Hence he cannot cease wishing to adopt goodness. Moreover, human nature is the single source shared by all things. If the nature of others has not been fully realized, his own nature remains deficient. How, then, could he cease wishing to encourage goodness?

Among those who followed him were those who did not consider themselves fully accomplished, those who employed others as though they were themselves, and those who attained abundance through a fondness for asking questions. All followed this Way. Thus it is said: “The sage regards the whole world as one body.” It is also said: “The sage is at one with others and has no self.” This is what these sayings mean.

Memorial

A model memorial of thanks on Ouyang Xiu’s appointment as Assistant Administrator under the Song dynasty. 〔Sixth year of Jiayou [1061].〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
貫選
同考試官教諭李　批〔說參知政事處無一語蹈〕
〔襲優於衆作錄之〕
同考試官教諭胡　批〔同心輔政最妙且引用俱〕
〔當時實事華而不浮其學歐而有得者乎〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔麗而有則〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔典雅〕
===
嘉祐六年　月　日伏蒙
聖恩命臣　爲參知政事者臣班聯
紫府與參密勿之謀身上
彤闈式佐台衡之寄禮實隆於異數
恩仰荷於曲成聞
命增慚循牆知懼臣脩　誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上
言伏以平章爲時之膴仕宜集衆思參政
乃
國之大臣實資忠益故軒轅首命乎六相而
堯舜徧宅乎百揆蒼姬綿有道之長貳公
弘化東郊得人之盛三后協心漢置御
punctuated:
貫選。
同考試官教諭李批〔說參知政事處，無一語蹈〕〔襲，優於衆作，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭胡批〔同心輔政最妙，且引用俱〕〔當時實事，華而不浮，其學歐而有得者乎！〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔麗而有則。〕
考試官教諭曲批〔典雅。〕
===
嘉祐六年，月，日，伏蒙聖恩，命臣爲參知政事者。臣班聯紫府，與參密勿之謀；身上彤闈，式佐台衡之寄。禮實隆於異數，恩仰荷於曲成。聞命增慚，循牆知懼。臣脩誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：伏以平章爲時之膴仕，宜集衆思；參政乃國之大臣，實資忠益。故軒轅首命乎六相，而堯舜徧宅乎百揆。蒼姬綿有道之長，貳公弘化；東郊得人之盛，三后協心。漢置御
translation_en:
Selected across the classics groups [?].
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “In its treatment of the office of Vice Grand Councilor, not a single phrase imitates earlier writing. Superior to the other compositions; include it.”
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The treatment of assisting government with a united purpose is particularly fine. Moreover, all the allusions concern actual events of the period. Ornate without being insubstantial—surely this writer has learned something from studying Ouyang!”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Elegant and conforming to proper standards.”
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and refined.”
===
On the [unspecified] day of the [unspecified] month in the sixth year of Jiayou, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious command appointing me Vice Grand Councilor. My rank now places me among those of the Purple Palace, participating in its confidential deliberations; I ascend the vermilion palace gates to assist those entrusted with the chief ministership. The ceremonial honor is indeed exalted through this exceptional distinction; I gratefully receive the favor that has fostered me in every way. Hearing the command, I feel still greater shame; keeping close to the wall in deference, I know fear. Your servant Xiu, in utmost apprehension and dread, bows his head to the ground, repeatedly kowtows, and submits these words:
I humbly consider that the grand councilorship is an eminent office of our age, whose holder should bring together the thoughts of many; the Vice Grand Councilor is a great minister of the state, on whose loyalty and beneficial counsel the state truly depends. Thus Xuanyuan first appointed six ministers, while Yao and Shun filled the full range of official posts. The Ji house of Zhou long sustained its virtuous rule, with two dukes extending its transforming influence; when worthy men abounded in the eastern suburbs, three ministers worked with one mind. The Han established the office of Censor…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
史大夫戒重權於獨用唐列中書門下主
衆務於分曹天啓
皇圖堂開政事輪班知印用以佐鼎實而總
朝綱書
敕齊銜行得賛
國鈞而陪
廟論共謀可以底績臻道揆法守之良斷金
本於同心運謨明弼諧之化職思稽往牒
之善官階居次相之榮苟非其人實難斯
===
任故呂餘慶猶須於慎擇雖薛居正不易
其名稱齒伍上公以實備之人之介設軏
別殿見當正之量之宏引對彰賢剛方表
績顧迂拙獨慚於前輩誤
寵光比及於匪人雖自慶其遭逢實無由於酬
荅茲蓋伏遇
如天之仁根於成性
好生之德洽於民心
punctuated:
史大夫，戒重權於獨用；唐列中書門下，主衆務於分曹。天啓皇圖，堂開政事。輪班知印，用以佐鼎實而總朝綱；書敕齊銜，行得賛國鈞而陪廟論。共謀可以底績，臻道揆法守之良；斷金本於同心，運謨明弼諧之化。職思稽往牒之善，官階居次相之榮。苟非其人，實難斯任。故呂餘慶猶須於慎擇，雖薛居正不易其名。稱齒伍上公，以實備之人之介；設軏別殿，見當正之量之宏。引對彰賢，剛方表績。顧迂拙獨慚於前輩，誤寵光比及於匪人。雖自慶其遭逢，實無由於酬荅。
茲蓋伏遇如天之仁根於成性，好生之德洽於民心。
translation_en:
…the Censor-in-Chief, guarding against the concentration of great power in a single person; the Tang established the Secretariat and Chancellery, dividing responsibility for the many affairs of government among separate offices. Heaven inaugurated the imperial enterprise, and the Hall of Government Affairs was opened. Taking turns in charge of the seal, they assisted in harmonizing the contents of the tripod—that is, governing the realm—and oversaw the guiding principles of court administration. Inscribing their titles together on imperial decrees, they helped direct the state and participated in deliberations at court. Joint planning could bring achievements, attaining excellence both in determining principles and in observing established rules. The strength to cut through metal rests upon unity of purpose; through planning and deliberation, they manifested the transforming influence of harmonious assistance. The duties of the office follow the good precedents recorded in earlier annals; its rank carries the honor of the vice-chief councillorship. Unless the right person is found, this responsibility is indeed difficult to discharge. Thus even Lü Yuqing required careful selection, and even for Xue Juzheng the designation was not changed. Ranked alongside the highest dignitaries, one supplies a person of integrity [?]; provision in a separate palace hall reveals the breadth of the measure appropriate to rectitude [?]. Summoned to imperial audience, their worthiness was made manifest; firmness and uprightness distinguished their achievements. Yet I, impractical and inept, can only feel ashamed before my predecessors: through a mistaken bestowal, the radiance of imperial favor has reached an unworthy person. Although I rejoice in my good fortune, I truly have no means of repaying it.
This is surely because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose Heaven-like benevolence is rooted in your innate nature, and whose virtue of cherishing life permeates the hearts of the people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
澤溥氾以無私
道合弘而益裕
萬幾總理四海乂安謂臺閣之深嚴本圖協贊
以樞機之繁劇要在象閒非亟以資兼聽
並觀之明蓋欲以成大道爲公之治俾令
承乏偶爾缺員貳政非才自合奉身而退
分符要地將貽持祿之譏矧當韓琦富弼
之才諒無庸於借聽正際
上恬下熙之盛恐莫裨於賛襄辭避未能顛迷
===
無措人以爲寵者臣以爲憂世之所榮者
臣之所懼竊念臣粗知章句罔識時宜昔
主聖頃裁文體肯恤人言諫院久塵奚補
讓移書幸承
衮之足賴詞林虛辱實華
國之未能茲復
甄拔之隆益矢涓埃之報苟曲學而違初志
亦何顏以見古人事出
廟堂共圖畫一之守計關民社相期謀斷之
punctuated: 澤溥氾以無私，道合弘而益裕。萬幾總理，四海乂安。謂臺閣之深嚴，本圖協贊；以樞機之繁劇，要在象閒。非亟以資兼聽並觀之明，蓋欲以成大道爲公之治。俾令承乏，偶爾缺員。貳政非才，自合奉身而退；分符要地，將貽持祿之譏。矧當韓琦、富弼之才，諒無庸於借聽；正際上恬下熙之盛，恐莫裨於賛襄。辭避未能，顛迷無措。人以爲寵者，臣以爲憂；世之所榮者，臣之所懼。竊念臣粗知章句，罔識時宜。昔主聖頃裁文體，肯恤人言，諫院久塵，奚補讓移書？幸承衮之足賴，詞林虛辱，實華國之未能。茲復甄拔之隆，益矢涓埃之報。苟曲學而違初志，亦何顏以見古人？事出廟堂，共圖畫一之守；計關民社，相期謀斷之
translation_en:
…Your beneficence spreads far and wide without partiality; your Way accords with breadth and grows ever more ample. You direct the myriad affairs of government, and all within the Four Seas enjoys peace. You hold that the solemn, secluded offices of central government were established to provide collaborative assistance, and that the complexity and urgency of pivotal affairs require composure [?]. Your purpose is not merely to gain the clarity that comes from hearing all sides and viewing matters together, but to achieve a government in which the Great Way serves the common good. You have thus allowed me to fill a vacancy when a post happened to fall vacant. Lacking the ability to assist in government, I ought properly to withdraw from office; entrusted with the tally of authority in an important locality, I shall invite criticism for merely clinging to my stipend. Moreover, with men of the talents of Han Qi and Fu Bi serving, there can surely be no need to borrow my counsel. At this flourishing time, when those above are tranquil and those below prosper, I fear I can contribute nothing by way of assistance. Unable to decline, I am bewildered and at a loss. What others regard as favor, your servant regards as anxiety; what the world considers glory, your servant fears.
I humbly reflect that I possess only a rough knowledge of textual interpretation and do not understand what the times require. Formerly, under a sage ruler, literary style was recently regulated, with regard for what people said [?]. I long encumbered the Remonstrance Bureau; what benefit did I bring through admonitory correspondence [?]? Fortunately, I received support from the imperial robes [?]. I undeservedly occupied a place in the literary academy, yet was truly unable to bring literary distinction to the state. Now, once again receiving this great favor of selection and advancement, I pledge all the more to repay it with whatever tiny contribution I can make. If I should distort my learning and betray my original aspirations, with what face could I meet the ancients? In affairs proceeding from the court, we shall together seek to uphold uniform governance; in plans concerning the people and their local communities, we shall expect of one another the capacity for planning and decision…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
資居攝總於元勳豈敢懷召公之弗悅阿
衡恊於一德惟知效仲虺之胥匡此惟
國是之能諧庶亦臣心之少遂也伏願
體乾健坤厚之誠
德旣聖而益聖
保豐亨豫大之業
治已隆而愈隆
壽祚延於無疆民生康於有永臣無任瞻
天仰
===
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
孫文登
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔敷對〕
punctuated:
資。居攝總於元勳，豈敢懷召公之弗悅？阿衡恊於一德，惟知效仲虺之胥匡。此惟國是之能諧，庶亦臣心之少遂也。伏願體乾健坤厚之誠，德旣聖而益聖；保豐亨豫大之業，治已隆而愈隆。壽祚延於無疆，民生康於有永。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
孫文登
同考試官教諭鄭批〔敷對〕
translation_en:
…the capacity to plan and decide. With the regency entrusted to a foremost meritorious minister, how could I dare harbor the Duke of Shao’s displeasure? As A-heng harmonized all through a single virtue, I know only to emulate Zhong Hui in mutual correction and support. Thus may agreement on the proper course of state affairs be achieved, and perhaps my own aspirations may also find some small fulfillment. I humbly pray that Your Majesty embody the sincerity of Heaven’s vigor and Earth’s generosity, becoming ever more sagely in virtue; preserve the enterprise of abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness, bringing an already flourishing government to still greater flourishing. May your longevity and sovereign blessings extend without limit, and may the people’s lives enjoy peace forever. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sagely Majesty, your servant is overcome with intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖製難於詳整了能一一條答詞意莊肅且復仰窺
制作之本凡占所養矣豈亦涵泳
聖化而有得者歟
考試官教諭鄭　批〔聞見該博筆力雄健錄之〕
以式多士
考試官教諭曲　批〔明悉可錄〕
文之爲用大矣聖人用之以化成天下也
則爲經世之文焉用之以傳授心法也則
爲道統之文焉夫文一而已而其用則殊
惟於其所謂一者而有得焉由是存之則
爲心學發之則爲事業自其心學者出之
而道以明夫是之謂教天下之文道統之
傳是也自其事業者昭之而道以行夫是
之謂治天下之文經綸之迹是也治教雖
異致而必本於道然後謂之文否則惟於
其用之殊者徒得其似而未聞乎本之一
焉以是而謂之文吾見其用亦小矣未敢
以爲與於斯文也鴻濛之初人文之理雖
punctuated:
聖製難於詳整，了能一一條答，詞意莊肅，且復仰窺制作之本，凡占所養矣，豈亦涵泳聖化而有得者歟？
考試官教諭鄭，批〔聞見該博，筆力雄健，錄之〕以式多士。
考試官教諭曲，批〔明悉可錄〕。
文之爲用大矣！聖人用之以化成天下也，則爲經世之文焉；用之以傳授心法也，則爲道統之文焉。夫文一而已，而其用則殊。惟於其所謂一者而有得焉，由是存之則爲心學，發之則爲事業。自其心學者出之，而道以明，夫是之謂教天下之文，道統之傳是也；自其事業者昭之，而道以行，夫是之謂治天下之文，經綸之迹是也。治教雖異致，而必本於道，然後謂之文。否則，惟於其用之殊者徒得其似，而未聞乎本之一焉，以是而謂之文，吾見其用亦小矣，未敢以爲與於斯文也。鴻濛之初，人文之理雖
translation_en:
…Imperial compositions are difficult to treat comprehensively and coherently, yet [?] he has answered each point in turn. His language and meaning are dignified and solemn; moreover, he reverently probes the foundations of imperial authorship, revealing his cultivated attainments [?]. Might he, too, have gained understanding through immersion in the transforming influence of the sage emperor?
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔“His knowledge is comprehensive, and his writing vigorous. Select this answer”〕 to serve as a model for the assembled candidates.
Examiner Qu, an Instructor, comments: 〔“Clear and thorough; worthy of selection.”〕
Great indeed is the usefulness of wen—writing and cultural expression! When the sage uses it to transform and perfect all under Heaven, it becomes writing for ordering the world; when he uses it to transmit the essential teachings of the mind, it becomes writing that carries the succession of the Way. Wen is but one, yet its uses differ. Only by grasping what constitutes this unity can one preserve it within as learning of the mind and express it outwardly in practical achievements. When it issues from learning of the mind and thereby illuminates the Way, this is what is called writing that instructs all under Heaven: the transmission of the succession of the Way. When it is manifested through practical achievements and thereby puts the Way into practice, this is what is called writing that governs all under Heaven: the traces of ordering the world. Though governing and teaching have different ends, they must be rooted in the Way before they can be called wen. Otherwise, one merely acquires a semblance of its different applications, without understanding the unity of its foundation. If this is called wen, I consider its usefulness slight indeed, and would not venture to count it as participating in this cultural tradition. At the beginning of primordial chaos, although the principles of human culture…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
具而隱於無自河圖洛書肇開萬古之秘
而天下之文始燦然矣然其理則不外乎
圖書之所謂極也堯舜禹湯文武以是相
傳以成二帝三王之治而典謨訓誥於是
乎出蓋嘗讀其書而於所謂精一執中祗
台敬翼之傳者有以見心學之文焉又於
所謂昭明於變誕敷章信怙冒永清之治
者有以見治功之文焉然非有意於文者
也而萬世之文莫加焉道在此而文自不
===
能外也降而漢唐宋之君於斯道之極槩
乎其未有聞矣雖有漢孝武之號令文章
煥然可述唐太宗之爲文賦詩贍麗冲邁
宋太宗之援翰屬思極其精妙若可稱矣
然內多欲者而治以虛耗尚功名者而不
及禮樂機深事隱而徒以崇儒幸學爲文
所謂帝王之文巍然煥然之本固已無矣
區區辭藝之末雖有可稱於治理何關也
洪惟我
punctuated:
具而隱於無，自河圖洛書肇開萬古之秘，而天下之文始燦然矣。然其理則不外乎圖書之所謂極也。堯舜禹湯文武以是相傳，以成二帝三王之治，而典謨訓誥於是乎出。蓋嘗讀其書，而於所謂精一執中、祗台敬翼之傳者，有以見心學之文焉；又於所謂昭明於變、誕敷章信、怙冒永清之治者，有以見治功之文焉。然非有意於文者也，而萬世之文莫加焉。道在此，而文自不能外也。
降而漢唐宋之君，於斯道之極，槩乎其未有聞矣。雖有漢孝武之號令文章，煥然可述；唐太宗之爲文賦詩，贍麗冲邁；宋太宗之援翰屬思，極其精妙，若可稱矣。然內多欲者而治以虛耗，尚功名者而不及禮樂，機深事隱而徒以崇儒幸學爲文，所謂帝王之文巍然煥然之本，固已無矣。區區辭藝之末，雖有可稱，於治理何關也？
洪惟我
translation_en:
…was present, yet lay concealed in the unmanifest. Only when the River Chart and the Luo Writing first disclosed the secrets of all antiquity did the cultural patterns of the world begin to shine forth. Yet their underlying principle extends no further than the supreme standard expressed in that Chart and Writing. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu transmitted this to one another, thereby achieving the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; from this arose the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements. In reading their writings, one can discern the cultural expression of the learning of the mind in such transmitted teachings as being discerning and single-minded, holding fast to the mean, and being reverent and watchful [?]. Likewise, in their government—making virtue illustrious and transforming the people, broadly disseminating instruction and manifesting trustworthiness, protecting and sheltering the people and securing enduring peace—one can discern the cultural expression of achievements in governance. Yet they did not deliberately seek cultural brilliance, and the cultural achievements of all subsequent ages could not surpass theirs. The Way resides here, and cultural expression naturally cannot fall outside it.
Coming down to the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, they seem never to have heard of the supreme standard of this Way. Emperor Xiaowu of Han issued commands and writings whose brilliance deserves recounting; Emperor Taizong of Tang composed prose and poetry of rich beauty and lofty spirit; Emperor Taizong of Song took up the brush and marshalled his thoughts with consummate refinement. These might seem worthy of praise. Yet the ruler whose inner desires were many brought depletion and exhaustion through his government; the ruler who prized achievement and fame fell short in rites and music; and the ruler whose calculations were deep and whose dealings were concealed merely treated honoring Confucian scholars and visiting the imperial school as cultural accomplishment. The foundation of what is called the lofty and resplendent culture of emperors and kings was already absent. Though their trifling accomplishments in literary skill may deserve praise, what bearing do they have on good government?
In reverent contemplation of our…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸經綸海隅肇造區宇而
開創於前
成祖文皇帝光臨璿極脩輯六經丕承鴻緒而
繼統於後
聖神相繼遂能驅逐夷狄開蕩函夏
弘宣文教再覩太平自古帝王之土宇已淪
而廓清萬世生民之綱常既絕而復續自
其心之所存者言之則
帝王之盛德也自其功之所及者言之則
===
帝王之大業也是以
製作之文經天緯地而渾噩之體襲典參盤蓋
二祖之心卽堯舜禹湯文武之心故其治卽二
帝三王之治而欲其言之不典謨訓誥不
可得也是故以言乎勸戒臣民綱維治理
也則有
大誥三編爲條二百有四以華風淪没彝斁
傾頹私勝公微多致愆罪而作也有
資世通訓爲章凡十有四總先賢之論託
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸，經綸海隅，肇造區宇而開創於前；成祖文皇帝光臨璿極，脩輯六經，丕承鴻緒而繼統於後。聖神相繼，遂能驅逐夷狄，開蕩函夏，弘宣文教，再覩太平。自古帝王之土宇已淪而廓清，萬世生民之綱常既絕而復續。自其心之所存者言之，則帝王之盛德也；自其功之所及者言之，則帝王之大業也。是以製作之文，經天緯地，而渾噩之體襲典參盤。蓋二祖之心卽堯舜禹湯文武之心，故其治卽二帝三王之治，而欲其言之不典謨訓誥，不可得也。
是故以言乎勸戒臣民、綱維治理也，則有《大誥》三編，爲條二百有四，以華風淪没、彝斁傾頹、私勝公微、多致愆罪而作也。有《資世通訓》，爲章凡十有四，總先賢之論，託
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, rose like a dragon in the Huai region, brought order to the farthest reaches of the realm, and established the empire, first laying its foundations. Chengzu, the Wen Emperor, gloriously ascended the imperial throne, revised and compiled the Six Classics, and magnificently carried forward the great inheritance, succeeding to the imperial line. These sagely and divinely gifted rulers followed one another, and thus were able to expel the barbarians, clear the Chinese realm, widely propagate literary and moral instruction, and witness great peace once again. The territory of the emperors and kings of antiquity, once fallen into alien hands, was cleared and restored; the cardinal relationships and constant moral norms of the people for all ages, once severed, were renewed. Viewed in terms of what they cherished in their hearts, this was the abundant virtue of emperors and kings; viewed in terms of the reach of their achievements, it was the great enterprise of emperors and kings. Thus their writings gave order to Heaven and Earth, while their style, in its primal simplicity, followed the Canons and stood alongside the “Pan Geng” chapters of the Book of Documents. For the hearts of the two imperial ancestors were the very hearts of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Their government was therefore the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; it was impossible that their words should fail to embody the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of antiquity.
Thus, as regards exhorting and admonishing officials and commoners and upholding orderly government, there are the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), comprising 204 articles. These were written because Chinese customs had fallen into decline, enduring moral norms had become corrupted and collapsed, private interests prevailed while public duty waned, and transgressions and crimes frequently resulted. There is also the Comprehensive Instruction to Aid the World (Zishi Tongxun), comprising fourteen chapters, which gathers the arguments of earlier worthies and entrusts…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
謞者之評以世人性愚見淺而作也二書
皆托始於
君臣五常要終於頒行禍福救世之心切矣以
言乎察於敬忽明於災祥也則有
精誠之錄焉上采六經旁稽傳記其所載則
敬
天也忠
君也孝
親也有
===
存心省躬二錄焉一則舉自古帝王徵驗之
迹一則惟以漢唐宋臣下而言其所言皆
祭祀災祥之事禍福感應之機也而
精誠之一心
存省之一誠愼修之旨微矣皆我
太祖之文也若夫至德要道存乎孝而孝者萬
善之本也故與人爲善也則舉卓然可述
者二百有七人而作
孝順事實之書以虞舜大孝爲首又采傳記
punctuated:
謞者之評，以世人性愚見淺而作也。二書皆托始於君臣、五常，要終於頒行禍福，救世之心切矣。以言乎察於敬忽、明於災祥也，則有《精誠》之錄焉，上采六經，旁稽傳記，其所載則敬天也，忠君也，孝親也。有《存心》《省躬》二錄焉，一則舉自古帝王徵驗之迹，一則惟以漢唐宋臣下而言，其所言皆祭祀災祥之事、禍福感應之機也。而《精誠》之一心、《存》《省》之一誠，愼修之旨微矣。皆我太祖之文也。
若夫至德要道存乎孝，而孝者萬善之本也。故與人爲善也，則舉卓然可述者二百有七人，而作《孝順事實》之書，以虞舜大孝爲首，又采傳記
translation_en:
…the judgments of critics [?], composed because people were foolish in disposition and shallow in understanding. Both books begin with the relationship between ruler and minister and the Five Constant Virtues, and culminate in the dispensation of misfortune and blessing: their concern to save the world is urgent indeed. As for discerning reverence and negligence and understanding calamities and auspicious signs, there is the Record of Perfect Sincerity (Jingcheng). It draws upon the Six Classics and consults transmitted accounts; what it records concerns reverence for Heaven, loyalty to the ruler, and filial devotion to parents. There are also the two records, Preserving the Mind (Cunxin) and Examining Oneself (Xinggong). One adduces instances of verified consequences concerning emperors and kings from antiquity onward; the other speaks exclusively of subjects serving under the Han, Tang, and Song. Both discuss sacrifices, calamities and auspicious signs, and the workings of stimulus and response that bring misfortune and blessing. The single-mindedness of Perfect Sincerity and the undivided sincerity of Preserving the Mind and Examining Oneself convey a subtle teaching of conscientious self-cultivation. These are all writings of our Taizu.
As for consummate virtue and the essential Way, they reside in filial piety, and filial piety is the root of all goodness. Thus, to encourage others in goodness, he selected 207 people whose outstanding conduct merited recounting and compiled the book True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), beginning with the great filial piety of Yu Shun. He also drew upon transmitted accounts…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
得百六十有五人作
爲善陰隲之書而以蔣王靈應爲首二書體
天地之撰而皆以匹婦之事終之正
制序所謂一念之善通乎
神明抑推天而驗之人言人而徵諸天者耶
眞得勸世勵俗之道矣千聖萬古妙於心
而性者心之所自出也故
存心養性也則采古聖賢嘉言而作
聖學心法以
===
君父子臣釐爲四卷而揭其綱又統言專言分
爲三十一條而詳其目輯先儒成書及論
議格言而作
性理大全以周張邵朱二蔡六儒之撰列於
先以理氣鬼神性理道統論學諸子歷代
君道治道詩文十類之說序於後二書盡
天下之道而獨以心性之名
命之正
制序所謂萬事必根於心而學之至則可以爲
punctuated:
得百六十有五人，作《爲善陰隲》之書，而以蔣王靈應爲首。二書體天地之撰，而皆以匹婦之事終之，正制序所謂「一念之善通乎神明」，抑推天而驗之人，言人而徵諸天者耶？眞得勸世勵俗之道矣！千聖萬古，妙於心，而性者，心之所自出也。
故存心養性也，則采古聖賢嘉言而作《聖學心法》，以君、父、子、臣釐爲四卷而揭其綱，又統言、專言分爲三十一條而詳其目。輯先儒成書及論議格言而作《性理大全》，以周、張、邵、朱、二蔡六儒之撰列於先，以理氣、鬼神、性理、道統、論學、諸子、歷代、君道、治道、詩文十類之說序於後。二書盡天下之道，而獨以心性之名命之，正制序所謂「萬事必根於心，而學之至則可以爲
translation_en:
…found one hundred and sixty-five people and compiled Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan yinzhi), placing the account of King Jiang’s miraculous responses first. These two books embody the workings of Heaven and Earth, yet both conclude with the deeds of an ordinary woman. This is precisely what the imperial preface means by “A single good thought communicates with the spirits.” Might they also reason from Heaven and find verification in human affairs, and speak of human affairs and find corroboration in Heaven? They truly grasp the way to encourage the world toward goodness and improve its customs! For the myriad sages throughout the ages, the subtle essence lies in the mind; and human nature is that from which the mind originates.
Thus, for preserving the mind and nurturing human nature, admirable sayings of ancient sages and worthies were gathered to compile The Essential Method of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). Its guiding framework was set out in four volumes, organized under ruler, father, son, and minister; its particulars were further elaborated in thirty-one sections of general and specific discussion. Completed works, discussions, and maxims of earlier Confucian scholars were collected to compile The Great Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan). Works by the six Confucian scholars Zhou, Zhang, Shao, Zhu, and the two Cais were placed first. These were followed by discussions arranged in ten categories: principle and material force; ghosts and spirits; human nature and principle; the transmission of the Way; discussions of learning; the various masters; successive dynasties; the way of the ruler; the way of governance; and poetry and prose. These two books encompass the Way in its entirety, yet their titles invoke only mind and human nature. This is precisely what the imperial preface means by “All affairs must be rooted in the mind, and when learning reaches its utmost, one can become …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人學不至於聖人則不足謂之學者也
眞得脩身立教之道矣皆我
成祖之文也肆天下家傳人誦寡過而歸極迴
心而鄉道淳風翔洽聲教宣流天下
泰和者垂百七十餘年於玆矣乃我
皇上聰明神聖應運
中興以
天縱之資
纘溥將之緒
===
秉禮樂之期
操制作之柄恢弘
聖猷大新物覩
稽古禮文之事蔚乎盛矣乃又發爲文章以光
宇宙首制
明倫大典一書推明統嗣之不同詳論義情之
兼盡立人極而光
聖孝所以定萬世之綱常也
敬一之箴五箴之註致謹於言行樞機之初益
punctuated:
聖人，學不至於聖人，則不足謂之學者也。」眞得脩身立教之道矣，皆我成祖之文也。肆天下家傳人誦，寡過而歸極，迴心而鄉道，淳風翔洽，聲教宣流，天下泰和者垂百七十餘年於玆矣。
乃我皇上聰明神聖，應運中興，以天縱之資，纘溥將之緒，秉禮樂之期，操制作之柄，恢弘聖猷，大新物覩，稽古禮文之事蔚乎盛矣。乃又發爲文章，以光宇宙。首制《明倫大典》一書，推明統嗣之不同，詳論義情之兼盡，立人極而光聖孝，所以定萬世之綱常也。《敬一》之箴、五箴之註，致謹於言行樞機之初，益
translation_en:
…a sage.
