If learning does not bring one to sagehood, it is insufficient to be called learning.” These writings truly grasp the way of cultivating oneself and establishing moral instruction; all are the writings of our Chengzu. Thus, throughout the realm, every household transmitted them and every person recited them. People diminished their faults and returned to the ultimate standard, turned their hearts and directed themselves toward the Way. Pure customs spread everywhere, and imperial moral instruction flowed far and wide. The realm has enjoyed supreme harmony for more than 170 years down to the present.
Now our Emperor, intelligent, enlightened, divine, and sagely, has responded to Heaven’s appointed cycle and brought about a restoration. With his Heaven-endowed gifts, he has carried forward the vast and enduring imperial legacy, presided over an age of rites and music, and wielded the authority to establish institutions. He has enlarged the sagely plan and brought a great renewal before all eyes. His undertakings in examining ancient ritual forms have flourished splendidly. He has also expressed himself in writings that illuminate the universe. First he composed the Great Compendium Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), elucidating the distinction between succession to the imperial line and succession as an heir, and discussing in detail how both moral duty and human feeling can be fully satisfied. By establishing the highest human standard and making his sagely filial piety shine forth, he thereby fixed the cardinal bonds and constant norms for all ages. His Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness (Jingyi) and his annotations to the Five Admonitions exercise utmost care at the very point from which words and actions spring, and increasingly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
密於
郊廟天人之際妙心傳而熙
聖學所以接千聖之道統也若夫
欽天記頌蓋以明昭受之誠
平臺詠歌又以啓臣鄰之歡則又莫非
敬一之寓者也
天藻奎章紛綸葳蕤未易殫述其文皆天地日
月也其旨則圖之所謂太極疇之所謂皇
極二帝三王相授而守之一道也於此益
有以見我
===
皇上之媲美帝王同符
聖祖而非漢唐宋諸君之所可望矣然
皇上以神聖之資光大之學逈越千古而於爲
文乃惟
祖宗是法者此正漢唐宋之君所不得而聞者
也伏讀
祖宗之文明白易簡不爲文釆緣飾而開心見
誠入人之深天下誦之以至於今而用之
punctuated:
密於郊廟天人之際，妙心傳而熙聖學，所以接千聖之道統也。若夫《欽天記頌》，蓋以明昭受之誠；《平臺詠歌》，又以啓臣鄰之歡，則又莫非敬一之寓者也。天藻奎章，紛綸葳蕤，未易殫述。其文皆天地日月也，其旨則圖之所謂太極、疇之所謂皇極，二帝三王相授而守之一道也。於此益有以見我皇上之媲美帝王、同符聖祖，而非漢唐宋諸君之所可望矣。
然皇上以神聖之資、光大之學，逈越千古，而於爲文乃惟祖宗是法者，此正漢唐宋之君所不得而聞者也。伏讀祖宗之文，明白易簡，不爲文釆緣飾，而開心見誠，入人之深，天下誦之以至於今，而用之
translation_en:
…more exacting in the rites at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, where Heaven and humanity meet. They give subtle expression to the transmission of the mind and illuminate sagely learning, thereby continuing the succession of the Way handed down through a thousand sages. As for the Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven (Qintian ji song), it makes manifest the sincerity with which the heavenly mandate is received; the Songs of the Platform (Pingtai yongge) likewise awaken joy among the attendant ministers. These, too, all embody reverent concentration on the One. His celestial compositions and stellar writings are abundant and luxuriant, and cannot readily be described exhaustively. These writings are all like Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon. Their purport is what the Diagram calls the Supreme Ultimate and what the Categories of the Great Plan call the August Ultimate: the single Way that the Two Emperors and Three Kings transmitted to one another and upheld. Here we see still more clearly that our Emperor rivals the ancient emperors and kings in excellence and accords with the Sagely Founder—heights that the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song could not hope to attain.
Yet although the Emperor, through his divine and sagely endowments and his vast and luminous learning, far surpasses all preceding ages, in composing prose he takes only his imperial ancestors as models. This is precisely what the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song never had the opportunity even to hear of. Humbly reading the writings of the imperial ancestors, we find them lucid, straightforward, and simple. They do not resort to literary embellishment, but lay open the heart and reveal sincerity, profoundly moving their readers. All under Heaven have recited them down to the present day, and their use…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
不窮者此正二帝三王無意於文而言之
自文行之自遠之妙道而我
皇上之爲文也多於
君臣恭和從容燕詠之際此即
聖誥之君臣同遊
帝王之明良喜起者矣是以海內向化譽髦彙
征而作人之化昭如也愚也陶育於菁莪
棫樸之中而涵濡乎禮樂詩書之教爲日
久矣於
聖製之對敢不以經世道統之說而揚厲之
===
第二問
同考試官教諭崔　批〔王政莫大乎教養我〕
申嘉瑞
聖祖與
皇上惓惓焉以此爲急保民致治之道無以加矣此作鋪張殆盡是善頌
聖政者歟
同考試官學正林　批〔說教養處鑿鑿可據是達〕
於治體者
punctuated:
不窮者，此正二帝三王無意於文，而言之自文、行之自遠之妙道。而我皇上之爲文也，多於君臣恭和、從容燕詠之際，此即聖誥之君臣同遊、帝王之明良喜起者矣。是以海內向化，譽髦彙征，而作人之化昭如也。愚也陶育於菁莪棫樸之中，而涵濡乎禮樂詩書之教爲日久矣。於聖製之對，敢不以經世道統之說而揚厲之？

第二問

同考試官教諭崔，批〔王政莫大乎教養我〕

申嘉瑞

聖祖與皇上惓惓焉以此爲急，保民致治之道無以加矣。此作鋪張殆盡，是善頌聖政者歟！

同考試官學正林，批〔說教養處鑿鑿可據，是達〕於治體者。
translation_en:
…and remain inexhaustible in their application: this is precisely the wondrous Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, who had no deliberate intention of producing fine writing, yet whose words naturally possessed literary grace and circulated far and wide. Our Emperor’s writings, moreover, are often composed when ruler and ministers harmonize reverently, exchanging verses at leisure during banquets. This exemplifies the ruler and ministers sharing their outings in the Sacred Admonitions, and the enlightened sovereign and worthy ministers rejoicing together and spurring one another to action under the ancient emperors and kings. Thus all within the seas turn toward his transforming influence, eminent talents advance together, and the transforming power that nurtures men of ability shines manifestly. I, in my humble capacity, have long been nurtured amid the cultivation of talent celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood” and “The Oak Trees,” and steeped in the teachings of rites, music, the Odes, and the Documents. In responding to this imperially composed question, how could I fail to extol it through an account of ordering the world and the orthodox transmission of the Way?

Second Question

Shen Jiarui 申嘉瑞

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui 崔, Instructor: “Nothing in kingly government is greater than educating and nourishing the people. Our sacred founding emperor and our present Emperor have earnestly treated this as their urgent concern. No way of protecting the people and achieving good order can surpass it. This essay expounds the subject almost exhaustively. Surely its author is skilled in praising the sagely government!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin 林, Instructor: “The passages discussing education and nourishment are precise and well grounded. This is someone who understands the essential principles of government.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭　批〔以教養歸之誠深得探本〕
〔之論〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔典實〕
帝王之御世也有冒天下之至仁有先天
下之實政仁也者所以存於中而爲政之
體政也者所以布於外而爲仁之施非仁
則政爲徒法而惠澤不足以下究非政則
仁爲徒善而法制不足以成能故有慈愛
惻怛之心存於中而復有紀綱法度之施
===
布於外仁以基政政以達仁則開創於前
者有以垂休於不替紹述於後者足以保
洽於無疆矣此我
太祖高皇帝於天造草昧之初首舉農桑學校
之政而
皇上於重熙累洽之世益以勸農教士而纘承
光大之凡以
至仁之心而達之實政者也
治化日隆而風俗日美有由然哉請爲執事竟
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭，批〔以教養歸之誠，深得探本〕〔之論。〕
考試官教諭曲，批〔典實。〕
帝王之御世也，有冒天下之至仁，有先天下之實政。仁也者，所以存於中而爲政之體；政也者，所以布於外而爲仁之施。非仁，則政爲徒法，而惠澤不足以下究；非政，則仁爲徒善，而法制不足以成能。故有慈愛惻怛之心存於中，而復有紀綱法度之施布於外。仁以基政，政以達仁，則開創於前者有以垂休於不替，紹述於後者足以保洽於無疆矣。此我太祖高皇帝於天造草昧之初，首舉農桑學校之政，而皇上於重熙累洽之世，益以勸農教士而纘承光大之，凡以至仁之心而達之實政者也。治化日隆，而風俗日美，有由然哉！請爲執事竟
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔By tracing education and material sustenance back to sincerity, this〕〔argument probes deeply into their foundation.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔Well grounded in classical precedent and substantive.〕
When emperors and kings govern the world, they possess both consummate benevolence that embraces all under Heaven and practical policies that lead all under Heaven. Benevolence resides within and constitutes the substance of government; government is enacted outwardly and puts benevolence into practice. Without benevolence, government is merely a body of laws, and its beneficence cannot reach down to the people. Without government, benevolence is merely good intentions, and laws and institutions cannot accomplish their work. Thus, a heart of loving concern and compassion must reside within, while discipline, order, laws, and standards are also put into practice outwardly. When benevolence provides the foundation for government and government gives effect to benevolence, those who first establish a dynasty can bequeath blessings that never lapse, and those who subsequently carry on their work can preserve peace and harmony without limit.
This is why our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, at the founding, when the world was still in its primordial disorder, first instituted policies concerning agriculture, sericulture, and schools. And why His Majesty, in an age of accumulated prosperity and enduring peace, has further encouraged farming and educated scholars, continuing and amplifying that legacy. All this gives expression to a heart of consummate benevolence through practical government. There is indeed a reason why the transforming influence of government grows daily more splendid and customs daily improve! Allow me, honored examiners, to complete…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
其說粤稽古昔聖神繼作之世制器尚象
之餘茹毛飲血之風變而耒耜之教興結
繩而治之俗易而書契之制作此其教養
斯民之法於此乎肇端矣逮及唐虞命棄
爲后稷以教稼穡命契爲司徒以教胄子
三代則有貢助徹之興制庠序校之興名
此其教養斯民之政於此乎漸備矣夫天
立君以爲民君承天以作極使或不能以
遂民之生復民之性其何以膺繼天立極
之任盡裁成輔相之道以成位乎其中哉
===
自是而漢而唐而宋中間世道之升降不
一而世主之純駁不無可議者降及胡元
以夷狄入主中國則魚肉我生靈而人不
知衣食之樂矣磔裂我冠裳而人不知彝
倫之敘矣不有
聖人者出則世道民物吾不知其何所止極也
我
太祖高皇帝以
punctuated:
其說。粤稽古昔聖神繼作之世，制器尚象之餘，茹毛飲血之風變，而耒耜之教興；結繩而治之俗易，而書契之制作。此其教養斯民之法，於此乎肇端矣。逮及唐虞，命棄爲后稷以教稼穡，命契爲司徒以教胄子。三代則有貢助徹之興制，庠序校之興名。此其教養斯民之政，於此乎漸備矣。夫天立君以爲民，君承天以作極，使或不能以遂民之生、復民之性，其何以膺繼天立極之任，盡裁成輔相之道，以成位乎其中哉？
自是而漢，而唐，而宋，中間世道之升降不一，而世主之純駁不無可議者。降及胡元，以夷狄入主中國，則魚肉我生靈，而人不知衣食之樂矣；磔裂我冠裳，而人不知彝倫之敘矣。不有聖人者出，則世道民物，吾不知其何所止極也。我太祖高皇帝以
translation_en:
…this explanation. Looking back to antiquity, when sages and divine rulers arose in succession, they fashioned implements by taking images as their models. Thereafter, the custom of eating raw flesh and drinking blood changed, and instruction in the use of plows arose; the practice of governing through knotted cords changed, and written records were devised. Here began the methods by which they educated and nourished the people. By the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, Qi 棄 was appointed Minister of Agriculture to teach sowing and reaping, and Xie 契 was appointed Minister of Education to instruct the sons of the nobility. Under the Three Dynasties, the gong, zhu, and che systems of agricultural taxation were established, and schools bearing the names xiang, xu, and xiao arose. Thus the institutions for educating and nourishing the people gradually became complete. Heaven establishes rulers for the people, and rulers receive Heaven’s charge to establish the supreme standard. If they cannot secure the people’s livelihood and restore their inherent nature, how can they discharge the responsibility of succeeding Heaven and establishing that standard, fully carry out the work of regulating and assisting Heaven and Earth, and take their proper place between them?
Thereafter came the Han, the Tang, and the Song. Throughout these ages, the moral condition of the world rose and fell unevenly, and the purity or admixture of their rulers’ virtue was not beyond criticism. Coming down to the barbarian Yuan, outsiders entered and ruled the Central Kingdom. They treated our living people as fish and meat, so that people no longer knew the pleasures of clothing and food; they tore apart our caps and robes, so that people no longer knew the proper ordering of the enduring human relationships. Had no sage arisen, I do not know to what extremity the world’s moral condition, its people, and its creatures would have come. Our founding emperor, Taizu Gao, by…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
天縱之聖應運而興掃除腥膻正一統宇知農
桑爲衣食之本學校爲敎化之原故首
頒條章凡有司給由赴京者若無桑株數目
學校緣由論擬違
制其崇重之意已見於此矣故
卽位之後念齊魯之民餽糧給軍而免山東秋
夏之稅平燕都下晉冀念民之困於徵斂
而免北平河東山西之稅因軍國取給供
億浩繁則寧國太平等四郡再行蠲稅焉
===
因民力勤動轉運艱難則河南等省揚州
等府盡蠲稅糧焉其免山西陝右之稅則
因軍需轉運
宮殿經營也其免姑熟六州四縣之稅則因
甲仗之餘供億之盛也至十三年則又
下詔曰荷
上天眷佑君主華夷十又三年倉廩盈府庫充
今民力未甦凡天下今年夏稅秋糧盡蠲
免之其
punctuated:
天縱之聖，應運而興，掃除腥膻，正一統宇，知農桑爲衣食之本，學校爲敎化之原，故首頒條章：凡有司給由赴京者，若無桑株數目、學校緣由，論擬違制。其崇重之意，已見於此矣。
故卽位之後，念齊魯之民餽糧給軍，而免山東秋夏之稅；平燕都，下晉冀，念民之困於徵斂，而免北平、河東、山西之稅。因軍國取給，供億浩繁，則寧國、太平等四郡再行蠲稅焉；因民力勤動，轉運艱難，則河南等省、揚州等府盡蠲稅糧焉。其免山西、陝右之稅，則因軍需轉運、宮殿經營也；其免姑熟六州四縣之稅，則因甲仗之餘、供億之盛也。
至十三年，則又下詔曰：「荷上天眷佑，君主華夷十又三年，倉廩盈，府庫充。今民力未甦，凡天下今年夏稅秋糧，盡蠲免之。」其
translation_en:
…with Heaven-endowed sagacity, rose in response to the destined time, swept away the rank and foul invaders, and brought order to the unified realm [?]. He knew that farming and sericulture were the foundation of clothing and food, and that schools were the source of moral transformation. He therefore first promulgated regulations: whenever officials of the local administrations received service certificates and proceeded to the capital, if these lacked figures for mulberry trees or an account of the schools, their cases were to be adjudicated as violations of an imperial decree. His intention to accord these matters great importance was already evident in this.
Thus, after ascending the throne, mindful that the people of Qi and Lu had supplied grain to the army, he remitted Shandong’s autumn and summer taxes. After pacifying the capital at Yan and taking Jin and Ji, mindful of the people’s distress under tax exactions, he remitted the taxes of Beiping, Hedong, and Shanxi. Because provisioning the army and state entailed immense demands, he again remitted taxes in the four prefectures including Ningguo and Taiping. Because the people’s strength had been exhausted by labor and transport was difficult, he entirely remitted the grain taxes in provinces including Henan and prefectures including Yangzhou. His remission of taxes in Shanxi and Shanyou was on account of the transport of military supplies and the construction of palaces. His remission of taxes in Gushu, six subprefectures, and four counties [?] was on account of the aftermath of warfare and the heavy burden of provisioning.
In the thirteenth year, he again issued an edict: “Favored by Heaven’s watchful protection, I have ruled over Chinese and non-Chinese alike for thirteen years. The granaries are full, and the treasuries well stocked. Yet the people’s strength has not recovered. Let this year’s summer taxes and autumn grain levies throughout the realm be entirely remitted.” His…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
深仁厚澤形於播告者蓋以民承胡元之後塗
炭已極而繼以轉輸供億之苦故其
存恤之典欲甦民生於久困以遂其生也嗚
呼其所以凝
天命結人心以培千萬世不拔之基者不在此
乎又以教化爲國之首務故
誥禮部尚書則曰爲國之治道非禮則無法所
以禮之爲用表也法之爲用裏也故設官
備禮協和人神務得通今古博羣書明於
===
禮而善周旋者乃爲是任
誥國子祭酒有曰太學之設不獨教生徒而已
王者親祭必寡故設官以代之其職在潔
牲牢淨廚竈精籩豆祭不失時尚竭乃恭
而臨祭靜乃神以對神於太學生有
諭則勑以篤道之志申以亂常之法欲其志在
謙柔恭謹固守仲尼四非之篤於國學師
徒有
諭則謂師必盡師者之禮學必盡學者之誠欲
punctuated:
深仁厚澤形於播告者，蓋以民承胡元之後，塗炭已極，而繼以轉輸供億之苦，故其存恤之典，欲甦民生於久困，以遂其生也。嗚呼！其所以凝天命、結人心，以培千萬世不拔之基者，不在此乎？
又以教化爲國之首務，故誥禮部尚書則曰：「爲國之治道，非禮則無法。所以禮之爲用，表也；法之爲用，裏也。故設官備禮，協和人神，務得通今古、博羣書、明於禮而善周旋者，乃爲是任。」
誥國子祭酒有曰：「太學之設，不獨教生徒而已。王者親祭必寡，故設官以代之。其職在潔牲牢、淨廚竈、精籩豆，祭不失時。尚竭乃恭而臨祭，靜乃神以對神。」於太學生有諭，則勑以篤道之志，申以亂常之法，欲其志在謙柔恭謹，固守仲尼四非之篤。於國學師徒有諭，則謂師必盡師者之禮，學必盡學者之誠，欲
translation_en:
…The profound benevolence and generous favor expressed in these proclamations arose because the people, emerging from the rule of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, had already suffered the utmost misery, only to endure further hardships transporting supplies and meeting official demands. His provisions for their relief therefore sought to revive their livelihoods after prolonged distress and enable them to sustain their lives. Ah! Was this not how he secured Heaven’s Mandate and bound the people’s hearts to him, laying an unshakable foundation for countless generations?
He also regarded moral instruction as the foremost business of government. Thus, in an admonition to the Minister of Rites, he said: “In the way of governing a state, without ritual propriety there can be no standards. Ritual propriety functions as the exterior; law functions as the interior. Hence officials are appointed and rites fully provided, to bring humans and spirits into harmony. For this office, one must obtain someone versed in past and present, widely read in the books, knowledgeable in ritual, and adept in ceremonial conduct.”
An admonition to the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education said: “The Imperial University was established not merely to instruct students. The occasions on which the sovereign personally offers sacrifice must be few, so officials are appointed to act in his place. Their duties are to keep the sacrificial animals pure, the kitchens and stoves clean, and the sacrificial baskets and vessels in perfect order, and to ensure that sacrifices are offered at the proper times. Exert your utmost reverence when attending the sacrifices, and quiet your spirit to encounter the spirits.” In instructions to the students of the Imperial University, he enjoined a steadfast commitment to the Way and reiterated the laws against violating the constant moral norms. He wished them to aspire to humility, gentleness, reverence, and circumspection, and to adhere firmly to Zhongni’s four prohibitions against seeing, hearing, speaking, or acting contrary to ritual propriety. In instructions to the teachers and students of the state school, he said that teachers must fully observe the proprieties incumbent upon teachers, and students must bring complete sincerity to learning, wishing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
其時忽有言使得聞嘉言善行發先聖之
幽德以資後嗣其
省頑有文則欲人慮患以防險脩德以善終
且其
國學之建已於未
登極之前三年而
詔立郡縣學即於
登極後之二年而於八年即
詔天下以立社學其申牖民性昭布
===
綸綍者以胡元之後民皆習染汙俗而不知
仁義禮樂之教諄復之訓欲啓民生於久
贖以復其性也嗚呼其所以成人才厚風
俗以垂億萬載無疆之休者不在此乎夫
膺命之初萬事草創財用宜不足矣而顧有餘
者蓋萃人心於旣渙之餘而撙節愛養之
深至耳教化宜未遑矣而獨首舉者蓋斡
世道於
維新之時而化導興起之恐後耳一時
punctuated: 其時忽有言，使得聞嘉言善行，發先聖之幽德，以資後嗣。其《省頑》有文，則欲人慮患以防險，脩德以善終。且其國學之建，已於未登極之前三年，而詔立郡縣學，即於登極後之二年，而於八年，即詔天下以立社學。其申牖民性、昭布綸綍者，以胡元之後，民皆習染汙俗，而不知仁義禮樂之教；諄復之訓，欲啓民生於久贖，以復其性也。嗚呼！其所以成人才、厚風俗，以垂億萬載無疆之休者，不在此乎？夫膺命之初，萬事草創，財用宜不足矣，而顧有餘者，蓋萃人心於旣渙之餘，而撙節愛養之深至耳。教化宜未遑矣，而獨首舉者，蓋斡世道於維新之時，而化導興起之恐後耳。一時
translation_en:
…that, when words were unexpectedly spoken [?], they might hear exemplary sayings and good deeds, reveal the unmanifest virtue of the former sages, and thereby benefit later generations. His text Admonishing the Stubborn (Xing wan) sought to make people anticipate trouble so as to guard against danger, and cultivate virtue so as to reach a good end. Moreover, the National University had already been established three years before he ascended the throne. In the second year after his accession, he decreed the establishment of prefectural and county schools; in the eighth year, he decreed the establishment of community schools throughout the realm. His repeated efforts to enlighten the people's nature, and his public promulgation of imperial pronouncements, arose because, after the rule of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, the people had all become steeped in corrupt customs and knew nothing of instruction in benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music. His earnest, repeated admonitions sought to awaken the people from their long-standing condition [?; the transcription reads “long redemption”], so that they might recover their original nature.

Ah! Was it not through these measures that he developed men of talent and enriched customs, bequeathing boundless blessings for countless ages? When he first received the Mandate, everything was being built from the ground up, and financial resources might well have been insufficient. Yet there was instead a surplus, surely because he reunited the people's hearts after their dispersal, and exercised the utmost frugality and loving care in nurturing them. There might well have been no leisure for moral instruction, yet he made it his first undertaking, surely because, as the realm was renewed, he sought to redirect the course of society, fearing that he might fall behind in guiding and inspiring the people. At that time…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
仁厚之化薰蒸透徹
盛治氣象藹然宇宙間矣易謂
聖人作而萬物覩茲其會哉
列聖相承益隆紹述康阜之休百餘年猶一日
也至我
皇上纘繼前烈益潤
鴻猷以
聖祖之心爲心以
聖祖之政爲政而於農桑學校尤惓惓焉自今
===
觀之如
躬籍田之耕時
西苑之御聞奏災而亟加賑貸遇水旱而竭
誠祈省
神機運用無非休息之實蓋與
聖祖同出一軌也有
明倫大典以定綱常有
敬一之箴以布學校定文體而澆訛之習去
正士途而倖進之門塞
punctuated: 仁厚之化薰蒸透徹，盛治氣象藹然宇宙間矣。《易》謂：「聖人作而萬物覩。」茲其會哉！列聖相承，益隆紹述，康阜之休，百餘年猶一日也。至我皇上纘繼前烈，益潤鴻猷，以聖祖之心爲心，以聖祖之政爲政，而於農桑學校尤惓惓焉。自今觀之，如躬籍田之耕，時西苑之御，聞奏災而亟加賑貸，遇水旱而竭誠祈省，神機運用，無非休息之實，蓋與聖祖同出一軌也。有《明倫大典》以定綱常，有敬一之箴以布學校，定文體而澆訛之習去，正士途而倖進之門塞。
translation_en:
…the transforming influence of benevolence and generosity permeated everything, and the atmosphere of flourishing government filled the universe. The Book of Changes says: “When the sage arises, all beings behold him.” Was this not precisely such a moment? Successive sage emperors carried on the succession, increasingly honoring and continuing their predecessors’ work. The blessings of peace and prosperity remained constant for more than a hundred years, as though it were a single day. Now our Emperor has succeeded to the achievements of his predecessors and further enriched their grand designs. He takes the Sagely Ancestor’s heart as his own heart and the Sagely Ancestor’s government as his own government, devoting particular care to agriculture, sericulture, and schools.

Looking at the present, we see him personally ploughing the imperial ritual field and visiting the Western Park at appropriate times [?]. On hearing reports of disasters, he promptly provides relief and loans; when floods or droughts occur, he prays and examines himself with utmost sincerity. Every exercise of his sagacious judgment gives practical substance to allowing the people rest and recuperation. In this he follows precisely the same course as the Sagely Ancestor. There is the Great Compendium Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian) to establish the cardinal relationships and constant moral principles; there is the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen) for distribution to schools. By regulating literary style, he eliminates frivolous and erroneous habits; by rectifying scholars’ routes into office, he closes the doors to advancement through undeserved favor…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
宸翰布昭無非惇庸之典蓋與
聖祖同出一心也是皆
仁厚一脉綿綿相傳
作於前者有以開光明俊偉之業
大於後者足以衍雍熙悠久之盛齊民安享
於樂利之天多士沐浴於菁莪之化
泰和景象雖唐虞盛時又何以加於此哉夫爲
政之本不外乎
君心之仁而此心之存不出於誠之一字故孟
===
子謂先王有不忍之心之政而治可運諸
掌中庸以天下國家之九經而行之以一
不忍者仁之端而一者誠之謂也苟仁而
非誠則仁爲有間而凡紀綱法度之布徒
爲文具之末禮樂刑政之施秪爲粉飾之
具此爲治之大經大法皆不外一誠以爲
之地也我
聖祖開創於前
皇上建極於後是皆於教養斯民深致意焉前
punctuated: 宸翰布昭，無非惇庸之典，蓋與聖祖同出一心也。是皆仁厚一脉，綿綿相傳。作於前者，有以開光明俊偉之業；大於後者，足以衍雍熙悠久之盛。齊民安享於樂利之天，多士沐浴於菁莪之化。泰和景象，雖唐虞盛時，又何以加於此哉？夫爲政之本，不外乎君心之仁，而此心之存，不出於誠之一字。故孟子謂先王有不忍之心之政，而治可運諸掌；《中庸》以天下國家之九經，而行之以一。不忍者，仁之端，而一者，誠之謂也。苟仁而非誠，則仁爲有間，而凡紀綱法度之布，徒爲文具之末；禮樂刑政之施，秪爲粉飾之具。此爲治之大經大法，皆不外一誠以爲之地也。我聖祖開創於前，皇上建極於後，是皆於教養斯民深致意焉。前
translation_en:
The imperial writings, promulgated far and wide, are all ordinances for honoring the worthy and employing the deserving; they surely issue from the same mind as those of the sagely progenitor. All this is one continuous lineage of benevolence and generosity, transmitted without interruption. Those who initiated it in earlier times thereby founded a brilliant and magnificent enterprise; those who enlarged it afterward have extended an enduring flourishing of harmony and peace. The common people peacefully enjoy a world of happiness and benefit, while the many scholars are bathed in the nurturing influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Mugwort” (Jing e). Such a scene of supreme harmony—even the flourishing age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun could hardly surpass it!

The foundation of government lies solely in the benevolence of the ruler’s heart, and preserving this heart rests on the single word “sincerity.” Thus Mengzi says that the former kings possessed a heart that could not bear others’ suffering and a corresponding government, so that governing could be managed as readily as turning something in the palm of one’s hand. The Doctrine of the Mean sets out nine guiding principles for governing the world, the state, and the family, yet says that they are carried out through one thing. The inability to bear others’ suffering is the beginning of benevolence, and that one thing means sincerity. If there is benevolence without sincerity, benevolence will have interruptions: the promulgation of institutions, laws, and standards will amount merely to empty formalities, and the implementation of rites, music, punishments, and administration will serve merely as outward embellishment. These great principles and fundamental methods of government all depend upon sincerity alone as their foundation.

Our sagely progenitor established the dynasty in earlier times, and His Majesty has since established the supreme standard of rulership. Both have devoted profound attention to educating and nourishing this people. The earlier…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
創後承一皆以至誠爲之匪徒事乎虛文
是以
德意宣昭和氣充暢而收家給人足之效成遵
道遵路之風矣昔周公陳后稷公劉風化
之所由以告成王而成王以此守成卒爲
周之令主蓋周家王業之本端在乎此而
帝王傳心之要亦不越乎此今
皇上緝熙宥密而上符
皇祖眞出周成王之上此
===
祈天永命之道
社稷靈長之慶也雖然愚尤有説焉立政以
心固也不曰爲政在人乎夫養之道至矣
而所以任養民之責者則在乎守令宋朱
光庭有言圖治莫先於擇守令郡守得其
人則千里受其賜縣令得其人則百里受
其賜誠使愼簡於斯不顓顓於考校必試
其人之果諳於民事而篤厚者而後授之
而重任之則必能宣布
punctuated:
創後承，一皆以至誠爲之，匪徒事乎虛文。是以德意宣昭，和氣充暢，而收家給人足之效，成遵道遵路之風矣。昔周公陳后稷、公劉風化之所由，以告成王，而成王以此守成，卒爲周之令主。蓋周家王業之本端在乎此，而帝王傳心之要亦不越乎此。今皇上緝熙宥密，而上符皇祖，眞出周成王之上。此祈天永命之道，社稷靈長之慶也。
雖然，愚尤有説焉。立政以心，固也，不曰「爲政在人」乎？夫養之道至矣，而所以任養民之責者，則在乎守令。宋朱光庭有言：「圖治莫先於擇守令。郡守得其人，則千里受其賜；縣令得其人，則百里受其賜。」誠使愼簡於斯，不顓顓於考校，必試其人之果諳於民事而篤厚者，而後授之，而重任之，則必能宣布
translation_en:
…founded the undertaking, and the successor carried it on: both acted with utmost sincerity, rather than merely attending to empty forms. Thus their benevolent intentions have been clearly proclaimed, harmonious influences have spread abundantly, and they have achieved sufficiency for every household and every person, establishing a custom of following the proper Way and path. Formerly, the Duke of Zhou explained to King Cheng the sources of the transforming moral influence of Hou Ji and Gong Liu. King Cheng preserved his inherited achievement by these means and ultimately became an excellent ruler of Zhou. Indeed, the foundation of the Zhou royal enterprise lay precisely here, and the essential teaching transmitted from the minds of emperors and kings likewise went no further than this. Now Your Majesty continues in luminous virtue, profound and tranquil, matching your imperial ancestor above and truly surpassing King Cheng of Zhou. This is the way to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate, and the blessing that ensures the dynasty’s lasting prosperity.
Nevertheless, I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. That establishing government depends upon the heart is certainly true; yet is it not also said, “The conduct of government depends upon men”? The way of nourishing the people is perfected, but responsibility for nourishing them rests with prefects and county magistrates. Zhu Guangting of the Song said: “In seeking good government, nothing takes precedence over choosing prefects and county magistrates. When the right man is appointed prefect, the people over a thousand li receive his benefits; when the right man is appointed county magistrate, the people over a hundred li receive his benefits.” If selection for these posts is truly careful, without concentrating exclusively on formal assessments, and candidates must first be tested to establish that they are indeed versed in the people’s affairs and sincere and generous in character, before being appointed and entrusted with weighty responsibilities, then they will assuredly be able to proclaim…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
德意以撫綏民物而民之被其澤者益深矣教
之道至矣而所以任教民之責者則在乎
師儒宋程伯淳有言治天下以正風俗得
賢才爲本宜擇學明德尊者爲太學師次
以分教天下之學擇士教之以升於朝誠
使愼簡於斯不拘拘於資格必試其人之
果深於經術而老成者而後授之而重禮
之則必能敷揚禮教以成就人才而士之
成其德者益廣矣然此固愚平日所聞於
前哲之言耳惟執事者不以老生常談棄
===
之或以轉聞於
上未必不爲
今日盛治之一助
第三問
楊枚
同考試官教諭李 批 治曆能明差法則其時自
正而至要尤不外於周官以辨敘事以詔救政二語士子
往往不知題意所在此作引對詳切而忠告之意溢於言
punctuated:
德意，以撫綏民物，而民之被其澤者益深矣。教之道至矣，而所以任教民之責者，則在乎師儒。宋程伯淳有言：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。宜擇學明德尊者爲太學師，次以分教天下之學，擇士教之，以升於朝。」誠使愼簡於斯，不拘拘於資格，必試其人之果深於經術而老成者，而後授之，而重禮之，則必能敷揚禮教，以成就人才，而士之成其德者益廣矣。然此固愚平日所聞於前哲之言耳。惟執事者不以老生常談棄之，或以轉聞於上，未必不爲今日盛治之一助。
第三問
楊枚
同考試官教諭李批：治曆能明差法，則其時自正。而至要尤不外於《周官》「以辨敘事」、「以詔救政」二語。士子往往不知題意所在，此作引對詳切，而忠告之意溢於言
translation_en:
…the ruler’s benevolent intentions, thereby comforting and pacifying the people and all living things; the benefits received by the people will then grow still deeper. The means of instruction are fully developed, but responsibility for educating the people rests with the scholarly teachers. Cheng Bochun of the Song said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent. Those whose learning is clear and whose virtue commands respect should be chosen as teachers at the Imperial University; next, such men should be assigned to teach in schools throughout the realm. Select scholars and educate them so that they may advance to service at court.” If selection for these posts is indeed careful, without rigid adherence to formal qualifications, and candidates are tested to ensure that they possess profound classical learning and mature judgment before they are appointed and treated with great respect, they will surely spread ritual instruction and develop talented men. The scholars who perfect their virtue will then become ever more numerous. Yet these are merely teachings of earlier worthies that I have heard in the course of everyday life. If only you gentlemen charged with this matter do not dismiss them as an old scholar’s platitudes, but perhaps transmit them to His Majesty, they might yet contribute something to the flourishing government of our day.
Third Question
Yang Mei
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: If, in regulating the calendar, one understands the methods for calculating discrepancies, its timing will naturally be correct. The essentials lie above all in the two phrases from the Offices of Zhou: “to distinguish and arrange affairs in order” and “to advise on corrective measures in government.” Candidates often fail to grasp the point of the question. This essay adduces evidence and responds in precise detail, while its spirit of loyal counsel overflows its words…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
外錄之非但以其文焉已也
同考試官教諭胡　批　〔典事謹變爲治曆之要子〕
能鋪敘條析辨而有則其强學待問者乎
考試官教諭鄭　批　〔說天人交贊處學步董賈〕
場中如此作者絕少中用之七無能出其右矣
考試官教諭曲　批　〔條對中不失渾厚遠到〕
之器也
===
對觀象以應時者推天以合人理之不容
變也因時以立政者脩人以奉天機之不
容已也何則天運於上非有理以推之則
高遠者不可得而知也人爲於下非有機
以通之則感召者不可得而言也聖人者
出揆之以理不泥於迹握之以機不拘於
時則推之於積分而其數可稽焉考之於
躔度而其象可占焉審之於代謝而其氣
可協焉故凡垂象以示人脩政以合天蓋
交相贊也尚何差殊之足言哉知乎此則
聖人之制曆以辨敘事以詔救政有可得
punctuated:
外。錄之，非但以其文焉已也。
同考試官教諭胡批：〔典事謹變爲治曆之要，子〕能鋪敘條析，辨而有則，其强學待問者乎！
考試官教諭鄭批：〔說天人交贊處，學步董賈。〕場中如此作者絕少，中用之七，無能出其右矣。
考試官教諭曲批：〔條對中不失渾厚遠到〕之器也。
對：觀象以應時者，推天以合人，理之不容變也；因時以立政者，脩人以奉天，機之不容已也。何則？天運於上，非有理以推之，則高遠者不可得而知也；人爲於下，非有機以通之，則感召者不可得而言也。聖人者出，揆之以理，不泥於迹；握之以機，不拘於時。則推之於積分，而其數可稽焉；考之於躔度，而其象可占焉；審之於代謝，而其氣可協焉。故凡垂象以示人，脩政以合天，蓋交相贊也。尚何差殊之足言哉？知乎此，則聖人之制曆，以辨敘事，以詔救政，有可得
translation_en:
…beyond the words. It is included here not merely for its literary merits.
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Ordering affairs and attending carefully to changes are essential to regulating the calendar” [?]. You〕 can expound matters fully and analyze them point by point, making distinctions in an orderly manner. Surely you are one who studies diligently and stands ready to answer questions!
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing how Heaven and humanity assist one another, he follows in the footsteps of Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi.〕 Writers like this are exceedingly rare in the examination hall. Among the seven selected [?], none can surpass him.
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔In his answers to the successive points, he retains a substantial, generous character and far-reaching vision〕—such is his capacity.
Reply: Observing celestial phenomena to accord with the seasons means investigating Heaven so as to bring it into accord with human affairs: this is a principle that admits of no alteration. Establishing government in accordance with the seasons means putting human affairs in order so as to serve Heaven: this is an operation that cannot cease. Why is this? Heaven moves above; without principles by which to investigate it, its loftiness and remoteness cannot be understood. Human beings act below; without grasping the workings that connect them with Heaven, one cannot speak of the responses their actions call forth. When a sage arises, he measures these things by principle without becoming fixated on their outward traces, and grasps their workings without being confined by the times. By calculating accumulated fractional units, their numerical relations can be checked; by examining the degrees of celestial progression, their configurations can be interpreted; by scrutinizing successive changes, their vital forces can be harmonized. Thus Heaven displays phenomena to instruct humanity, and humanity puts government in order to accord with Heaven: each assists the other. What discrepancy, then, remains worth discussing? Understanding this, we may begin to explain how the sages established the calendar to distinguish and arrange affairs and to direct measures for remedying failures in government…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
而言矣雖然曆豈易言哉人非天不因爲
天之說者一寒一暑以爲歲一盈一虧以
爲月一晝一夜以爲日一經一緯以爲星
辰則天之所運而人所不能違也天非人
不成爲人之說者質之錯行而歲無不成
稽之晦朔而月無不明審之甲乙而日無
不正辨之縱橫而星辰無不序則人之所
推而天亦不能外也然天運雖有常而動
靜消息實則微妙而難窮人事雖有貞而
===
吉凶悔吝係於感通而難必乃若以次星
致位以景儀致晷以冬夏致日以春秋致
月此周所以設馮相氏之官職司其常以
辨敘事而興民功者出於此矣以分土觀
妖祥以歲星觀吉凶以雲辨祲象以風命
乖別此周所以設保章氏之官職司其變
以詔救政而謹天戒者由於此矣曆之作
也夫豈徒哉求之於前黃帝使羲和占日
常儀占月區車占星象大撓作甲子而總
punctuated: 而言矣。雖然，曆豈易言哉？人非天不因。爲天之說者，一寒一暑以爲歲，一盈一虧以爲月，一晝一夜以爲日，一經一緯以爲星辰，則天之所運而人所不能違也。天非人不成。爲人之說者，質之錯行而歲無不成，稽之晦朔而月無不明，審之甲乙而日無不正，辨之縱橫而星辰無不序，則人之所推而天亦不能外也。然天運雖有常，而動靜消息實則微妙而難窮；人事雖有貞，而吉凶悔吝係於感通而難必。乃若以次星致位，以景儀致晷，以冬夏致日，以春秋致月，此周所以設馮相氏之官，職司其常，以辨敘事而興民功者出於此矣。以分土觀妖祥，以歲星觀吉凶，以雲辨祲象，以風命乖別，此周所以設保章氏之官，職司其變，以詔救政而謹天戒者由於此矣。曆之作也，夫豈徒哉？求之於前，黃帝使羲和占日，常儀占月，區車占星象，大撓作甲子，而總
translation_en:
…can thus be discussed. Even so, how could the calendar be easy to discuss? Human beings must take Heaven as their basis. From Heaven’s side, one period of cold and one of heat constitute a year; one waxing and one waning constitute a month; one day and one night constitute a full day; and the fixed and moving celestial bodies constitute the stars. These are Heaven’s movements, which human beings cannot contravene. Yet Heaven’s work requires human beings for its completion. From the human side, by checking the intersecting celestial movements, every year is duly established; by examining the last and first days of the lunar month, every month is clearly determined; by scrutinizing the cyclical signs jia and yi, every day is correctly designated; and by distinguishing longitudinal and transverse positions, all the stars are put in order. These are human calculations, beyond which Heaven itself cannot depart. Yet although Heaven’s movements have regular patterns, their motion and stillness, waning and growth, are subtle and difficult to fathom fully. Although human affairs have enduring principles, good fortune, misfortune, regret, and distress depend on responsive interaction and are difficult to ascertain with certainty.
As for determining celestial positions from the stellar lodges, determining shadows with a shadow-measuring instrument, determining the sun’s position at the winter and summer solstices, and determining the moon’s position at the spring and autumn equinoxes: these explain why the Zhou established the office of Astronomer (Fengxiang shi), charged with overseeing celestial regularities. From this came the means to distinguish and order seasonal activities and set the people’s work in motion. Observing ominous and auspicious signs according to territorial divisions, discerning good and ill fortune through Jupiter, distinguishing baleful celestial manifestations through clouds, and identifying aberrations through winds: these explain why the Zhou established the office of Astrologer (Baozhang shi), charged with overseeing celestial anomalies. From this came the means to advise remedial measures in government and heed Heaven’s warnings. Could the making of the calendar have been without purpose?
Looking back to earlier times, the Yellow Emperor had Xihe observe the sun, Changyi observe the moon, Quche [?] observe the stellar configurations, and Danao devise the jiazi cycle; and to bring together…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
其術則有容成氏焉少昊使玄鳥氏司分
伯趙氏司至青鳥氏司啓丹鳥氏司閉而
爲曆正則有鳳鳥氏焉法因之而漸著矣
堯命仲叔以主四時所以爲敬授者有其
本焉舜察璣衡以齊七政所以爲省方者
有所自焉法因之而大備矣是故制其器
以尚象占其數以授時因其序以分職觀
其文以察變所以承天而宅民者何嘗不
本於曆哉求之於後漢之曆凡五變其善
===
而可取者唯司馬遷乎蓋其大初曆原於
鍾律以黃鍾八十一分爲日法復自前曆
上元推之得歲之甲寅又自十一月冬至
逆之得時之甲子日月如合璧五星如連
珠故其晦朔弦望無一毫之殊焉唐之曆
凡八變其最而可稱者唯僧一行乎蓋其
大衍曆本於蓍策以二始位剛柔以二終
紀閏餘以卦氣定七十二候以中星正二
十四氣以晦朔正日月之會以日度正周
punctuated: 其術，則有容成氏焉。少昊使玄鳥氏司分，伯趙氏司至，青鳥氏司啓，丹鳥氏司閉，而爲曆正，則有鳳鳥氏焉。法因之而漸著矣。堯命仲叔以主四時，所以爲敬授者有其本焉；舜察璣衡以齊七政，所以爲省方者有所自焉。法因之而大備矣。是故制其器以尚象，占其數以授時，因其序以分職，觀其文以察變，所以承天而宅民者，何嘗不本於曆哉？求之於後，漢之曆凡五變，其善而可取者，唯司馬遷乎？蓋其大初曆原於鍾律，以黃鍾八十一分爲日法，復自前曆上元推之，得歲之甲寅；又自十一月冬至逆之，得時之甲子。日月如合璧，五星如連珠，故其晦朔弦望無一毫之殊焉。唐之曆凡八變，其最而可稱者，唯僧一行乎？蓋其大衍曆本於蓍策，以二始位剛柔，以二終紀閏餘，以卦氣定七十二候，以中星正二十四氣，以晦朔正日月之會，以日度正周
translation_en: …as for bringing their techniques together, there was Rongcheng. Shaohao charged the Xuanniao clan with overseeing the equinoxes, the Bozhao clan with overseeing the solstices, the Qingniao clan with overseeing the opening of the seasons, and the Danniao clan with overseeing their closing; serving as Director of the Calendar was the Fengniao clan. Through these arrangements, calendrical methods gradually became established. Yao commanded the Zhong and Shu brothers to preside over the four seasons, providing a foundation for reverently transmitting the seasons to the people. Shun examined the celestial sphere and its sighting tube to bring the seven celestial regulators into accord, providing a basis for inspecting the regions. Through these measures, calendrical methods became fully developed. Thus instruments were fashioned to represent celestial configurations; numerical cycles were examined to announce the seasons; offices were assigned according to their sequence; and celestial patterns were observed to discern changes. How could the means of complying with Heaven and settling the people ever have failed to rest upon the calendar? Looking to later times, the Han calendar underwent five changes in all. Was not Sima Qian’s the worthy one deserving adoption? His Taichu Calendar [written 大初 here] was based on the pitch standards of bells, taking the eighty-one divisions of the Huangzhong pitch standard as the denominator for calculating days. Reckoning from the supreme epoch of the preceding calendar, he obtained a jiayin year; reckoning backward from the winter solstice in the eleventh month, he obtained a jiazi time. The sun and moon were like paired jade discs joined together, and the five planets like strung pearls. Thus there was not the slightest discrepancy in its determinations of the last and first days of the lunar month, the quarter moons, and the full moon. The Tang calendar underwent eight changes in all. Was not the monk Yixing’s the finest and most praiseworthy? His Dayan Calendar was based on the yarrow stalks used in divination. It used the two beginnings to assign positions to the firm and yielding, and the two endings to record the intercalary remainder. It used the seasonal influences associated with the hexagrams to determine the seventy-two pentads, and the culminating stars to rectify the twenty-four solar terms. It used the last and first days of the lunar month to determine the conjunctions of the sun and moon, and the degrees of the sun’s motion to rectify the full circuit…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
天之數且其推移增損無非大易之準焉
宋元以來之曆非無可取其至當而可尚
者其惟郭守敬乎蓋其授時曆多本於一
行考正者凡七則創法者凡七則自冬至以迄日行創法
者凡七則自日行以距白道凡夫推步占
候無非大衍之法焉是故改歲而正始明
孟月而象魏布順令而彝典裕遇災而警
惕著所以酬世而宰物者何嘗不本於曆
哉
===
明興稽古圖治尤先於曆璣衡有官而羲和之
職舉焉銅候有儀而推測之法昭焉圭景
有晷而占步之數準焉
頒布有時而臣民之式具焉
履端立極體其元也布象考績正其朔也平
秩勸工唯其時也五刑九伐順其氣也
朝會封告率其期也眚災弔賻處其度也是
故歲周於上而天道明統正於下而人紀
立其與黃帝之儀軌今昔如一道而損益
punctuated:
天之數，且其推移增損，無非大易之準焉。宋元以來之曆，非無可取，其至當而可尚者，其惟郭守敬乎？蓋其授時曆多本於一行，考正者凡七則，創法者凡七則，自冬至以迄日行，創法者凡七則，自日行以距白道。凡夫推步占候，無非大衍之法焉。是故改歲而正始明，孟月而象魏布，順令而彝典裕，遇災而警惕著，所以酬世而宰物者，何嘗不本於曆哉？
明興，稽古圖治，尤先於曆。璣衡有官，而羲和之職舉焉；銅候有儀，而推測之法昭焉；圭景有晷，而占步之數準焉；頒布有時，而臣民之式具焉。履端立極，體其元也；布象考績，正其朔也；平秩勸工，唯其時也；五刑九伐，順其氣也；朝會封告，率其期也；眚災弔賻，處其度也。是故歲周於上而天道明，統正於下而人紀立。其與黃帝之儀軌，今昔如一道，而損益
translation_en:
…the numerical measure of the circuit of Heaven; moreover, all its adjustments, additions, and subtractions follow the standards of the great Book of Changes. The calendars of the Song and Yuan periods and thereafter were not without merit, but was not Guo Shoujing’s the most fitting and worthy of esteem? His Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li) was largely based on Yixing’s work. There were seven provisions for corrections and seven for newly devised methods, extending from the winter solstice to the sun’s motion; there were seven provisions for newly devised methods, extending from the sun’s motion to the moon’s orbital path [?; the transcription appears to repeat and displace part of the enumeration]. All its astronomical calculations and observations followed the methods of the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li). Thus, at the change of year, the proper beginning is made clear; in the first month of each season, proclamations are displayed at the palace gate towers; by following seasonal ordinances, the standing institutions are enriched; and when calamities occur, vigilance and apprehension become manifest. How could the means of responding to the needs of the age and governing all things ever fail to be rooted in the calendar?
When the Ming arose, it examined antiquity in seeking good government and gave particular priority to the calendar. Officials were appointed to oversee the astronomical instruments, and thus the duties of Xi and He were fulfilled. Bronze instruments for observation were provided, and thus the methods of calculation and measurement were made clear. Gnomons were provided for measuring shadows, and thus the numerical results of observation and calculation were made accurate. The calendar was promulgated at prescribed times, and thus officials and people were supplied with a standard to follow. Establishing the beginning and setting the governing standard embodies its calendrical origin; displaying celestial configurations and assessing achievements rectifies its beginnings of months; ordering duties equitably and encouraging work accords with its seasons; the five punishments and nine forms of punitive expedition follow its seasonal influences; court assemblies and the proclamation of enfeoffments observe its appointed dates; remitting penalties in times of calamity, offering condolences, and providing funeral assistance conform to its proper measures. Thus, as the year completes its circuit above, the Way of Heaven becomes clear; as the calendrical system is rectified below, the ordering principles of human society are established. Its rules and standards and those of the Yellow Emperor follow one and the same Way, past and present, while making reductions and additions …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
勝國之法取其順承之理曆名
大統監曰
欽天其與堯舜之敬授先後同一揆所以
贊化育固斯世於熙和蓋有非漢唐宋元所
可望其下風矣猗歟偉哉夫制曆固足以
善治而議曆尤貴於得法於此考究之弗
精則敘弗順其常天時愆度而不知詔弗
隨其變人事乖違而罔覺矣然則其法豈
可以不論乎議曆有日躔者日之行每日
===
遶地一週凡行三百六十五度四分度之
一積三百六十五日四分日之一而與天
會是爲一歲也月離者月之行每日遶地
一週凡不及日十三度十九分度之七積
二十九日九百四十分日之四百九十九
而與日會是爲一月也日與天會者一歲
一次而二十四氣由之以生日之所以盈
者基於此也月與天會者一歲十二次而
十二朔由之以生日之所以虛者本於此
punctuated:
勝國之法，取其順承之理。曆名《大統》，監曰欽天，其與堯舜之敬授，先後同一揆。所以贊化育、固斯世於熙和，蓋有非漢唐宋元所可望其下風矣。猗歟，偉哉！夫制曆固足以善治，而議曆尤貴於得法。於此考究之弗精，則敘弗順其常，天時愆度而不知；詔弗隨其變，人事乖違而罔覺矣。然則其法豈可以不論乎？

議曆有日躔者，日之行每日遶地一週，凡行三百六十五度四分度之一，積三百六十五日四分日之一而與天會，是爲一歲也。月離者，月之行每日遶地一週，凡不及日十三度十九分度之七，積二十九日九百四十分日之四百九十九而與日會，是爲一月也。日與天會者，一歲一次，而二十四氣由之以生，日之所以盈者基於此也。月與天會者，一歲十二次，而十二朔由之以生，日之所以虛者本於此
translation_en:
…the calendrical methods of the preceding dynasty, adopting their principles of orderly succession. The calendar is named “Grand Unification” (Datong), and the directorate is called the Directorate of Astronomy (Qintian). In its reverent communication of the seasons, it follows the same standard as Yao and Shun, despite their separation in time. In assisting Heaven and Earth's transforming and nourishing work and securing this age in prosperity and harmony, its achievements surely surpass anything the Han, Tang, Song, or Yuan could hope to approach. Ah, how magnificent! Establishing a calendar can indeed promote good government, but in deliberating upon calendrical matters, obtaining the correct methods is especially important. If these are not investigated precisely, the ordering of time will fail to accord with its regular patterns, and deviations in Heaven's seasons will go unrecognized; proclamations will fail to follow its changes, and discrepancies in human affairs will go unnoticed. How, then, could these methods go undiscussed?

In calendrical discussion, there is what is called the sun's course. The sun travels once around the earth each day, covering in all 365¼ degrees. After 365¼ days, it returns to conjunction with Heaven: this constitutes one year. As for the moon's course, the moon travels once around the earth each day, falling short of the sun by a total of 13 and 7/19 degrees. After 29 and 499/940 days, it comes into conjunction with the sun: this constitutes one month. The sun comes into conjunction with Heaven once each year, and from this arise the twenty-four solar terms. This is the basis of the surplus of days. The moon comes into conjunction with Heaven [?] twelve times each year, and from this arise the twelve new moons. The shortfall of days is rooted in this…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
也分一日爲十二辰又細分之爲一百刻
氣朔假此以推步而日未嘗有法也分斗
柄指十二辰又細分之爲二十四度星辰
乘之以觀候而斗未嘗有分也閏餘者氣
朔盈虛之所致故三年一閏五年再閏積
至十九年七閏而氣朔又同日也歲因之
以定而節令由之以彰乎歲差者天運日
躔之所致蓋天道平運而舒則漸差而西
日道內轉而縮則漸差而東度數積於盈
===
縮而勢不得不因之以差乎故程子有言
曰曆象之法大抵主於日月一事既正其
餘可推邵康節於日月交感之際以陰陽
求之方於差法不失而朱子以爲冠絶古
今蓋有見矣是故日者實也陽之積不得
不盈月者闕也陰之積不得不虧合盈與
虧而閏生焉蓋無閏則時不定時不定則
歲不成三年不閏則差一月而以正月爲
二月九年不閏則差三月而以春時爲夏
punctuated: 也。分一日爲十二辰，又細分之爲一百刻，氣朔假此以推步，而日未嘗有法也。分斗柄指十二辰，又細分之爲二十四度，星辰乘之以觀候，而斗未嘗有分也。閏餘者，氣朔盈虛之所致，故三年一閏，五年再閏，積至十九年七閏，而氣朔又同日也。歲因之以定，而節令由之以彰乎？歲差者，天運日躔之所致。蓋天道平運而舒，則漸差而西；日道內轉而縮，則漸差而東。度數積於盈縮，而勢不得不因之以差乎？故程子有言曰：「曆象之法，大抵主於日月，一事既正，其餘可推。」邵康節於日月交感之際，以陰陽求之，方於差法不失，而朱子以爲冠絶古今，蓋有見矣。是故日者實也，陽之積不得不盈；月者闕也，陰之積不得不虧。合盈與虧而閏生焉。蓋無閏則時不定，時不定則歲不成。三年不閏，則差一月，而以正月爲二月；九年不閏，則差三月，而以春時爲夏
translation_en:
…so it is. A day is divided into twelve double-hours, and further subdivided into one hundred quarter-hours (ke). These are used to calculate the solar terms and new moons, although the day itself has no inherent rules of division. The directions in which the Dipper’s handle points are divided among the twelve stations, and further subdivided into twenty-four degrees [?]. These are used to observe the stars and ascertain the seasons, although the Dipper itself has no such divisions. The remainder requiring intercalation results from the excess and shortfall between solar terms and new moons. Thus there is one intercalary month in three years and two in five years; after nineteen years, with seven intercalary months, the solar term and new moon once again fall on the same day. Is it not through this that the year is fixed and the seasonal divisions become manifest?

Precession results from the movement of heaven and the sun’s passage along its course. Heaven’s course proceeds evenly and extends, gradually shifting westward; the sun’s course turns inward and contracts, gradually shifting eastward. As the differences in degrees accumulate through excess and contraction, must not a corresponding displacement inevitably arise? Thus Master Cheng said: “The methods of calendrical calculation and celestial observation depend chiefly on the sun and moon. Once one matter is correctly established, the rest can be inferred.” Shao Kangjie investigated the mutual interaction of sun and moon through yin and yang, thereby avoiding error in the method of calculating displacement [?]. Master Zhu considered him unsurpassed in all antiquity and the present; surely this judgment rested on insight.

Thus the sun signifies fullness: the accumulation of yang cannot but produce excess. The moon signifies deficiency: the accumulation of yin cannot but produce shortfall. Combining excess and shortfall gives rise to intercalation. Without intercalation, the seasons cannot be fixed; without fixed seasons, the year cannot be constituted. If no month is intercalated for three years, the discrepancy amounts to one month, and the first month is treated as the second. If none is intercalated for nine years, the discrepancy amounts to three months, and spring is treated as summer…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
時寒暑失常歲事罔功矣此治曆必在於
制閏月而制閏尤先於精差法然其道非
一端之可言焉一曰得人誠得通星曆之
要如郭守敬者以盡考求之責明天人之
理如許衡氏者以盡講究之方則觀於天
文察於時變可坐而得之矣二曰立元至
朔同日謂之章同在日首謂之蔀蔀終六
旬謂之紀歲朔又復謂之元變化殊方朓
朒異分由此而正之矣馬融謂上天之體
===
不可測知天之事者唯有璣衡可恃即世
之渾天儀也誠能模倣設立則運旋轉之
體以窺七曜之行考驗非所當先乎李謙
曰上能合於數百載之前則下可垂之永
久丘濬曰以今曆與古曆相較比則其踈
密自見誠能斟酌損益則卽本定之制以
合已往之迹准古非所當求乎准古者稽
其同異使之有所取衷也考驗者辨其徵
應使之有所觀感也立元者要其終始使
punctuated: 時，寒暑失常，歲事罔功矣。此治曆必在於制閏月，而制閏尤先於精差法，然其道非一端之可言焉。一曰得人。誠得通星曆之要如郭守敬者，以盡考求之責；明天人之理如許衡氏者，以盡講究之方，則觀於天文，察於時變，可坐而得之矣。二曰立元。至朔同日謂之章，同在日首謂之蔀，蔀終六旬謂之紀，歲朔又復謂之元。變化殊方，朓朒異分，由此而正之矣。馬融謂上天之體不可測，知天之事者唯有璣衡可恃，即世之渾天儀也。誠能模倣設立，則運旋轉之體，以窺七曜之行，考驗非所當先乎？李謙曰：「上能合於數百載之前，則下可垂之永久。」丘濬曰：「以今曆與古曆相較比，則其踈密自見。」誠能斟酌損益，則卽本定之制，以合已往之迹，准古非所當求乎？准古者，稽其同異，使之有所取衷也；考驗者，辨其徵應，使之有所觀感也；立元者，要其終始，使
translation_en:
…season. Cold and heat would lose their regularity, and the year’s labors would yield no results. Thus, regulating the calendar necessarily depends on establishing intercalary months, and establishing intercalation depends above all on refining the methods for calculating discrepancies. Yet the proper approach cannot be explained through a single aspect.

The first requirement is to obtain suitable men. If one truly obtained someone like Guo Shoujing, who understood the essentials of astronomy and calendrical calculation, to fulfill the responsibility of investigation, and someone like Xu Heng, who understood the principles of Heaven and humanity, to pursue thorough inquiry, then understanding celestial patterns and discerning seasonal changes could readily be achieved.

The second requirement is to establish an epoch. When the winter solstice and new moon fall on the same day, this is called a zhang; when both also fall on the first day of the sexagenary cycle, this is called a bu; when the bu concludes a sixtyfold cycle, this is called a ji; when the year and new moon return once more to their starting points, this is called a yuan. The diverse courses of change and the differing fractions by which the moon runs ahead or falls behind can thereby be corrected.

Ma Rong held that the configuration of the heavens cannot be fathomed, and that those seeking to understand celestial affairs can rely only on the jeweled instrument and sighting tube—that is, the armillary sphere used in the world today. If one could truly construct and install an instrument on this model, setting its revolving structure in motion to observe the courses of the seven luminaries, should empirical verification not take priority?

Li Qian said: “If it accords with events several hundred years in the past, it can be handed down for all time to come.” Qiu Jun said: “Compare the present calendar with ancient calendars, and their relative imprecision and precision will become apparent.” If one could truly weigh what should be removed or added, adapting an established system to accord with the records of the past, should conformity with antiquity not be sought?

Conformity with antiquity means examining similarities and differences so that there is a basis for sound judgment. Empirical verification means distinguishing observable signs and their correspondence with predictions so that there is a basis for observation and understanding. Establishing an epoch means bringing together the end and the beginning, so that…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
之有所契合也得人者明其理數使之有
所擬議也曆之道盡於陰陽也陰陽盡於
差法也差法盡於四者之要也由是推之
於秒忽毫釐之積分其數有可驗也考之
於日月星辰之躔度其象有可觀也審之
於寒暑晝夜之往來其氣有可徵也以辨
敘事者敘此也以詔救攻者救此也孰謂
曆法有不明而治道有難成哉古有之聖
人不能違時而能以事適時適時者其功
===
大此之謂矣方今
聖人在上以天地爲本以陰陽爲端以四時爲
柄以日星爲紀七政齊而三光全五氣布
而四時行愚生咸育於
帝德廣運之中蓋已有年而於此猶惓惓焉蓋
天辰之高遠而吾能揆之也以理則日至
之微不難於前知天運之流行而吾能擦
之也有機則感召之頃可默回乎元化誠
弗恃其一定之形而不委之於適然之數
punctuated:
之有所契合也。得人者，明其理數，使之有所擬議也。曆之道盡於陰陽也，陰陽盡於差法也，差法盡於四者之要也。由是推之，於秒忽毫釐之積分，其數有可驗也；考之於日月星辰之躔度，其象有可觀也；審之於寒暑晝夜之往來，其氣有可徵也。以辨敘事者，敘此也；以詔救攻者，救此也。孰謂曆法有不明，而治道有難成哉？古有之：「聖人不能違時，而能以事適時。適時者，其功大。」此之謂矣。
方今聖人在上，以天地爲本，以陰陽爲端，以四時爲柄，以日星爲紀。七政齊而三光全，五氣布而四時行。愚生咸育於帝德廣運之中，蓋已有年，而於此猶惓惓焉。蓋天辰之高遠，而吾能揆之也，以理則日至之微，不難於前知；天運之流行，而吾能擦之也，有機則感召之頃，可默回乎元化。誠弗恃其一定之形，而不委之於適然之數，
translation_en:
…so that they may accord with one another. Obtaining the right men means elucidating the principles and numerical methods, so that these may be considered and assessed. The whole art of calendrical calculation lies in yin and yang; the workings of yin and yang lie in methods of calculating differences; and those methods lie in the essentials of the four matters just discussed. Proceeding from these, one can verify the numbers through the accumulation and subdivision of the minutest fractions; examine the celestial configurations through the positions traversed by the sun, moon, and stars; and ascertain the workings of qi through the alternation of cold and heat, day and night. When distinguishing and ordering affairs, these are what one orders; when issuing instructions for remedial action [?], these are what one remedies. Who could say that calendrical methods cannot be understood, or that the way of good government is difficult to accomplish? An ancient saying has it: “The sage cannot act against the seasons, but can adapt affairs to them. Great is the achievement of one who adapts to the seasons.” This is precisely what it means.
Now the sage occupies the throne, taking Heaven and Earth as his foundation, yin and yang as his starting point, the four seasons as his means of control, and the sun and stars as his framework. The seven celestial regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets—are in harmony, and the three luminaries—the sun, moon, and stars—are complete; the five forms of qi spread abroad, and the four seasons proceed in order. We humble students have all been nurtured within the far-reaching sway of imperial virtue for many years, yet remain deeply concerned with this matter. Though the heavenly bodies are lofty and remote, we can measure them: through principle, even the subtleties of the solstices are not difficult to know in advance. Though Heaven's movements flow onward, we can apprehend [?] them: where there is a responsive impulse, at the moment of its evocation one may silently redirect the primordial process of transformation. If one truly neither relies upon its fixed configuration nor leaves matters to merely fortuitous numerical outcomes…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
則增脩之愈勤所以凝承者有其道而已
至者可恃之於悠久矣謹畏之益加所以
消弭者有其要而未形者不至於譴告矣
奉順於上以爲治曆明時之本爕調於下以爲
敬天勤民之助則在吾
君吾相加之意焉而已矣愚生何容喙焉
第四問
孫榮仁
同考試官教諭楊　批〔條答無遺品藻曲當且詞〕
===
〔氣浩博不浮莊重有要是必有才有德之士錄之非以其〕
〔文耳〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔有考據有斷制是善尚論〕
〔古人者〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔鋪敘得體當是作手〕
古之才德原於一後之才德岐於二夫德
者本也才者末也一則本末兼該二則末
焉而離其本者多矣何也學也者學夫道
也學道而有得於心者德也才稟於氣氣
punctuated:
則增脩之愈勤，所以凝承者有其道，而已至者可恃之於悠久矣；謹畏之益加，所以消弭者有其要，而未形者不至於譴告矣。奉順於上，以爲治曆明時之本；爕調於下，以爲敬天勤民之助，則在吾君吾相加之意焉而已矣。愚生何容喙焉？

第四問
孫榮仁
同考試官教諭楊　批〔條答無遺，品藻曲當，且詞〕〔氣浩博不浮，莊重有要，是必有才有德之士，錄之非以其〕〔文耳。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔有考據，有斷制，是善尚論〕〔古人者。〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔鋪敘得體，當是作手。〕

古之才德原於一，後之才德岐於二。夫德者本也，才者末也。一則本末兼該，二則末焉而離其本者多矣。何也？學也者，學夫道也。學道而有得於心者，德也。才稟於氣，氣
translation_en:
…then, by pursuing self-cultivation still more diligently, one has the proper way to secure and sustain what has been received, and may count on the blessings already bestowed to endure. By increasing reverent caution still further, one grasps the essentials of averting calamities, and those not yet manifest will not develop into admonitions from Heaven. Reverently complying with Heaven above provides the foundation for regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons; harmonizing affairs below assists in revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people. It remains only for our ruler and our chief ministers to give these matters their attention. What place is there for an ignorant student such as myself to offer an opinion?

Fourth Policy Question
Sun Rongren
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔His answers address every point without omission, and his evaluations are apt in every particular. Moreover, his〕〔writing has breadth and vigor without being superficial; it is dignified and substantial. He must be a man of both ability and virtue. We select him not merely for his〕〔literary skill.〕
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: 〔He offers evidential support and decisive judgments: here is someone skilled at discussing〕〔the men of antiquity.〕
Examiner Qu, Instructor, comments: 〔His exposition is well ordered and appropriate; he must be an accomplished writer.〕

In antiquity, ability and virtue had a single source; in later times, ability and virtue diverged into two. Virtue is the root, and ability the branch. When they are one, root and branch are both encompassed; when they are two, many pursue the branch while departing from its root. Why is this? Learning means learning the Way. What one acquires in the heart through learning the Way is virtue. Ability is endowed through qi; qi…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
有昏明强弱之等故其發之於事功或異
焉者才爾殊也古之君子優於德而達於
才其出而任天下之事心術正大事功俊
偉故曰原於一而本末兼該後世之士任
其氣質之偏隨世以就功名故風節著矣
而於德或違事功懋矣而於德或病故曰
岐於二而離其本者多矣請因明問而陳
之粤自唐虞三代之盛皐夔稷契之爲相
伊傅周召之爲臣都俞吁咈勤勞篤棐渾
===
渾然相忘於道化之中德泯於無亦不知
有所謂才也自是以降光岳氣分士習漸
靡因資禀以爲學任血氣以從事於是德
器才識始岐而爲二有不相爲用者矣白
居易曰存諸中者謂之德發諸外者謂之
才德如大圭不割也才如利刃不缺也司
馬光曰德勝才者爲君子才勝德者爲小
人是則德器也才識也可相有而不可以
相勝者也歷考諸古人如楊椎著書張衡
punctuated:
有昏明强弱之等，故其發之於事功，或異焉者，才爾殊也。古之君子優於德而達於才，其出而任天下之事，心術正大，事功俊偉，故曰原於一而本末兼該。後世之士任其氣質之偏，隨世以就功名，故風節著矣，而於德或違；事功懋矣，而於德或病。故曰岐於二而離其本者多矣。請因明問而陳之。
粤自唐虞三代之盛，皐夔稷契之爲相，伊傅周召之爲臣，都俞吁咈，勤勞篤棐，渾渾然相忘於道化之中，德泯於無，亦不知有所謂才也。自是以降，光岳氣分，士習漸靡，因資禀以爲學，任血氣以從事，於是德器才識始岐而爲二，有不相爲用者矣。白居易曰：「存諸中者謂之德，發諸外者謂之才。德如大圭不割也，才如利刃不缺也。」司馬光曰：「德勝才者爲君子，才勝德者爲小人。」是則德器也，才識也，可相有而不可以相勝者也。歷考諸古人，如楊椎著書，張衡
translation_en:
…has varying degrees of obscurity and clarity, strength and weakness. Thus, differences in its manifestation in practical achievements are simply differences in talent. The gentlemen of antiquity were abundant in virtue and accomplished in talent. When they came forward to undertake the affairs of the realm, their intentions were upright and magnanimous, and their achievements outstanding. Hence it is said that these originated in a unity that encompassed both root and branches. Scholars of later ages gave free rein to the biases of their temperaments and followed worldly trends in pursuit of achievement and fame. Thus, even when renowned for integrity, they sometimes departed from virtue; even when their accomplishments were great, their virtue was sometimes flawed. Hence it is said that the two diverged, and many became separated from their root. Allow me to explain in response to your discerning question.
In the flourishing ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, and Xie served as chief ministers, while Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao served as ministers. Whether voicing assent or remonstrance, they labored diligently and offered devoted assistance. In complete harmony, they forgot all distinctions between themselves amid the transforming influence of the Way. Virtue left no discernible trace, and they were not even conscious of anything called talent. Thereafter, the vital forces of the heavenly luminaries and the sacred mountains became divided, and the habits of scholars gradually deteriorated. They pursued learning according to their innate endowments and acted under the sway of their passions. Thus, moral character and talent and discernment began to diverge into two, sometimes failing to serve one another. Bai Juyi said: “What is preserved within is called virtue; what manifests itself outwardly is called talent. Virtue is like a great jade tablet that does not cut; talent is like a sharp blade without a nick.” Sima Guang said: “One whose virtue exceeds his talent is a gentleman; one whose talent exceeds his virtue is a petty man.” Thus, moral character and talent and discernment may coexist, but neither should overpower the other. Examining the ancients in turn, take, for example, the writings of Yang Chui [?], and Zhang Heng …

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
邵雍稱其盡陰陽之變見天地之心可謂
度越諸子矣然著美新之論竟不免投閣
之辱韓愈爲文蘇軾氏稱其文起八代之
衰道濟天下之溺可謂一代山斗矣然勤
三上之書卒不免一飽之嘆是葢屈身於
勢利役志于功名不復知有節義之懿矣
霍光之出入禁闥小心謹畏朱熹張栻嘗
稱其功同伊尹當大事屹如山嶽大節不
可奪矣而班固作傳以爲不學無術以其
===
驕乗庇顯也趙普之匡輔三朝終始勤慎
朱熹亦嘗稱其區處天下有仁者之功偉
績不可泯矣而藝祖因事嘗嘆須用讀書
人以其改元蹈蜀也是葢闇於大義寡於
見聞不復知有經術之學矣黄霸治郡八
年安養教化治行爲第一及徵拜丞相史
論其功名損於治郡殷浩屛居十年務養
名節人期以管葛及起刺揚州史論依違
無所建白是知霸之才惟長於治民浩之
punctuated:
邵雍稱其盡陰陽之變，見天地之心，可謂度越諸子矣。然著美新之論，竟不免投閣之辱。韓愈爲文，蘇軾氏稱其文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，可謂一代山斗矣。然勤三上之書，卒不免一飽之嘆。是葢屈身於勢利，役志于功名，不復知有節義之懿矣。
霍光之出入禁闥，小心謹畏，朱熹、張栻嘗稱其功同伊尹，當大事屹如山嶽，大節不可奪矣。而班固作傳，以爲不學無術，以其驕乗庇顯也。趙普之匡輔三朝，終始勤慎，朱熹亦嘗稱其區處天下，有仁者之功，偉績不可泯矣。而藝祖因事嘗嘆須用讀書人，以其改元蹈蜀也。是葢闇於大義，寡於見聞，不復知有經術之學矣。
黄霸治郡八年，安養教化，治行爲第一。及徵拜丞相，史論其功名損於治郡。殷浩屛居十年，務養名節，人期以管葛。及起刺揚州，史論依違，無所建白。是知霸之才惟長於治民，浩之
translation_en:
…Shao Yong praised him for fully comprehending the transformations of yin and yang and discerning the heart of Heaven and Earth. He could indeed be said to have surpassed the various philosophical masters. Yet he wrote the discourse In Praise of the Xin Dynasty and ultimately could not escape the disgrace of throwing himself from a tower. Of Han Yu’s writing, Su Shi said that his prose revived literature after eight dynasties of decline, and that his Way rescued the world from drowning. He could indeed be called the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of his age. Yet he diligently submitted letters three times and ultimately could not escape lamenting his want of a full meal. This was surely to bow before power and profit and enslave one’s aspirations to achievement and fame, no longer recognizing the beauty of integrity and righteousness.
Huo Guang entered and left the palace precincts with care, caution, and reverence. Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi once praised his achievements as equal to those of Yi Yin: in great affairs he stood firm as a mountain, and his integrity in matters of consequence could not be shaken. Yet Ban Gu, in writing his biography, judged him unlearned and lacking in method, because of his indulgence of Cheng [?] and his shielding of Xian. Zhao Pu assisted three reigns, remaining diligent and circumspect throughout. Zhu Xi likewise praised his management of the realm as having the achievements of a benevolent man; his great accomplishments could not be effaced. Yet the founding emperor once sighed, in connection with a particular incident, that he must employ men who had read books, because Zhao Pu’s choice of an era name repeated one used in Shu. This was surely to be ignorant of great moral principles and deficient in learning and experience, no longer recognizing the learning grounded in the Classics.
Huang Ba governed a commandery for eight years, bringing its people peace and sustenance and instructing and transforming them; his administrative record ranked first. When he was summoned and appointed Chief Councilor, however, the historical account judged that his achievements and reputation fell short of those he had attained in governing the commandery. Yin Hao lived in retirement for ten years, striving to cultivate his reputation and integrity, and people expected him to equal Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang. Yet when he emerged to serve as Regional Inspector of Yangzhou, the historical account judged him irresolute, with no proposals to submit. From this we know that Huang Ba’s talent lay only in governing the people, while Yin Hao’s…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
操不務於實用相業非郡事之比清談無
事功之實故耳孔明之在三國也感三顧
之勤得出處之正朱熹稱其爲王者之佐
而陳壽以爲將略非其所長張浚之當南
渡也感知遇之恩盡匪躬之節朱熹稱其
有忠義之心而又議之曰才力有不逮是
知亮之仗義討賊先立其大浚之銳志恢
復奮發於誠大受固其所長小知或有所
歉故耳李固杜喬精忠勁節不避黨錮之
禍漢家之氣賴以維持乃於梁冀之逆肆
於聲討坐失大事機之權張栻蓋嘗論之
二子可謂忠則忠矣而識何其踈耶王珪
魏徵隨事納忠卒致功業之盛貞觀之治
庶幾成康乃於玄武之役不能成仁未免
事讎之恥范祖禹蓋嘗論之二子可謂才
則才矣而義何其虧耶周勃以重厚之資
誅呂以安劉乃不能對錢穀之數此其所
以終見詘於陳平矣張禹以純謹之行始
punctuated: 操不務於實用，相業非郡事之比，清談無事功之實故耳。孔明之在三國也，感三顧之勤，得出處之正，朱熹稱其爲王者之佐，而陳壽以爲將略非其所長。張浚之當南渡也，感知遇之恩，盡匪躬之節，朱熹稱其有忠義之心，而又議之曰：「才力有不逮。」是知亮之仗義討賊，先立其大；浚之銳志恢復，奮發於誠。大受固其所長，小知或有所歉故耳。李固、杜喬精忠勁節，不避黨錮之禍，漢家之氣賴以維持。乃於梁冀之逆，肆於聲討，坐失大事機之權。張栻蓋嘗論之：「二子可謂忠則忠矣，而識何其踈耶！」王珪、魏徵隨事納忠，卒致功業之盛，貞觀之治庶幾成康。乃於玄武之役，不能成仁，未免事讎之恥。范祖禹蓋嘗論之：「二子可謂才則才矣，而義何其虧耶！」周勃以重厚之資，誅呂以安劉，乃不能對錢穀之數，此其所以終見詘於陳平矣。張禹以純謹之行，始
translation_en:
…his moral cultivation was not directed toward practical use. The work of a chief councilor cannot be compared with administering a commandery, and pure conversation lacks the substance of actual accomplishment: that is all.

During the Three Kingdoms, Kongming, moved by the earnestness of the three visits, rightly chose when to leave retirement and enter service. Zhu Xi praised him as a man fit to assist a true king, yet Chen Shou considered military strategy not to be his strength. At the time of the southward transfer of the Song court, Zhang Jun, moved by the favor of being recognized and employed, devoted himself selflessly to his duty. Zhu Xi praised his loyal and righteous heart, yet also observed: “His ability and strength fell short.” Thus we know that when Liang upheld righteousness and attacked the rebels, he first established what was of greatest importance; and that Jun’s determined resolve to recover the lost territory sprang from sincerity. They were certainly strong in bearing great responsibilities, though perhaps deficient in particular kinds of knowledge.

Li Gu and Du Qiao possessed unstinting loyalty and unbending integrity. They did not shrink from the calamity of partisan proscription, and through them the vitality of the Han ruling house was sustained. Yet when faced with Liang Ji’s treason, they indulged in public denunciations and thereby forfeited the opportunity to exercise timely judgment in a momentous affair. Zhang Shi once commented on them: “These two men may indeed be called loyal, but how deficient their discernment was!”

Wang Gui and Wei Zheng loyally offered counsel as circumstances required, ultimately achieving great accomplishments. The government of the Zhenguan reign came close to that of Kings Cheng and Kang. Yet in the incident at Xuanwu Gate, they failed to fulfill benevolence through death and could not escape the shame of serving their enemy. Fan Zuyu once commented on them: “These two men may indeed be called capable, but how deficient their righteousness was!”

Zhou Bo, endowed with a steady and substantial character, destroyed the Lü clan and secured the Liu ruling house. Yet he could not answer questions about the figures for revenue in money and grain. This was why he ultimately proved inferior to Chen Ping. Zhang Yu, whose conduct was scrupulous and circumspect, from the beginning…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
終無過舉乃不識剛正之字此其所以卒
得以保身矣陽城諫諍之疏與日月而爭
光及出補外郡乃自署曰催科政拙其偏
于撫字者乎蔡邕兩漢之史與班馬而爭
衡及應董卓徵召一歲九遷何取于文章
也耶嗚呼鑾輿在前屬車在後淸道而後
行必稱德之驥始可以駕君之車及用之
戰陣施之狩獵則非駿足疾驅超軼而絕
塵者不足以多獲而取勝然則曰德器曰
===
才識亦各有取焉爾也雖然論人於三代
之上者不可不備論人於三代之下者不
可不恕於諸子中求其長而舍其短孰其
大而略其細吾於孔明有取焉觀其寧靜
致遠以爲學開誠布公以立業八陣圖而
變合之機神出師表而忠義之氣烈信王
者之佐伊呂之儔也陳壽以私怨訾之豈
足以知孔明者哉噫才德兼全尚矣君子
果能涵養本源以蓄其德精深造詣以充
punctuated:
終無過舉，乃不識剛正之字，此其所以卒得以保身矣。陽城諫諍之疏，與日月而爭光；及出補外郡，乃自署曰：「催科政拙。」其偏于撫字者乎？蔡邕兩漢之史，與班馬而爭衡；及應董卓徵召，一歲九遷，何取于文章也耶？嗚呼！鑾輿在前，屬車在後，淸道而後行，必稱德之驥，始可以駕君之車；及用之戰陣，施之狩獵，則非駿足疾驅、超軼而絕塵者，不足以多獲而取勝。然則曰德器，曰才識，亦各有取焉爾也。
雖然，論人於三代之上者，不可不備；論人於三代之下者，不可不恕。於諸子中求其長而舍其短，孰其大而略其細，吾於孔明有取焉。觀其寧靜致遠以爲學，開誠布公以立業，《八陣圖》而變合之機神，《出師表》而忠義之氣烈，信王者之佐、伊呂之儔也。陳壽以私怨訾之，豈足以知孔明者哉？噫！才德兼全，尚矣！君子果能涵養本源以蓄其德，精深造詣以充
translation_en:
…throughout, he committed no improper act, yet he did not understand the words “firmness and uprightness.” This was how he ultimately managed to preserve himself. Yang Cheng’s memorials of remonstrance rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance; yet when he was appointed to a post in an outlying prefecture, he described himself as “inept at collecting taxes.” Was he perhaps unduly inclined toward nurturing the people? Cai Yong’s history of the two Han dynasties rivaled the works of Ban Gu and Sima Qian; yet when he answered Dong Zhuo’s summons, he received nine promotions in a single year. What, then, is there to esteem in literary accomplishment? Alas! When the imperial carriage leads and the attendant carriages follow, proceeding only after the road has been cleared, only a fine horse renowned for its virtue may draw the ruler’s carriage. But for battle or hunting, only a swift horse that races ahead, outstripping others and leaving the dust behind, suffices to secure abundant game and win victory. Thus moral character and capacity, on the one hand, and talent and discernment, on the other, each have their particular uses.
Nevertheless, in judging men of the Three Dynasties and earlier, one must demand completeness; in judging men after the Three Dynasties, one must allow for their shortcomings. Among these men, if we seek their strengths and set aside their weaknesses, weigh their greater qualities [?] and pass over minor details, I find much to esteem in Kongming. Consider how he pursued learning through tranquility and far-reaching aspiration, and established his achievements through sincerity and impartiality. His Diagram of the Eight Battle Formations reveals a wondrous mastery of tactical transformation and coordination, while his Memorial on Dispatching the Army burns with loyalty and righteousness. Truly, he was a helper to a true king, a peer of Yi Yin and Lü Shang. Chen Shou disparaged him out of personal resentment; how could he be qualified to understand Kongming? Ah! To possess both talent and virtue in full is the highest attainment! If a gentleman can indeed nurture the fundamental source so as to store up virtue, and attain profound mastery so as to develop fully…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
其才出而見用於世其建立必有大可觀
者又進而爲三代之英唐虞之佐裁成輔
相之功全儒者之能事始畢矣愚生學未
能以通古今之故智未足以悉品藻之公
迂踈之見掇拾之聞敢以就正於執事不
識以爲何如
第五問
楊永貴
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔守令人知其重而不知其所由重吾子反覆言之切中肯綮用世之志可以占矣〕
===
考試官教諭鄭　批〔以前脩之卓然者取以爲勸有見之言也〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔詞可爲訓錄之以式多士〕
對欲民之安貴乎知要而要之所在莫先
任親民之官別其繁簡稽其賢否久其職
業又必隆其激勸而後任使之道得焉是
故繁簡別則才不枉用賢否稽則志得向
進職任久則事可責成激勸隆則願各攸
punctuated:
其才，出而見用於世，其建立必有大可觀者。又進而爲三代之英、唐虞之佐，裁成輔相之功全，儒者之能事始畢矣。愚生學未能以通古今之故，智未足以悉品藻之公，迂踈之見、掇拾之聞，敢以就正於執事，不識以爲何如？
第五問
楊永貴
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔守令人知其重，而不知其所由重。吾子反覆言之，切中肯綮，用世之志可以占矣。〕
考試官教諭鄭　批〔以前脩之卓然者取以爲勸，有見之言也。〕
考試官教諭曲　批〔詞可爲訓，錄之以式多士。〕
對：欲民之安，貴乎知要，而要之所在，莫先任親民之官，別其繁簡，稽其賢否，久其職業，又必隆其激勸，而後任使之道得焉。是故繁簡別，則才不枉用；賢否稽，則志得向進；職任久，則事可責成；激勸隆，則願各攸
translation_en:
…his talents. When he comes forth and is employed in the world, his accomplishments will surely be considerable and worthy of admiration. Advancing further to become an outstanding figure like those of the Three Dynasties, an adviser like those of Tang and Yu, he will fully accomplish the work of shaping and assisting the natural order; only then will the Confucian scholar’s undertaking be complete. My learning, as an ignorant student, does not yet encompass the circumstances of past and present, nor is my understanding sufficient to ensure complete impartiality in judging men. With these impractical views and gleanings of knowledge, I venture to submit myself to your correction. I wonder what you think of them.
Fifth Policy Question
Yang Yonggui
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: 〔People know that prefects and magistrates are important, but do not know what makes them important. You discuss this repeatedly, striking precisely at the heart of the matter. From this one can discern your aspiration to serve the world.〕
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔You select outstanding examples among worthy predecessors as encouragement. These are words of insight.〕
Comment by Examiner Qu, Instructor: 〔These words can serve as instruction. They are recorded here as a model for the assembled scholars.〕
Response: To bring peace to the people, what matters is knowing the essentials. Among these essentials, nothing takes precedence over appointing officials who deal directly with the people, distinguishing the complexity or simplicity of their duties, examining whether they are worthy, and keeping them long in their posts. One must also give ample encouragement; only then will the proper way of appointing and employing officials be attained. Thus, when complex and simple duties are distinguished, talent is not misapplied; when worthiness and unworthiness are examined, their aspirations can be directed toward advancement; when tenure in office is lengthy, officials can be held responsible for completing their tasks; when encouragement is ample, each person’s aspirations…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
遂要莫先於此矣要得而民可安民安而
治天下不猶運之掌哉執事發策乃以安
民之要在擇守令爲言其不忍閭田里之
愁歎而思欲以手援之者乎愚請終日言
之幸借聽焉天生烝民不能自治必有任
其責者然不能不資人以共理之凡以爲
民也故內而公卿外而司尹無非任職以
治事而守令又所以奉其令以致之於民
者也自昔重其任而不輕者蓋付之以安
===
民之寄而上之良法美意咸藉以行之否
則扞格淤壅而有所不通矣是故輕守令
是輕民也而可哉矧夫守令之所行與內
而公卿之所爲實相關焉人心有欲節制
之使歸於一民好異宜調劑之使得其平
是卽冢宰掌邦治之事也申布條敎以淑
民性安擾衆庶以歸至順是卽司徒掌邦
敎之事也秩其祭祀以和上下是卽宗伯
掌邦禮之事也脩其戎作以禁凌犯是卽
punctuated:
遂。要莫先於此矣。要得而民可安，民安而治天下，不猶運之掌哉？執事發策，乃以安民之要在擇守令爲言，其不忍閭田里之愁歎，而思欲以手援之者乎？愚請終日言之，幸借聽焉。
天生烝民，不能自治，必有任其責者；然不能不資人以共理之，凡以爲民也。故內而公卿，外而司尹，無非任職以治事，而守令又所以奉其令以致之於民者也。自昔重其任而不輕者，蓋付之以安民之寄，而上之良法美意咸藉以行之；否則扞格淤壅，而有所不通矣。是故輕守令，是輕民也，而可哉？矧夫守令之所行，與內而公卿之所爲，實相關焉。人心有欲，節制之使歸於一；民好異宜，調劑之使得其平，是卽冢宰掌邦治之事也。申布條敎，以淑民性；安擾衆庶，以歸至順，是卽司徒掌邦敎之事也。秩其祭祀，以和上下，是卽宗伯掌邦禮之事也。脩其戎作，以禁凌犯，是卽
translation_en:
…fulfilled. Nothing takes precedence over these essentials. Once they are secured, the people can be brought peace; and once the people are at peace, would governing the realm not be like turning something in the palm of one’s hand? In setting this policy question, you gentlemen have said that the essential means of bringing peace to the people lies in selecting prefects and county magistrates. Is this because you cannot bear the sorrowful sighs arising from the villages and fields [?], and wish to extend a helping hand? In my humble opinion, this deserves a whole day’s discussion; I beg you to lend me your ear.
Heaven brought forth the multitude of people, who cannot govern themselves, so there must be someone to take responsibility for them. Yet that person cannot dispense with others’ assistance in governing them jointly: all this is for the people’s sake. Thus, from the dukes and ministers at court to the administrators outside it, all hold office to conduct affairs; prefects and county magistrates, moreover, carry out their superiors’ commands and put them into effect among the people. From ancient times, their responsibilities have been regarded as weighty, never lightly esteemed, because they are entrusted with bringing peace to the people, and all the sound laws and benevolent intentions of those above depend on them for implementation. Otherwise, obstruction and blockage prevent these from getting through. Thus, to slight prefects and county magistrates is to slight the people. How could that be acceptable?
Moreover, what prefects and county magistrates do is closely connected with what the dukes and ministers at court undertake. Human hearts have desires: restraining and regulating them so that they conform to a single standard, and accommodating the people’s differing preferences and needs so that each receives equitable treatment—these are precisely the duties of the Minister of State in overseeing the realm’s administration. Promulgating rules and instructions to improve the people’s character, and pacifying and nurturing the multitude so that they attain the utmost accord—these are precisely the duties of the Minister of Education in overseeing the realm’s instruction. Ordering their sacrifices so as to bring harmony between those above and those below—these are precisely the duties of the Minister of Rites in overseeing the realm’s rituals. Attending to their military preparations so as to prevent aggression and encroachment—these are precisely…

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
司馬掌邦政之事也刑以禁暴止邪使民
日遷善遠罪者非即司寇之掌邦禁乎土
以興事勸功使民得居業阜財者非司空
之掌邦土乎是故事者民之脉也內者外
之原也公卿者守令之宗也天下者郡縣
之總也事異而脉未嘗不通也勢異而原
未嘗不合也分異而宗未嘗不統也行異
而總未嘗不該也內而提綱挈領公卿之
所涖事者以澤民也外而承流宣化守令
===
之所涖民者以報政也其實一而已矣然
公卿之涖事者雖職賛佐以治民其勢遠
遠則未免於民踈又孰若守令之躬以施
政於民者尤爲至近而最親哉黷貨而淫
刑是戕衆者也性庸而行劣是佐姦者也
執拗而乖方是僨事者也望風而顧指是
敗紀者也是皆有位之蠹爲民之殃所不
容於堯舜之世執事之所欲去者諒無以
出此矣乃如公儀子之治圃是裕民者也
punctuated:
司馬掌邦政之事也。刑以禁暴止邪，使民日遷善遠罪者，非即司寇之掌邦禁乎？土以興事勸功，使民得居業阜財者，非司空之掌邦土乎？是故事者，民之脉也；內者，外之原也；公卿者，守令之宗也；天下者，郡縣之總也。事異而脉未嘗不通也，勢異而原未嘗不合也，分異而宗未嘗不統也，行異而總未嘗不該也。內而提綱挈領，公卿之所涖事者，以澤民也；外而承流宣化，守令之所涖民者，以報政也。其實一而已矣。
然公卿之涖事者，雖職賛佐以治民，其勢遠，遠則未免於民踈。又孰若守令之躬以施政於民者，尤爲至近而最親哉？黷貨而淫刑，是戕衆者也；性庸而行劣，是佐姦者也；執拗而乖方，是僨事者也；望風而顧指，是敗紀者也。是皆有位之蠹，爲民之殃，所不容於堯舜之世。執事之所欲去者，諒無以出此矣。乃如公儀子之治圃，是裕民者也。
translation_en:
…the work of the Minister of War (Sima), who directs the realm’s military administration. To employ punishments to restrain violence and halt wrongdoing, leading the people daily toward goodness and away from crime—is this not the Minister of Justice’s (Sikou) charge over the realm’s prohibitions? To administer land so as to undertake projects and encourage productive effort, enabling the people to remain settled in their livelihoods and increase their wealth—is this not the Minister of Works’ (Sikong) charge over the realm’s lands? Thus administrative affairs are the people’s vital channels; the central administration is the source of local administration; the dukes and ministers are the guiding authority for prefects and magistrates; and the realm is the aggregate of its prefectures and counties. Though affairs differ, their vital channels are always connected; though circumstances differ, their sources always converge; though duties differ, their guiding authority always unifies them; though practices differ, the whole always encompasses them. At court, the dukes and ministers grasp the essential principles and direct affairs to benefit the people. In the localities, prefects and magistrates carry forward imperial influence and spread its transforming instruction, overseeing the people to fulfill their administrative charge. In substance, these are one and the same.
Yet although the dukes and ministers who direct affairs are charged with assisting in governing the people, their position is remote; such remoteness inevitably leaves them distant from the people. How can they compare with prefects and magistrates, who personally administer government among the people and are especially close and intimately connected to them? Those who crave wealth and impose excessive punishments injure the populace. Those whose character is mediocre and whose conduct is base abet wrongdoing. Those who are obstinate and depart from proper methods ruin affairs. Those who watch which way the wind blows and look for cues undermine discipline. All these are parasites in office and calamities for the people, such as would not have been tolerated in the age of Yao and Shun. Surely those whom you, honored examiners, wish to remove fall within these categories. By contrast, Master Gongyi’s handling of his vegetable garden exemplifies enriching the people.

title: 嘉靖二十五年河南鄉試錄
text:
公叔之種樹是任人者也不以艾大夫之
使民者使其民是弗擾者也不以羊叔之
課最者課其最是弗取者也是皆庶職之
良爲民之福誠無忝於父母之任執事之
所欲擇者諒無以易此矣夫職之所在固
無彼此之別而權之所寄容有低昂之分
漢紀獨詳守相此其微意有在矣蓋縣幾
倍於郡令幾倍於守其廉其貪其才其庸
况得枚舉而縷計哉誠得一賢守以臨於
===
其上則爲令若長有所勸沮善者自奮而
不肖者將無所容矣故訓戒丁寧唯守相
之是及矣六條問事專二千石之獨察矣
此傳所以不詳於令夫豈令之治效不逮
於郡耶觀王尊之守安定則出敎告屬縣
以明謹所職而毋以身試朱博之爲冀州
而以兩令換縣因其有才不職而改任之
薛宣亦以刺史當察墨綬之長吏夫告之
者守任之者守察之者又守也則上下相
punctuated: 公叔之種樹，是任人者也；不以艾大夫之使民者使其民，是弗擾者也；不以羊叔之課最者課其最，是弗取者也。是皆庶職之良，爲民之福，誠無忝於父母之任。執事之所欲擇者，諒無以易此矣。夫職之所在，固無彼此之別，而權之所寄，容有低昂之分。《漢紀》獨詳守相，此其微意有在矣。蓋縣幾倍於郡，令幾倍於守，其廉其貪，其才其庸，况得枚舉而縷計哉？誠得一賢守以臨於其上，則爲令若長有所勸沮，善者自奮，而不肖者將無所容矣。故訓戒丁寧，唯守相之是及矣；六條問事，專二千石之獨察矣。此傳所以不詳於令，夫豈令之治效不逮於郡耶？觀王尊之守安定，則出敎告屬縣，以明謹所職，而毋以身試；朱博之爲冀州，而以兩令換縣，因其有才不職而改任之；薛宣亦以刺史當察墨綬之長吏。夫告之者守，任之者守，察之者又守也，則上下相
translation_en:
…Gongshu’s planting of trees exemplifies entrusting responsibilities to others. Not employing the people as the Grand Master Ai did exemplifies refraining from disturbing them [?]; not assessing outstanding performance as Yang Shu did exemplifies refraining from exactions [?]. These are all worthy men among the various officials, blessings to the people, and truly do not disgrace their charge as the people’s parents. Surely those whom you wish to select can be no different from these.

Where official duties are concerned, there is fundamentally no distinction between one office and another; yet in the authority entrusted to them, there may be differences of degree. The Annals of Han treats governors and chancellors alone in detail: there is a subtle purpose behind this. Counties are several times more numerous than commanderies, and county magistrates several times more numerous than governors. How could their integrity or greed, their ability or mediocrity, possibly be enumerated individually and assessed in detail? If one truly obtains a worthy governor to preside over them, county magistrates and chiefs will have encouragements and restraints. The good will exert themselves, while the unworthy will find no place to remain. Thus earnest instructions and admonitions were addressed only to governors and chancellors; investigations under the Six Articles focused exclusively on officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank. This is why the biographies do not treat county magistrates in detail. Could it really be that their achievements in government fell short of those of commandery governors?
